text:
I've been here a few times after hearing great reviews... unfortunately, I have not been super impressed. I keep going back though trying to get a really good meal- I still have hope!

We went for brunch and the menu was fine, limited compared to the full menu, which is to be expected. I ordered the BLUE CRAB CAKES, spicy green tartar sauce, mesclun green salad. 15 which were super tasty, but extremely small. I usually take home half my meals anyways, but this wasn't even enough to fill me up! Very nice flavor though. We also had the CASHEW CRUSTED HAWAIIAN FISH, ginger butter, Texmati rice, sautéed spinach, sweet potato chips. 15. which to be honest, was just alright. I was hoping that a seafood place would have something more exciting than Mahi mahi on its menu. Both of these options were on the brunch menu, but for some reason we were told that they were not available for brunch...in the end the server brought them to us with no explanation...

Our table also had the MAINE LOBSTER ROLL, caper mayonnaise, red pepper, celery, scallion, coleslaw, handcut fries. 16, which looked good, but the person eating it didn't comment.They also ordered TRADITIONAL EGGS BENEDICT, English muffin, Canadian bacon, poached eggs, béarnaise. 9.5..which they didn't like (I thought it looked good..)

We tried both the FRESH PACIFIC NORTHWEST OYSTERS and the GULF OF MEXICO OYSTERS. I enjoyed them quite a lot. I had a cocktail, but the server had never made it before and she seemed very confused about putting it together, and was even more surprised when I told her that it was actually very good!

After we finished our meal, we were all so hungry that we each ordered a dessert (we usually do not eat desserts)..when they came, we were shocked! they were massive! We had to box them up to take home and ended up sharing only one between the 4 of us. I thought this a bit strange considering the portion sizes of the mains to be so small..the deserts were all excellent-I had some bread pudding/run concoction- amazing. 

The next time we came was for Happy Hour (Daily 4:30-6:30). We entered the restaurant and the host looked at us like we were someplace we shouldn't have been and asked what we wanted!!! um...We want to sit down and eat!!!? 

We ordered the STEAMED BLACK MUSSELS (7), as did most everyone else around us, but we were really, really surprised to see that they arrived with the cling film still on them, and the bowl really hot- this obviously came out of the microwave! The clams and muscles (we got a mix portion) were all overcooked and rubbery! What a disappointment. The oysters, which were great on our previous visit, were all shucked incorrectly! Each and every oyster had bits of shell in. We attempted to get the attention of the bar staff, but there were so busy that it was impossible. We couldn't even get bread from bar staff/or servers...in the end we had to grab a bus boy who ended up serving us. To be fair, they were really busy on this day, but I felt really let down by the quality of the food. 

I did enjoy the Happy Hour vibe- there were tons of people there...and the patio is a great place to sit. 

I will give this place one more try...I am determined to like it....I hope they impress us a bit more the next time.

The doctor was pretty decent at stitching me up. I had a fairly small scar considering the extent of my injury. He was a little on the impatient side waiting for my anesthetic to set in though. I could still feel it a bit when he sewed me up (ouch). 

On the flip side: every time I have visited a relative here I have been more and more freaked out. 2 visits have been in the past 1-2 years. The more recent visit was for a relative who had a baby in May 2009. The wait to get into maternity ward is LONG. There's only one elevator in and out of the maternity wing and you have to stop at security and they take your license from you and give you a badge, want to know who you're going to see, etc. I can understand that but the guards are not very quick about it so a queue forms rather quickly. I went up 2-3 times over the course of  2-3 days and had to wait longer and longer each time. 

The other visit as I said was in ICU, Cardiac ICU in particular. You have to come to a waiting room and call the nurses desk to get in. This area is not nearly as "crazy" on security as Maternity. I went to visit my grandfather every day for a total of about 10 days and except for the first time no one even stopped me to ask where I was going when I was on my way to the waiting room. The ICU nurses were not to my expectation. Several times a medication would run out and begin beeping alerts and the nurse would not come. I have decent knowledge of medical equipment so I understand that the difference between "warning" type beeps when the meds are getting low and "ran out" beeping. I typically had to go GET a nurse to come refill a medication or fix whatever equipment was having a problem. When he was moved from ICU to regular admission rooms, no one had ANY idea where he was. Front desk originally directed me to ICU still and then the nurse on the waiting room phone advised me he was not there. I then had to go back to another service desk to ask where he was. Later he was moved from one regular room to another and during that move I had to stop and ask two nurses before someone would look it up and tell me where he was. Nothing scarier than walking into a room where your sick grandpa was last night when you left him and finding an empty bed! In his case in regular rooms, the nurses were TERRIBLE. The whole hospital is horribly dirty really. The nurses are hit & miss. Some are sweet and caring and some obviously wish they had another job and don't mind making it obvious. Additions have been made randomly over time so the layout is a huge maze. No one is interested in helping you find the room you're looking for. If I am still living here when I have a child I will definitely be insisting on going to another hospital such as Tampa General or St. Josephs. I'd rather go to any hospital but here!

"This is the perfect example of what I imagine a middle-aged mainline business man or some other local variety of briefcase monkey thinks of as "hip".  Very nice looking interior screams of overwrought dollar signs: sleek looking but soulless and obviously the product of restauranteurs with FAR too much money to throw around.  But none the less, nice, new, clean, innocuous-looking place.  A few TV's playing local sports teams behind the relatively small and forgettable bar.  

Never have I seen so many service personnel standing around-nice to have a server to customer ratio of 1 to 2 I guess, but again, inefficiency and money-hemorrhaging abound.  Beer selection is sub-par, mostly macro and a few typical craft offerings.  I suppose cocktails are the reason people go here?  And I can't objectively comment on this as I did not partake.  

Food was a crippling disappointment- not just for the selection (which was as trite and antiquated as can be, by the way-the negative tone has nothing to do with volume of selection, as I also believe elephantine novel-sized menus are about as appealing as anal-exploratory surgery ) or the menu design, or the plateware, but the quality was utterly insulting and pathetic.  I ordered the Vegetable Platter (I believe that's what it was called) for I think $10.  What arrived was a row of hackneyed selections, 3 of which I can GUARANTEE came straight out of a #10 can from either Sysco or US Foods: roasted red peppers julienned straight from the can (I could taste the tin flavor still-not even doctored up with a basic marinade), pickled cauliflower, and some kind of (likely) Tuscan-style white bean preparation.  The other components were broccoli rape which had absolutely no seasoning, and grilled scallions/baby leeks, which again had no discernible seasoning or adornment.  All this was served with what I can only gasp in horror to say was a single slice of diner-style toasted white bread.  The whole thing tasted of refrigerator-burnt margarine or incredibly cheap butter which is stored unwrapped in a refrigerator.  Absolutely insulting to someone who has been a professional chef for over a decade; unforgivably bland and boring.  

Prices were definitely high for the above described food.  Beer was priced on par with local places, cocktails/booze I can't say.

Laughter is the only response I can justifiably give when asked about this place. "

text:
THE GOOD: -Location: Cherry Hill has traffic. Here, you can avoid route 70/38 for much of your daily errands. Jefferson Hospital is down the street; Erlton plaza & Whole Foods is 2 min away; Haddonfield rd gives you the holy trinity of Trader Joe's, Costco, & Wegman's in 5 min. You can walk to CVS/Walgreen's, post office, a lousy bagel shop, OK sushi, Vietnamese food, banks, & a good bakery. Across kings hwy gets you good (for S. Jersey) pizza @ Johnny's, dollar general, & 7-11. Plus the town library is huge and right next door. The 457 (to Haddonfield/Philly PATCO) & 455 (Cherry Hill mall) bus lines are here. -Security deposit of $500: a lot less than many places. Yes, I got mine back! -ALL utilities (minus internet/cable) are included: A huge savings & the biggest draw aside from location & views. My current complex charges about $80/mo. just for water/sewer! PSE&G also isn't cheap. Stoves are gas if you like to cook. -Concrete construction: Noise @ apartments is largely luck. Sound still enters through vents based on where your unit is. A unit I visited had an upstairs neighbor whose whole family took baths anywhere from 10pm to 1am 7 days a week . We heard it all! New "luxury apartments" are nearly all cheap wood-frame construction with zero sound or climate insulation. The concrete makes a difference for noise, fire safety, and heating/cooling. Pack command hooks to hang anything on the walls. Each unit's front door is also solid "project style" steel, felt secure when locked and bolted. -Decent parking: There will always be car break-ins, "reserved spots" someone else decides to park in, etc. Fortunately the former never happened, & the latter only occurred one time. They do charge a fee ($15 monthly during my time there) and it was 1 car per unit. There is additional parking on the street, and guest parking wasn't too bad.
-Common area: Gyms in each building were fairly well equipped. The pool is giant & open all summer. There's also a dog area by each building and some outdoor fitness stuff. For elections, the polling place is on the ground floor, very convenient. They've spent $ renovating the hallways, building lobbies and mail rooms. If only they had a rooftop deck or co-working space...
-Views: Each building is 13 stories (listed 12 with "European style" numbering for ground floor). If you get a west-facing unit high enough up, you'll probably have a view of the expanding Philly skyline. I did, and it was nice to see the morning sun reflect off the Comcast center in the AM & see PM sunsets. Beautiful way to wind down the day & something to look at if you work from home. -I never saw roaches.-Large balconies: Not in all units, so check on that. THE BAD: (oh boy here we go) -Aging, poorly functioning physical plant: There were regular water shut offs, sometimes for hours. They'd try to give some advance notice, but it happened too often. -Central A/C: Cooling is provided by chillers on the roof that are either on or off. They arbitrarily shut down in September & don't turn back on until late May. Do they look at climate change or weekly forecasts to decide when to start the system for a South Jersey summer that now starts in April? Of course not! Unfortunately, NJ and Cherry Hill only require landlords to provide heat, not AC, and they take advantage of this. Plan on portable AC units to supplement what lacks cooling-wise. At least you don't pay directly for their use. Of note: the leasing office has its own ductless/split system to ensure employee comfort. -Smoking is allowed: I once had issues with smoke coming into my apartment from a neighbor. Management was clear about their policy to NOT be smoke-free. After complaints to office & Camden county health dept, office lent me an air filter, which didn't do much. -Prepare for leaks/dripping ceilings: They'll provide a utility bucket & paint the ceiling once leak stops. Get ready, it will happen to you at some point. This also means that when a leak is below, maintenance will be knocking at your door god knows when. The leaks got so bad that the "solution" was to enter each unit and perform a "drill out" of everyone's AC vents. Yes, they took a GIANT drill bit to the wall, then divert the leaking water to your "private" balcony via PVC pipes. So the last few months, I didn't spend much time on my balcony. Ants also started entering my apartment following this "repair." They did offer pest control as a band aid atop the band aid. -Not all units have dishwashers or washer/dryer:-Breed restrictions not enforced: saw pit bulls and other large, aggressive dogs almost every day. -Trash chutes clearly designed in the 1950's: chutes woefully small takes quite an effort to fit today's bags down them. So what happens? Bags left on the floor! -Package rooms: Too small & thefty. BIG rent hikes: 1 BR cost in 2017: $1160. Now? $1900! This place really was "home" 2017-19 & served me well. "Nothing is perfect." Set expectations accordingly & enjoy!

Found out about this place through Yelp and went there for a Sunday afternoon when the wife wanted breakfast food (she often does) and I didn't (I seldom do).

The layout of the place is nice, with an atrium in what was once a big old Victorian house on the Drexel campus right near the sororities.  The place couldn't help but have a "collegiate" feeling to it, and this was evident in the rest of the clientele and a scruffy staff that also was typical of a campus eatery, but despite that we didn't feel out of place with a 10-year old in tow and at least one of us being way older than college age (that would be me).

Our server, Matt, was friendly and attentive to our all of our questions and to our son who shared his name.  They kept Ms. Native's coffee filled (she said it was quite good, to follow up on similar comments from other reviewers) and I thought it was cool that they served RC Cola and Diet Rite instead of the usual soft drink suspects.

The wife almost changed her mind about breakfast and was going to go with The Islander but Matt informed us that the market cost on the tuna was a lot higher than what was printed on the menu $16.99 instead of $13.49 (the online version says $12.99) and the wife decided on a brunch special Libra's Egg White Omelet with broccoli rabe, onions, beans, long hots and goat cheese.  It was nice of him to let us know rather than just charge us more and he was apologetic.

Our youngster ordered the cheeseburger off the kids menu.  I opted for a 1/2 sandwich and cup of soup - chicken salad and a vegetable couscous concoction, and replaced the fries with a tossed salad for a small upcharge.

The wife loved her omelet, finding it flavorful with the garlic really coming to the forefront, and the potatoes were nicely seasoned and fresh.  Our son ravaged his burger on a soft brioche bun and freshly cooked potatoes - the bun was a bit big for the burger but that happens a lot with kids menus since most places won't have several bread options. I've gone and had enjoyed their all-you-can-eat several times before graduating so it was a pretty big shock when I came back and saw that the place has literally gone to hell.

I came as a party of three. Considering the size of the place (the size of an apartment living room), at no point should it ever take 10-15 minutes to try to grab the attention of your server. It was over 30 minutes into the meal and with constant hounding that they even brought us our soup or salad. The food took the usual forever, and by the end of the meal we were wondering if all the staff but one had raptured (5/21/11). During past visits, the sushi was always large chunks of rice, but at least covered with decently sized fish slices. Today, the rice to sushi ratio was so skewed, it might as well have been rice covered with fish-paper. It's never a good thing when you can see the rice through an almost translucently thin slice of fish.

It would also have been nice to stock some paper towels in the restroom. 

It was after the meal that was unbelievable. An older waitress brought us the check, which had a 15% charge on it (and it was not the gratuity either). She insisted it was a fee for getting all-you-can-eat. Does that make sense? So they wanted us to pay for the meal, and then a fee for the RIGHT to choose that meal? When we insisted that this charge made no sense (and there had obviously been no disclosure of such prior to ordering), she started yelling (nearly screaming) at our faces. It wasn't until we called for another waitress and asked for a manager that she started screaming FINE! FINE! and told us she'd take the fee off. It was the single worst service I've ever experienced in Philadelphia.

All in all, I was wondering why the reviews to this establishment went from Meh to Crackden terrible before today. Now I know. We shan't visit again. After all, Vic's is still in business.

The beignets at Cafe Beignet are just what you were thinking of when you thought of New Orleans beignets.

They come in a little paper boat, and they're not covered with a mountain of powdered sugar (a generous portion to be sure, but not as though someone had dumped an entire cup of powdered sugar over the plate).  They came out very fresh and hot and were a tasty way to start the day.  I also ordered a cafe au lait, and maybe it is because I am regularly a strong black coffee drinker, but I thought it was only o.k.  Cream tends to cut and mellow out the flavor of coffee, so the cafe au lait tasted like I wasn't drinking much.  That being said, I ordered one to get the experience, and getting the experience is what I did.

In addition to the food, this Cafe Beignt is located in the jazz garden, so there is typically some live music.  Like I said, my hotel room was just across the street, so I heard plenty of music.  The signs say it starts at 10.00, but I can tell you from my bedside clock that most mornings it started promptly at 8.00

Some of the Yelp reviews indicate the Cafe Beignet on Royal is a better choice than the one on Bourbon street.  I'll probably head there soon, so I can compare and contrast in that review.

text:
The Carousel Bar is one of those locations you must visit when you're in the city of New Orleans. Not because Hotel Monteleone, which houses the Carousel Bar, is a sight to see or place to be - it's your standard hotel. Although during the summer, it is the hosting site for Tales of the Cocktail, a yearly convention that began in this hotel and one which celebrates the growth, evolution, and all things cocktail related within the industry. Fortunately, I had the privilege to attend  one of the days of this year's event - such a fun filled boozy time!
Back to my point, the city's cocktail history is tied to this hotel, as it is the birthplace of one of its other traditional cocktails and also a classic, the Vieux Carré. Unlike the Sazerac I enjoyed nearby at the Roosevelt Hotel, the Vieux Carré here is reasonably priced. With a better ambiance to go with it. One thing you can and SHOULD do is find yourself a seat at the bar, because as it's name implies, it is a carousel. Therefore, it slowly revolves around the bar - nothing exciting or crazy - but it's definitely an experience that should be marked off during a visit. Good luck on a busy night though, finding a seat on the bar can be a rare opportunity.

During my visit, I did as I should, ordered a proper Vieux Carré and plopped myself on the carousel. Left happy having fulfilled both those responsibilities I placed on myself.

text:
Amici's Downtown Italian Restaurant

First off, let me just say delish!! 

We were randomly walking down New York St., looking for where my phone's GPS said another restaurant was supposed to be...and ended up coming upon Amici's first. We were so hungry we decided to go for it. I'm starting to really like these types of restaurants...ones that used to be a home. They have a very different & warming feel to them when you're walking in.

The menu wasn't huge, but there was enough that no mater how picky of an eater you are, you can probably find something. And if all else fails just do what we did...go with pizza! Luckily it was really good pizza. I've had some bad experiences with pizza places in Indy. Coming from the Chicago area, and working & going to school in Chicago, I have very high standards for my pizza. So far I've only found a small handful of places that can cut it around here. Now I'll have to add Amici's to the list. The crust tasted fresh & homemade; the toppings (cheese & pepperoni) were fresh & not over done (nothing overpowered anything else); and the sauce had a little something extra in it. It took us a while to figure it out, it almost tasted like there was something fruity added to it. We finally had to ask the waitress what it was. I won't spoil the surprise for you...I'll just recommend going to try it out for yourselves. 

Overall it was a very good restaurant. I strongly suggest having wine, beer, or just water with you dinner. My only complaint comes from ordering a soda to drink, and being brought a can & a glass with ice....and paying 2.75 for it. I understand mark-up, but that was a little much...even for me. I don't drink, but apparently the Chianti was pretty good.

Check this place out.

Also got a Miso ramen, but I'd like to describe it as onion soup. The whole soup was hijacked by onions, every bite was filled with al dente white onions, there was definitely more onions than ramen noodles. I would have rather they floated a Gruyere covered crouton and called it French onion soup. My last review was a two star and on top of my above statements the reason why it dropped to a one star was because everyone in the restaurant could care less how we were doing. I truly hope this isn't what people accept as GREAT ramen. 
I have been here twice now and both times have had less than stellar meals. Live in the neighborhood so stopped by a couple times to check it out.  Some pluses and minuses overall, but overall a decent brunch option.

First time there was a Sunday prime time brunch with 4 of us, and waited about 10 minutes for a table, the place was crowded.  The second time, on a Saturday early afternoon, we were seated immediately.

Service the first brunch was excellent, the waiter was a young man who was around a lot and very attentive.  The second time service was awful, a young woman who just didn't seem to have us specifically on her radar.  We actually finished 15-20 minutes after a table of 4 that came 5 minutes after we did with the same waitress, it was very strange.  Either she was clueless or we had turned her off to us somehow.

Anyway, the food is very good for a local brunch-type place and is the biggest plus. The homemade biscuit is a must have (unfortunately they were out one of the times we went), and the entrees were pretty uniformly excellent.  Peach French Toast was ordered at both brunches and is a star, thick fluffy pieces of bread cooked perfectly with actual pieces of peach and a light peachy syrup.  The flavor combination is perfect if you like sweet brunch foods.  The open face egg and cheese and sausage sandwich was very good, the croissant it was served on was lightly toasted and very light and flaky.  My daughter got a Baked egg casserole the first brunch and it also was an excellent savory dish.  The only downsides on the food, the first brunch we all shared a cinnabon, which was a little heavy and ordinary tasting, which surprised me since they seem to bake all their own pastries there fresh. text:
My wife and I decided to try Prime 47 after hitting up most of the high-end steak spots in Indy over the last three months (St. Elmo's, Ruth's Chris downtown, Ruth's Chris at Ironworks, Tonys, and Capital Grille). The restaurant is beautiful. The space reminds me of an old school bank, one in which the manager had a large office on the second floor from where he could look down over the operations on the first. Our server was very pleasant and dressed in the typical old fashioned steakhouse short-white-coat style.

We started off with the fried shrimp and calamari. This was absolutely delicious. Because I'm not a fan of mayonnaise, we had them bring the sauces out on the side. There were two sources: a citrus aioli and a kung pao. The kung pao was ridiculously good. I had also ordered a salad, but this never came. That was actually OK because I didn't want to get too full prior to my steak.

I ordered the bone-in dry-aged ribeye priced at $87. My wife ordered the 8 ounce prime fillet. This is where the wheels came off. My steak looked beautiful when it came out and was cooked to a perfect medium-rare. Unfortunately though, the only thing I could taste when I bit into the first piece of rib cap was smoke and char. This flavor was so overwhelming that I couldn't even tell if the steak had been salted. It was the kind of flavor I would've been impressed with had it been a Kroger choice grade steak and cooked on a neighbor's outdoor grill during a pool party. For an $87 bone-in prime cut however, it was unacceptable. 

Fortunately our server could see that I was pretty upset with my steak; so he offered for me to try something else. So I ordered the Delmonico ribeye. This was actually brought out by the manager with his apologies from the kitchen. He asked me to cut into it to make sure it was cooked my liking. I felt incredibly embarrassed for him when I cut into it and it was cooked to a blue rare. You could tell he was very taken aback, saying something to the effect of: "oh they must have tried to rush it out of the kitchen." He took it back with no questions asked and stated that he would just take my steak off the bill entirely. A few  minutes later the manager brought the steak back to the table. This time it was perfectly cooked to medium-rare. Unfortunately though, it had the same flavor as the dry-aged I initially tried: overwhelmingly smoky/charred that completely drowned out the flavor of the beef. Since both the manager and our server had gone to such great lengths to try to make me happy, I did finish the steak to show my gratitude. I could just as easily have eaten a few bites and taking the rest home to re-purpose though. 

In terms of my wife's fillet, it was just OK. The taste of smoke and char was definitely not as dramatic, but the steak had very little flavor. It was also slightly undercooked: my wife ordered it medium, but it was definitely a solid medium-rare in the center. This actually worked out for me though, because I was able to try the portion of the steak that was too undercooked for her.

The only side we ordered was the truffle fries. These were delicious. Cooked to a beautiful crisp and perfectly seasoned. Our server did bring us out some broccoli, which Prime 47 is trying out is a new side offering. It was OK: probably a little too salty and just in general not a high-quality side you would expect to be served at a high-end prime steakhouse. Bringing this to our table though was another very nice gesture to make up for my disappointment with my steak. 

The final conciliatory gesture was being served a dessert cookie with ice cream and chocolate sauce, and 2 complementary glasses of the Prosecco we had been drinking. The cookie was outrageously delicious. Unfortunately, I could barely eat it by this point because I was so full. 

All in all, I would say that prime 47 is a beautiful restaurant with a very professional and dedicated staff that serves excellent sides and desserts, but seriously underwhelming steaks. I've definitely come to realize over the past few months that I prefer a broiled to a grilled steak. So I initially thought that a rating of three out of five stars might be a little harsh. However, the grilled tomahawk ribeye I recently had at St. Elmo's is still one of the best steaks I've ever eaten. So I can't completely attribute my dissatisfaction with the steaks I tried at Prime 47 to their having been grilled alone. I could also see how someone might  enjoy the almost rustic flavor of the steaks here. I just didn't. 

3/5

text:
I went to Cafe Soule with my family last Sunday, August 6 for brunch, the day after all the crazy flooding that happened the night before. I made a reservation weeks earlier through a Yelp conversation with the owner - that was easy although I had to inquire about my reservation request because they didn't respond to quickly initially. There weren't too many patrons there but we got the largest table so this place probably doesn't require a reservation unless you have a larger group. I picked this place because it takes reservations plus I figured the menu would have something for everyone in my party. 

Upon arriving, I decided that the atmosphere could've been a little more cheery. It seemed kind of dark and damp and cold - although that could be due to the flooding/general atmosphere outside. Aside from that, our waiter could've been more friendly. He seemed a bit too casual for our liking. After ordering, he wasn't very attentive (checked on us once right after we got our food) and towards the end of our meal we actually had to flag him down to give him the credit card. 

Onto the food - it was just okay. We ordered a variety of things - 3 of the benedicts (Soule, Lafitte, and Benedicte), bananas foster waffle, and the meal of the morning. First off, my sister's benedict was not even very warm, which was a disappointment but not the end of the world. We actually couldn't find the kitchen, even when we went to the bathroom, so perhaps it's on another level and the food got cold while it was being brought to the table? Second, none of the benedicts' eggs were poached, but rather soft-boiled. That was disappointing. I can even make a poached egg at home. Maybe the plates were sitting out long enough that the yolks hardened before they made it to the table? Aside from that, I wish the Lafitte had more cajun/creole flavor or just seasoning in general - the crawfish were rather bland. The meal of the day was pretty basic and my dad would've liked to see it served with some jam or butter. He wanted to flag down our waiter but didn't end up catching his eye. The waffle was the redeeming part of this meal. Though the waffle was pretty basic (and almost reminiscent of the waffles you make at chain hotels), the bananas and toppings were nice. Nothing too crazy. 

I'd maybe try going again and ordering an omelette or a breakfast cocktail, but I'm not in a hurry to come back to Cafe Soule.

I do want to come back to try the other flavors but the bar will be set very low.

text:
Really delicious dinner here after a very, very long drive. I had the Idaho trout which was cooked perfectly, so delicate and flaky. It was served with the perfect amount of rice and just a little too little asparagus. Everything tasted great, though, and the almonds added the perfect amount of crunch. With it came the option of soup or salad; I went with the caesar salad which was a sort of deconstructed interpretation of a caesar salad, but really very tasty.

I also decided to try an Idaho wine-- the Cinder Viognier was really good. Don't be afraid that Idaho isn't well-known wine country... this is a nice white that paired really well with the fish!

Our server was also very friendly and helpful, suggesting which wines we should have with our meals and very kindly swapping out the clam chowder I had mistakenly ordered not knowing it had bacon in it. There is also some fun people-watching to be done, with the path running next to the patio. I could see the interior of the Cottonwood Grille being really great for an event, like a rehearsal dinner or even a wedding... For us, the patio made for a really enjoyable and relaxing introduction to Boise!

text:
I really wanted to like NOLA. In fact, I really did like NOLA right up until the end of the night when my table was unceremoniously kicked out because we'd reached the 3 hour seating limit.

The food at NOLA was really good. The country fried chicken was amazing. The various seafood appetizers that we had were great, and their drink selection is pretty good. But there were problems. They were out of a lot of menu items which, considering we arrived at 6:30pm, seemed a bit strange. They were out of at least 4 items very early in the night and ran out of more items as the night went on.

On the night we were there they had no wings, no nachos, no sweet potato fries, no etouffee, and they ran out of coconut shrimp part-way through the evening. Things weren't off to a promising start, but we ordered from the items that they hadn't run out of them and thoroughly enjoyed them.

Because NOLA is also a live music venue, we had planned to stay around after our meal and continue to order drinks. This was fine until our server came up and told us that she had been informed that we had to leave in 15 minutes because another party had reserved our table. She had delivered new drinks to us just moments earlier, so this was unwelcome news. The first band hadn't even finished!

After some discussions with a very unhelpful manager -- apparently the waitress had to fight with him to get him to even apologize -- we learned that they have a policy of limiting parties to 3 hours at a table. If they weren't a live music venue, this would be understandable. But because they are a music venue, it seems odd to have a time limit that would make more sense at a traditional restaurant. Still, we wouldn't have minded if they'd informed us of this at the start of the evening (or, better yet, when we made our reservation).

The manager did tell us that he would try to find space for us toward the back of the room, but he never returned to our table. After we cleared up our bill and left -- now in a very bad mood -- we noticed that there were many empty tables. Surely, both our party and the party with the 9:15 reservation could have been accommodated.

It's a shame, because up until the moment that we were so rudely ejected from the restaurant, we were all really enjoying the scene and thinking that we would likely be regular customers. Instead of gaining 5 new regulars, NOLA lost 5 customers and gained a negative Yelp review.

text:
Not as bad as we feared it could be.  Not as good as we hoped it might be.  Still, not even very friendly server and guacamole maker could balance out the deficits.  And this we say to Happy Hour goers; beware of their "two for one" policy for libations.  

It is partly that policy, which we laughed about at first "surprise" but then thought not so funny, partly garish decor and partly dated menu at high prices that leaves us feeling lukewarm.  We wouldn't refuse to come back here if someone suggested it.  Neither would we suggest this as destination.

VIBE
"We would have thought this cool when we lived in the East Bay in the 1980's.", my husband said as we settled in at one of the step up booth tables in the dimly lit bar.  "Yes",  I said.  "But that Medusa meets Lochness Monster sculpture evokes the bar from the first Star Wars movie."

Not that that is a bad thing.  But it is this thing.  If this was 30 years ago, we would have "dug it".  Different strokes in different times.  It seems laughably garish today.

HAPPY HOUR UNHAPPY SURPRISE
We arrived about ten minutes to six.  Our plan was to have a cocktail, peruse the dinner menu and decide if we wanted to stay for dinner.  Yeeps whose opinions  I respect had given this just 2 or 3 star ratings so we figured we'd approach with caution.

Our friendly server told us there was a Happy Hour deal that ended at six o'clock.  Two cocktails or glasses of wine for the price of one, she said.  Any wine or cocktail priced $15 or less qualified and both beverages had to be the same kind, she said.  

Sounded like a pretty good deal to us.

The server handed us an IPad to review  specialty cocktail menu and wine lists.  She said she would come back to take our order as the IPad was not for ordering just for reading the menu.  Seemed redundant to us since cocktail menus and wine list were on the table.   

This is indicative of the "flash without function" that seems hallmark for the space.  "Oooh, Myrtle, look at this!  An Ipad." 

More goofiness masquerading as coolness that makes this place laughable. 

We settled on top shelf Margaritas.  The drinks arrived in a tall glass with lots of ice and mixer and a straw.  Not the worst we've ever had.  Not the best.  Still, at $10 each on the menu and in the "two for one" Happy Hour mode, we were feeling good about the bargain price of $5 a drink.  

But to our unhappy surprise, after nearly an hour had passed and we were nearing the bottom of our libations and getting ready to depart  our server arrived with two more drinks.  

Speechless for a moment (not often a state for me) I asked "Umm?  We didn't order these".  

Our nice server said THIS was the "two for one" at Happy Hour.  You order one and you get a second one free after you drink the first one. 

Our first response was to laugh at being "had".  But being long past wanting to or being able to have two cocktails and navigate, this was lost on me as "value".  It seems a pretty sophomoric policy of the bar to over serve two drinks to folks who only want one.  Just sayin'.  

Our server said we weren't the first customers to feel "had" by the policy.  Seems to me ownership is shady to promote like this.  But it fit things being kind of "off" here all around.

EATS
Looking over the big, two sided, laminated dinner menu we decided we'd pass (hot rock cooked steak, bbq chicken pasta...dated), order the table-side guacamole in the bar with our drink and move on.

The schtick of table-side guac seems a relic of 2000's.  Like flaming cherries jubilee table-side was for  the 1970's.  But Barbacoa sells a lot of guacamole this way.  As many as three guys with guac carts work on busy nights making up to 40 orders each we learned.  Shtick sells. (PS - There is a tip jar on the cart to tip the maker.)  Whether made table-side or in the kitchen doesn't matter as long as the guacamole is good.  And this, made and served in a molecajete, was good.  

THIS N THAT:

1) PARKING:  Private lot and it was pretty full.  Goes to show, I guess, we are in the minority opinion about Barbacoa's mediocrity.

2) ACCESSIBILITY:  Troublesome.  My Yelp friends who use wheelchairs will understand how dangerous it is to have wheelchair users have to travel behind parked cars against traffic in a parking lot  because the building owners violate the 24 year old Federal Civil Rights law and Idaho Code to put curb cuts at ADA parking locations  Also only one table at standard height in bar.  All other seating requires step up.  Dining room is step down on one side but ramp in on another.

3) NEIGHBORS:  Boise Park owned lake and walking path right behind Barbacoa.  Fast food restaurant to front.

Woof...man...I wanted to write a review saying I experienced the best Cheesesteak in the world...

You won't find me writing that here.

So...as a Chicago-native visiting the city of Brotherly Love, naturally I wanted to set out to find the Best Philly Cheesesteak. During our exploration of the city, we asked every local where we should go. It appeared 3 places were mentioned the most:

1) Geno's
2) Jim's
3) Pats

While sipping a local pint, one local sold us on Geno's...he wouldn't let up on it. Even when our conversation was over...he would re-introduce himself to confirm Geno's is the place. Alright pal...we're in.

Dude must have been drunk. We show up to Geno's, put our order in. Steak, provolone, onions, peppers.

Now...I was unaware there's 2 ways to serve a Philly...chopped, or sliced. Geno's serves up sliced meat.

When we open sandwich...what do we see? Think strips of this pallid grey meat...grilled pepper and onions haphazardly thrown on the top of the sandwich...and barely any recognizable cheese. Whatever...flavor is what matters, right?

The best I could describe it is...meh...
The bread was good. The meat...tasted like it wasn't seasoned...and had a bit of a tough bite to it. The peppers and onions...no seasoning as well, so it made an already bland sandwich...more bland. OH! And the cheese...if you had me take a blind bite of this sandwich and ask me to describe what was on it...cheese wouldn't be on the list...because you couldn't taste it. 

Overall...it was an experience...but if I was asked by someone which cheesesteak purveyor to try...I'd probably advise someone that their luck may be better at a different establishment.

Then there's the Lusiani (Bluecoat gin, blueberry, lavender, tonic), for Mario Lusiani, a gold medalist cyclist in the 1928 Olympic Games. And how could I leave out the Da Ros,  which shares the namesake of Gianni Da Ros, who in 1999 was handed a record 20-year ban from the National Anti-doping Tribunal for trafficking doping substances. The ingredients in his drink are rosé sangria, strawberry, basil, and erythropoietin, a human growth hormone. Yum! (Just kidding about that last ingredient, of course - don't want to be sued).
 
If you have the opportunity, try to snag a table out on the patio. At this particular junction, the traffic on Kelly Drive isn't bad, and just beyond lies a great view of the Schuylkill River. You will be situated in the shadow of a large, nearby heavily-trafficked bridge, but the noise is surprisingly negligible. Kind of impedes the view of the sky, though.

I can't say much bad about this place. Service is attentive and friendly. 

Note: this is NOT a late night joint. Closes at 11:00 even on Friday and Saturday night. Kitchen most likely closes a lot earlier than that.

A restaurant that is good for nearly any occasion, whether it be a casual lunch/brunch, business lunch, or date night, In Riva has the ambiance, menu, and service to cater to all circumstances.

text:
There are so many wonderful hotels in New Orleans. Choose literally anywhere other than this place. The definition of "scam" is "a dishonest scheme," and that aptly describes this hotel. The only nice areas are the lobby bar, restaurant, and rooftop deck. Once you get past these areas and into the rooms, everything is cheap linoleum, smells like mildew, is filthy, the staff treats you with incredible disrespect.... it's impressively bad given how nice the public areas are. That is why 'scam' fits this place: a fake façade hiding the truth. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Check-in process: My wedding party (10 groomsmen, groom, bride, and 10 bridesmaids) stayed here the weekend of my wedding, occupying 20+ room nights, including the 9th-floor suite. I mention this because we were by far the largest group in the hotel that weekend. Check-in was Friday at 3pm, and check-out was Sunday at 11am. We called the week of the wedding to see if early check-in was available. They said they couldn't guarantee it, but that we had a suite and a huge room block, so our odds were good. When we showed up around noon (ambitious I know), no rooms were available. Keep in mind, bride and groom have different rooms the night before the wedding. The bride was going to take the suite both nights, and I was going to join her from my standard room into the suite the second night. Around 2pm we came back to try and check in again, and neither room was available. We were told, "A VIP was in the suite. He just checked out, and they're cleaning it." We waited in the lobby bar. At 3pm (their guaranteed check-in time), we went back to the check-in counter, and it was still not ready. At that point we really needed a room. The bride had to get ready, and news flash: it takes brides a very long time to get ready. At 3:45pm, an hour before we had to leave for dinner, neither of our rooms were still ready. At this point, I demanded a room, any room, because my wife-to-be absolutely needed to start getting ready. One of my groomsmen volunteered his room to my wife-to-be, and I got ready in a different groomsmen's room. We finally got the word that our rooms were ready on our way out of the door to dinner at 4:45pm, meaning we had to check in and move our bags at 11pm when we returned. No staff offered to help move our bags.

Since our room wasn't ready on time, my wife-to-be's clothes couldn't hang and un-wrinkle. After calling for a steamer 3 times over the course of an hour, I had to go down to the front desk and physically walk with them to get the steamer to ensure they brought it to my fiancée.

The smell: Room 718, I'll never forget it. The room my fiancée used to get ready smelled strongly like mildew. You couldn't avoid it. I brought it to the hotel staff's attention. Someone came up, acknowledged the smell, and said it was because no one had been staying there for a couple of days, which meant the A/C was off. She assured us that once the A/C was given a chance to run, the smell would go away. Spoiler alert: it didn't. They were also totally sold out of rooms, so that was our nasty-smelling room all weekend.

Cleanliness / Cleaning staff: I'll start addressing the cleanliness by saying my wife's feet literally turned dark black while she was wearing her wedding dress because she was walking around the suite in bare feet. That shouldn't happen. They made some bad attempts at making the bed and they did replace the towels, but they didn't wash any dishes, take out the trash, or clean the toilets / bathrooms. On the wedding day we asked them to come back to the suite to clean the mess they had left, and they told us the staff had left for the day (at 2pm??). Meanwhile, in my non-suite room, I asked them to come first thing in the morning to clean my room since people would be coming in and out all day (I was the groom after all). I asked them the night before, that morning both when I woke up, and on the way to breakfast (3x total) to ensure they didn't mess it up after the check-in debacle. They came to make the bed last minute, and didn't even replace my towels. Then they refused to come back. Lovely folks... I've stayed in Motel 6s with better housekeeping services and cleaner rooms

Lastly, and this is undoubtedly their worst offense: the "press pass." My wife and I chose this hotel to take pictures in the lobby. Credit where credit is due, the lobby bar/restaurant is well designed. As we began taking photos, the restaurant manager storms out and stands between us and the camera. To reiterate, a hotel employee chased a bride and groom down the street so that the hotel didn't appear in the background of any of their pictures. outrageous.

So many nice hotels in New Orleans. Stay in any one of them except this one.

Update: The hotel refunded me for part of my stay to make up for their mistakes. While it's too little too late, especially for an entire wedding party's worth of business, it was a nice gesture.

The gentleman's excuse is that they are open 24 hours a day and that brings added value, well not that much value. As far as the gym itself, it has quite a bit of equipment, but for a Gold's Gym, it's missing a lot of equipment. They only have one cable station, they don't have any stair master's,  and their are many different pieces of equipment they don't have that add the ability to switch up your workout. text:
One star for the waiter being friendly, .5 star for the dressing, and .5 star for the sauce. 
My girlfriend got a chicken dish which came with a salad, I got seafood linguini, and we split toasted ravioli and bread basket. I'm only going to review the items I tasted and the overall experience. 

-No music playing. It took me a minute to figure out why it felt so awkward in there. Then I realized I could hear everyone else's conversations clear as day because there was no background music. It was weird, like going on a date to the library. 
-One of my forks basically had a meal dried onto the handle. I mean, the hunk of old food on it was enormous. I've honestly never seen a utensil quite THAT disgusting. There's no excuse for that. A little spot occasionally, I understand that. Sometimes they're easy to miss. Not this one. It was nasty. 
-The bread was just basic. It wasn't Italian bread. It wasn't warm. It was just a bore. Plus, the napkin the bread was wrapped in had old sauce all over it. Not a stain (that would've been fine), but old sauce. 
-Overall, just had that gross feeling like I was in a dirty grimy place. 
-Bus boy type kid was friendly but started closing down the empty tables while a bunch of diners were still in there. Not only that, but he was closing down our tables too...while we were eating!  He literally came up to us and others and asked us to hand him the oil, parmigiana, and little candle off the tables. It made me feel really rushed and the place was supposed to be open for another hour and a half. 
-Wine selection was ok. Basically only one or two of each type, so not much to choose from. Even fewer by the glass choices. I'm a wine drinker, so I like to have plenty of choices of reds by the glass.  That's just me though, for mediocre restaurant, it was fine. 
-Toasted ravioli weren't very hot and weren't great. I've had better since I've lived here. I've honestly had better ones from the grocery store freezer. Sauce was ok though. 
-I did like the salad dressing. It was a pretty sweet dressing, but I liked it. 
-Seafood linguini.... The sauce wasn't bad - Lobster & Crab cream sauce. Lots of lobster and crab meat pieces in it. A ton of sea food flavor, which I really enjoy. It was a little oily though. Overall, good. 
The shrimp were good sized, but would be ten times better if they were grilled. Scallops were....tiny and kind of wet. Again, should've been pan seared to get a nice golden brown on the top and bottom. I understand this is the Midwest and seafood isn't as fresh here, but if it were cooked properly, it could still be good. 
My pasta was short. Like two inch long strands. I couldn't spin it onto my fork because it wasn't long enough to wrap around. Also, , my pasta was...brace yourselves...OVER COOKED like a son of a bitch. I mean, it was like mush. No, I repeat, NO mom and pop Italian restaurant should EVER over cook pasta unless a patron asks for over cooked pasta. Funny thing is, even with the other disappointments, I would've thought about going back, but once I ate the mushy pasta it was over. You just don't serve a girl from New York State who has a Sicilian mother and "off the boat" Sicilian grandparents over cooked pasta. You just don't.

text:
I've been to a number of the Marathon Grills in the city, and would say I usually have an average of a 2 1/2 star experience.  Sometimes everything goes swimmingly with the service and the food is great, and sometimes the orders get mixed up and they're out of everything.  Yesterday I went to the 10th street location, which is definitely the nicest atmosphere.  It's 2 stories (also has outdoor seating) and is light and airy.  

We went around noon, and they were already out of both of the soups of the day, which confused me.  The blender was also broken, which was a bummer since I was craving a smoothie.  Though that started off the meal on a bad foot, the experience definitely improved.  I got the blueberry lemonade, which was really refreshing.  One of my dining companions thought it was too sweet, but I thought it was fine.  I ordered a veggie burger with Vermont cheddar, which was delicious.  The patty was hearty and tasty, and the fixings were fresh.  The fries were also good, though a bit oily.  

I've been to brunch at Marathon a couple times, and the apple cinnamon pancakes are the best, but a good example of Marathon's inconsistency.  If they get it right, they're delicious, but last time I ordered them they left out the apple cinnamon part, and we had to have them remade.  

4 stars for food, 2 stars for consistency.

text:
I brought my family here for the prix-fixe menu during Northside Nights.  It was our 21st wedding anniversary, and we wanted to try Ocean Prime.

Unfortunately, Indianapolis has plenty of fine dining options, but not enough competent fine dining servers.  The effort was there, but not the execution.  Our server was very friendly, but he was disorganized and awkward/uncomfortable dealing with customers.  He charged the wrong check to my card (which I noticed and called to his attention) and then upon canceling that charge and bringing the new receipt, he forgot to bring my card back.  The host/maitre d' visited the table twice to check on us, but his manner was cloying and seemed insincere.  Just be friendly and be yourself, then move on please.

The atmosphere is nice, though the tables are quite close together--Manhattan style.

The food was fine. My daughter loved her steak.  My scallops were perfectly seared, but I would have liked them to arrive hotter and on a hot plate.  The risotto was too thick, but it tasted good.  My house salad was supposed to contain apples, but it had none--it looked as though the salads were being tossed and dispensed en masse.  I would hope that this salad is properly plated and definitely more complete when it is not part of the prix-fixe menu.  The highly touted carrot cake was just okay (it pales compared to my mom's!).

I can't often afford to pay retail at a place like Ocean Prime, so I won't be back unless it is a business dinner.  Better fine dining options in Indianapolis include Oceanaire, Palomino, Harry and Izzy's, St. Elmo's, Ruth's Chris, and even Morton's.  These other restaurants have experienced and capable waitstaffs, which is an absolute must when paying this much for a dinner.

When planning an anniversary trip I tend to try to make reservations at the best restaurants to surprise my wife. I do research for several hours, read the reviews, look over the menu, and contact locals (or people who vacation there) to pick and choose the best places. We arrived late into town and decided to call and cancel our reservation. It is a Friday night and there is no way we would be able to get a later reservation... Right? food was great

They came without notice, at every hour of the day, worked terribly slowly, and left the old pipes that they had removed all over.  when i reminded the real estate company that they had assured me that all of this work was going to be done before moving in, they shrugged. Two weeks after my first visit to Casino Del Sol, I came back with my family for my grandpa's birthday. The family that gambles together stays together. Don't judge us.

Our time at the casino was great! The blackjack dealers were all really friendly, the cocktail waitress was just as nice and made rounds frequently. She even brought me a bottle of water with each drink. 

Unfortunately, when we went to leave everything went downhill. My boyfriend and I decided before the night to take a cab home and had hitched a ride to the casino with family who were spending the night at the hotel. 

At around 2 a.m., we asked a security guard where the cabs were. She said she would call for one and it would be about 15 minutes. She said we had to wait outside otherwise we might lose our cab. We also called Discount Cab just to be safe. Discount couldn't give us an estimated time frame, but we figured the hotel had taken care of things.

40 minutes later, my we followed up with a different security guard . He had no update but said he saw a guy wait for over 90 minutes the other night. Great. Obviously the hotel knows they have a problem with cabs and have done nothing about it.

At around 3:00 a.m., we spoke to another security guard who was of no help. At 3:30 a.m., a VIP Taxi pulled up. My boyfriend and I tried to get in, but the driver informed us he was there to pick up an employee.

We then spoke with the security guard as to how we were unable to get a cab after 2 hours, but an employee could get one in 10 minutes. The security guard was rude and told us we should get over it.

Finally, around 4:10 a.m., the Discount cab that WE called arrived to picked us up.

The hotel's response also left something to be desired. I sent the casino a message on their website the following day detailing the incident and got no response. A week and a half later, I found an email to the customer service group and re-sent my response. 4 days later I got a response from customer service saying they were investigating the matter and would get back to me when they had finished the investigation.

I emailed them back today, 10 days after they said they were investigating. They responded that they did investigate, the Security Department took appropriate action, and they are looking into cab options. I'm glad they finally got around to looking into things, but it stinks that I had to be the one to follow-up. text:
Having read all of the wonderful reviews, I was excited about going to Arnaud's this past weekend to celebrate a friend's birthday.  Unfortunately, the food was terrible and not worth the expensive price tag:
-The endive salad sounded wonderful, but it was essentially a messy plate of bland coleslaw.  The "dressing" had absolutely no flavor (definitely not the lemon vinagairette described), the endives were shredded into uneven pieces, and the blue cheese was crumbled into insanely large chunks.  (My friends got the caesar, which was standard.)
-The oysters were terrible!  Per the waiter's recommendation (and yelp reviews), I ordered the Oyster's Bienville.  They were super heavy and overcooked.  The oysters themselves were shriveled and chewy, and were covered with greasy stuffing (probably twice as much stuffing as oyster), which were then covered with a piece of melted cheese.  Melted cheese with oysters?  Umm... really?  The description itself said that the oysters were served with mushrooms, onions, and seasonings, and then topped with a white wine sauce.  Stovetop stuffing and cheese were NOT on the description.
-The chicken dish was okay... nothing spectacular.
-The gumbo was watery and bland.
-The vegetables (green beans and asparagus) were cold and covered congealed mystery sauce.    
The restaurant's only high point was the dessert.  (We got bread pudding, bananas foster, and the chocolate cake.)

All in all, this was way overpriced and not at all as fabulous as others seem to think.  As someone with family roots in New Orleans who grew up with Creole food, this is NOT where you will find quality local food.  The ambiance and history are great, but that's essentially what you're paying for.

Typically, it's not an earthquake-earthquake that gets me interested in a cuisine. Two years ago, Cheng Du, capital of Sichuan Province in China, suffered a massive earthquake, and NPR reported live on site. Then, what typically gets me to a place like Szechwan Garden is earthquake-rocking recommendation from a fellow food adventurer (and shout out to Dented Ladle Dining's Jon & Ashley for this recommendation). 

Anyyywayyyyys... this lived right up to the hype and if this place were an alley that I could live, or say if they rented out their banquet hall to create a tent town, I'd invest in it and stay there a lot. Why? The food, that's why. 

I had never had true Chinese before, but from all the studying, all the background work I've done on it, and read about it, and oggled over, this was the place to be. I really wanted a whole fish cooked in any way they felt was best and served as a whole fish. And when I got here I saw an aquarium with fishes swimming in it, but there were only 3, which means, I think, that a lot of people order this dish, too. I mean, why would they have a very sterile looking aquarium with fish (that, yes, looked exactly like the fish on the eventual plate). What did I begin with? The eye of course. The dinner was a part of the Chew On This / Yelp Indy Supper Club and we had 20 at the table. I think some were a bit frustrated with the service, but having 20 all at once is really hard for a kitchen (that's also open to the public). I thought they did a great job with the situation. 

Our waitress "Julia" was fantastic. Funny. Emotive. Interesting. Open. And, her service of ice in a to-go tray has me now wanting to serve it that way at home from now on. Also, their presentation of the rice in a wooden basket was fantastic. 

The menu is so vast I want to try everything there. I'm hoping for a return visit soon with just a handful of friends to sit at the lazy susan table so we can share in this truly authentic venue. 

Cheng Du, a place I'd love to visit. For now, fully transported.

I thought the marinara for my daughter's linguine was excellent. My gulf fish capri, made tonight with blackened drum, was the best of the bunch. Dessert: We all had the bananas foster and polished it off despite being stuffed. 

The staff was wonderful, attentive and so friendly. My next time in New Orleans I will make it a point to come again.

text:
I stumbled across CRAVE Ice Cream Social during yesterday's excursion to the land of "I Have more money than I know what to do with!," or Geist, as most people call it. CRAVE is a relatively new shop having opened on 10/28/16, which doesn't seem like the ideal time to open up an ice cream shop almost directly alongside a large body of water. 

But hey, I suppose that gives them a few months to really get things together in anticipation of the summer lovin' that this place is bound to experience. 

I tend to like it when local businesses support other local businesses. This is the case with CRAVE, which sources their ice cream from a small batch shop in Anderson, sources their coffees/teas from nearby Noble Coffee & Tea Company and sources their pastries from Rosie's in Noblesville. The shop is located in a small strip area that houses Puccini's, a local bar and grill, some small/customized offices and a couple other businesses. It's right next to Geist Marina on the west side of the Fall Creek bridge. It's an inviting little place, a warm interior matched by an employee who was inviting, hospitable and was rushing to the door when she saw my plans to enter in a wheelchair. As you enter, a few tables are to the left and the ordering counter is straight ahead with 24 flavors of premium ice cream ready for tasting. They will let you sample their flavors. I ended up going with an old favorite - cookies n' cream. Pricing starts at what they called a kid's size at $3.25 - my guess is this size would suffice for many. When I initially said "a scoop," she reached for the kid's size - I upgraded it to the small for $4.50 plus tax. I'm guessing it was the equivalent of a two scoop serving. The ice cream was super creamy, perhaps a bit lighter on the "cookies" part than I would have liked but I also noticed that the ingredients are much finer than one might usually expect. That said, it was VERY good and definitely didn't have the processed feeling one gets from the larger shops.The coloring, while a tad different than some ice cream shops, is actually indicative of a more naturally made ice cream. 

While not everyone likes ice cream during the winter, I tend to think it's important to support shops like this one during their "off season" and I make an effort to visit. You can kinda sorta see Geist Reservoir from their shop and the entire area is pretty beautiful. I was genuinely impressed with the friendly customer service. Once I'd ordered the ice cream, she made an effort to move a chair from a table so I could sit there and enjoy it. They have one television that's on, but the environment is simply very relaxed with a few tables indoors and a couple spots outside available during the warmer months. text:
Made it to the Caribbean Room for opening night!  We loved the food.  There were a couple hiccups with the service.  Easily overlookable IMHO.  Here's the breakdown.

Food was delicious.  The menu had a balance between potential staples and seasonal hits.  We tried as many dishes as we could handle.  For starters, we ordered the shrimp renick (Shari V) and foie gras (me).  Total hits.  I don't know anything about the old Caribbean Room, but the shrimp renick is a throwback.  Healthy portion of jumbo lump crabmeat and shrimp mixed with a rich, creamy sauce.  It was baked and then bacon added on top.  Killer app.  Foie gras was a beaut.  Served with brioche for sure-oche.  

Our seasonal orders were a creole tomato salad and the squash blossoms.  Excellent execution on these dishes.  The salad was a summer blend of tomatoes on tomatoes on tomatoes.  Hard for me to explain the squash blossoms.  Very colorful dish.  More importantly, they were awesome.  

For entrees, Shari V had the red snapper and I had the rabbit and dumplings.  Mine was served with mushrooms, asparagus and served in a thin, savory broth.  I wasn't thrilled about the broth, because I thought it would make the dumplings soggy. Not an issue.  I loved my entree.  Shari V thought her snapper was a beautiful piece of fish, but a little overcooked.  She still ranked it highly.  I had a few bites and thought it was solid.  Some jumbo lumb crabmeat was served on top.  Never a bad idea.  Jumbo lump crabmeat is like the bacon of the sea.

Our waiter was Gianno or maybe Giovanni.  Not sure.  He was nice.  Prompt.  I mean he did not miss a single two-bite check in.  Very attentive and knowledgeable.  We pumped him for some background on the restaurant.  Without hesitation, he dropped some knowledge on us. He was friendly and polished.  Seemed like a seasoned waiter.  So the food was incredible and our waiter was solid, but there were some minor hiccups with the service.  One of the waiters dropped our dishes off, but really didn't give us any explanation about the dishes.  We had to prompt one server to tell us about our desert, the "Mile High Pie".  He didn't know the different ice creams in the dish.  No big deal.  Just little stuff.  

Ambiance - not great.  The chairs looked like lawn furniture.  Jackets were required for dinner.  That's fine, but the decor felt more casual than the patrons.  This disconnect was a bit awkward. 

In short, we loved the food.  5 stars.  I thought Caribbean Room did an excellent job of showing off New Orleans fare without overdoing the seasoning or sauces.  CR would be a great spot to show off New Orleans to out of towners or just to grab a nice dinner.  I anticipate the service will improve.  As for the ambiance, who knows.  Not my favorite.  But when the food is so good, who cares.

text:
Come for the side dishes and take them to your favorite good BBQ joint.

Many times you find a BBQ joint that has amazing BBQ and poorly executed sides that are almost an after thought.  All I can say is that Salt + Smoke should quit making BBQ and just make their business supplying side dishes to the many better BBQ places in the St. Louis area.

It started off pleasantly with a crowded house and expecting a wait, but the front of house staff was nice enough to push two tables together to sit my wife and sons and I almost immediately on a dinner night out to celebrate their end of school year.  We ordered a fairly simple selection of two burnt end brisket sandwiches, one double cheese burger with bacon, and a fish sandwich along with an appetizer of their fried brisket ravioli. 

The first clue that the night wasnt going to go well was when I asked my son how he wanted his burger and the waiter said that they only cook burgers one way and thats medium well.  Not sure how you can run a BBQ joint and not offer burgers cooked to order temp wise.  The rest of the order was straight forward with nothing customized or altered from their menu.  The wife ordered a Moscow Mule for a drink and I ordered a simple scotch.  

We ended up waiting a fairly good amount of time for the appetizer to come out.  The filing was dry and lacked any sauce and the dough was too thick which lead to a taste that was doughy more than anything else.  No flavor of the brisket came through, and the parsley sprinkled on top was tossed with what we originally thought was parmesan cheese but turned out to be what tasted like finely diced raw garlic.  

Before we each finished one ravioli the rest of the meal was served, which makes me wonder if the food was left at the counter sitting before it came to us as the difference in time between getting the appetizer and then the main dishes was vastly different.  The brisket on my order was cold lacking any cooking temperature what so ever, and my sons burger was well beyond medium well and the cheese on it was cool and hardening.  The wife said her fish was good but nothing special.

The only real good thing across all four dinner plates was the side dishes.  The slaw that the wife and I had was very tasty and had full thin slices of apple that really help the overall flavor.  The boys had white cheddar mac and cheese that was cooked nicely and had a wonderful flavor that when accented with a dash of pepper was even better.  

Since its not really a bar I wont spend much time on this one, but any place that serves a Moscow Mule in a plain glass should have their liquor license revoked.  Enough said there.

Salt + Smoke produced some great side dishes and some great sauces and I would gladly have them supply condiments to any BBQ joint in St. Louis, but outside of that the rest of the meal feel flat and was greatly a disappointment for the price.

text:
Pros: close to Penn campus, nice pool and  overall the front desk staff, maintenance and most of the people in the leasing  office were really nice people. 

Cons:

1. Noisy apartments. On my floor there was a dog that barked throughout the day. College kids also were quite loud and constantly playing music. It was also annoying that we could always here karaoke night at Bar Americana across the street. Karaoke night is not the fault of Domus, but certainly something to consider when selecting the apartment. 

2. Be prepared to be nickel and dimed for every penny. I'm very frustrated because Domus withheld $400 of my deposit claiming they had to do a "unscheduled clean" after I left. I left the apartment with what I consider expected wear and tear. I vacuumed and did a quick wipe down of surfaces but this was not adequate. On move out they subsequently took pictures of EVERYTHING.  Crumbs on the ground, soap scum, a few boxes of food inadvertently left in cupboard etc as a means to "prove" their justification that the apartment required a clean and they have the right withhold $400 of the deposit. The other option was to pay in advance for a $300 scheduled clean. Either way they are going to take your money. 

While we are on the nickel and dime topic: parking is $150/month for the first parking spot and $200/month for a second spot. Meanwhile the garage is not even close to being full. Multiple charges associated with filing an applications, signing/executing, adding people/modifying a lease. If you lose a fob they'll be quick to charge you $100 for a replacement.  This is all in addition to high rental fees for their apartments. 

3. Gym average at best. They have the essentials but by no means is it particularly luxurious. I guess its convenient that its open 24/7.

4. Pool usage -  On ideal days the pool was overrun with college kids and all their friends (I can't blame them).  One time I came down and there were glass bottles of alcohol lined up on the side of the pool.  I can deal with the people, but glass bottles and no one enforcing the rules is unacceptable.

5. Gas fireplace by the pool looks fun, but for the majority of the year that I lived there the gas fire place didn't work. 

6. Fire alarms - Over the course of the year I estimate the fire alarm when off at least 6 times, probably more.  One time it was really early in the morning and people were standing outside in the winter in their pajamas.  I'm not sure how many or if any of these turned out to be real fires vs malfunctioning of the alarm. At one point the fire alarm when off several times in one day.  To my knowledge we were never provided an explanation of why this was occurring. Towards the end of my lease this wasn't as much of a problem, but it sure was annoying in the beginning. 

If you have the budget to live in a place like Domus, I would look at other luxury apartments in the area. The location near Penn is very convenient, but if I had to do it all over again I would not rent from Domus.  I do not recommend living here.

text:
I love this concept. It's simple, satisfying, comforting, approachable, and reasonably affordable. Most importantly it's something kind of new for our community. Solid 3.5 star experience here, which means it's good.

First time here and I had to go with the rotisserie combo. Half pound of meat (chicken and Tri-tip, which is served medium rare), two sides and two house sauces for $14.99. 

The chicken was succulent, with just the right amount of wood fired flavor. The skin wasn't as done as I'd hoped though. It's my favorite part of a rotisserie chicken. 

Now I usually hate tri-tip. I find it tough, flavorless, and generally hard to eat. Hearing it was supposed to be medium rare had me excited though. That's how I enjoy beef. My portion came out overcooked, and the server was quick to replace it. The second portion was perfectly medium rare, sliced pretty thin though, and it appeared finished quickly on a grill. It was tender and well seasoned, and I ate every bite. 

For sauces I chose chimichurri and aji panca (red chili, not spicy). The chimichurri was bright and fresh with a clear hit of citrus. The aji panca was dark, earthy, and smoky. They both made great counterpoints and accents to the meats. The sauces get 5 stars! 

I went with the corn salad, at the recommendation of the server, and had the smoky beans. The corn salad was interesting with roasted corn, poblano peppers and red onion, which made for a nice fresh side item to the rich meats. The beans were ok. I noticed some rendered bacon in them, but overall they tasted like basic baked beans to me. Three stars on the sides, and that include my sample of the crinkle cut fries I tried off my friend's plate. 

Service was friendly and prompt in the beginning, but as one or two more tables filled in, it slid a bit. I was seriously surprised by this because our server seemed to be aware of everything at the beginning and she did stay on top of drink refills too. Overall, it was good though.

I definitely think this is some place others need to try. There were interesting burgers, apps and more in the menu that would definitely make this a place I'd come back to for lunch. I also noticed whole chicken meals for $26.99 and that's killer!

After living in Florida all my life, I've been to the Strawerry Festival a few times, and based on all my experiences I've arrived at an "A-OK" conclusion.

The festival is a big "to-do" event every year that draws locals and out of towners alike who flock here for greasy, American fair food at it's finest, some rickety rides, a few big name country artist concerts and of course strawberries galore.

Last year when I went with my family of about 8, it was a big production to find parking and get inside the gates. A bit of a hassle for sure. I am personally not a fan of any of the rides and wouldn't get on them if someone paid me, but my younger cousins had a blast riding rides until they couldn't walk in a straight line. 

As far as the food goes, I'm really not a fan of most of the options here, but I did like the fried pickles, which is something I must get anytime I can find them. I was impressed with the wide variety of vendors selling strawberry shortcake, it was hard to decide which to pick. I finally settled on a booth that had some extra yummy looking shortcake and indulged. It was super tasty for sure! Also got a few flats of strawberries to take home and freeze for the rest of the year. They were a great deal compared to getting them at the grocery store.

All in all, this is a family friendly event that anyone who lives here should check out at least once, especially if you like strawberries a lot, but it' s not something that keeps me coming back every year in a row.

It has that quintessential Santa Barbara style which was exactly what we were looking for. It also has plenty of overnight parking onsite for guests, which is a huge plus. 

You get a great deal with Rockwood in that they allow you to setup for your event the Friday before your wedding and cleanup/pickup on Monday. This makes life so much easier not having to rush the setup and cleanup and it helps save money on rentals since the rental companies are usually less busy on Fridays and Mondays. They do require that you hire a day-of wedding coordinator which increases the overall cost of the venue, but we found that it was well worth it to have a coordinator there to help organize our wedding day. 

Rentals and catering are not provided by the venue so you are able to chose exactly what you want and how much you want to spend on each. Santa Barbara Women's club provides a list of preferred vendors that they have worked with in the past and every one of the vendors that we chose from their list was phenomenal. Sue, the event coordinator at Rockwood, was a pleasure to work with throughout the planning process and was very responsive to all of our questions. Santa Barbara Women's club was by far the best value out of any of the other venues that we saw in the Santa Barbara area.
