I've eaten here a few times and I do really like their food! However, there's reasons why it's a 3 star rating in my book.
 There was a Uniboil in my hometown, but I never bothered to try it until they opened in Goleta. The uniboil back in my hometown also made it a 2 concept store with Phresh Teas as well.

I've tried their Sichuan spicy broth and healthy tomato, both are solid. I personally pick beef as my meat.
Popcorn chicken is the best in SB!! Tastes how it's supposed to be, but over priced at $7 for a basket. Esp since chicken thigh is a really cheap cut of meat! 

Issues with the store:

My 1st visit, I came with my boyfriend and they ran out of popcorn chicken at 5pm....we did end up trying their drinks, also known as Phresh Teas. My gripe is that they don't add enough toppings in their drinks when it's a 50 cent upcharge. There was literally only an inch sized layer of topping. I ordered a Hokkaido milk tea, 1/2 sweet and I saw that it was powdered, so nothing special. However, even at 1/2 sugar it was still really sweet as if it was regular sugar. It's probably because of the Hokkaido flavored powder containing sugar already. This is coming from someone who grew up in the 626 and got boba everyday after high school!

My bf got the fruit tea, which is good and what I've had before in the 626. Got lychee jelly, but was the same one inch amount inside. Personally I'd prefer chopped fruits than whole though, since it means less of the tea! The chunks are huge and you can only really eat the watermelon spear inside. It's usually lime, lemon, orange, and watermelon, but I'd suggest they mix up other fruit combos as well.

2nd visit, I came with friends and there was plenty of seating. We wanted to sit in against the wall where there was a cushioned bench on one side, but we were told to wait for a table with all chairs. Took over 10 mins to set up one table even though the store wasn't even busy..
The girl wiped the table clean but it was still soaking wet and my friend made a remark about it and the employee just said "oh it means it's clean!" I felt that she didn't piece it together that she needed to grab a dry towel to wipe it...so we did end up eating at the table while it was still wet.

3rd visit, I came with friends who were fans of uniboil back in Monterey Park. We ordered and one of my friends wanted the korean army stew, but substitute pork with beef. The manager said we couldn't do that, but my friend stated that the other uniboil she's a regular at are ok with it. The manager said she needed to talk to the other owners if it's allowed, but I don't see why a simple meat swap would be such a big deal. 
Anyways, she did end up giving a side of beef on the house, but the restaurant could have saved $$ by just substituting? we were confused, but at least we got extra meat?....haha

Anyways, I am glad that more authentic asian businesses are coming in, and as mentioned I like their food here, but there's some stuff they can fix! 

I'll still visit when I have a craving~

text:
I was told to eat here by a friend, so I was here for lunch at Mulate's here in downtown New Orleans, which is close enough to the larger than life Convention Center nearby.

I arrived here on a brisk Wednesday afternoon around 1pm after visiting the World War II museum nearby. I didn't know that this was the original Cajun restaurant in New Orleans till I got there. The restaurant itself was large enough and there wasn't much people dining in at the time. Quite possibly have beat the lunch rush for the day. With that said, I got a table pretty close to the entrance, even when the backside of the restaurant was completely empty. The menu was pretty extensive and the first thing I noticed was the prices. Although I shouldn't be complaining and I'm on vacation, it was pretty pricey, comparable to other similar restaurants I've been to around the country. My total tab with alcohol and gratuity came out to be around $50. At this experience at Mulate's, I experienced my first taste of étouffée in a cup. It was amazing and so good. Even the server said that they make the best in the city. That's hard to believe, but at the same time, it would be great to return to sample other places to see if that's the case. The alcohol I tried was the Tin Roof Voodoo, I think. It was a pale ale that was pretty good and a compliment to the meal. For the main entree, I opted for the roast beef Poboy, which was served with French fries. It was the first time that I had to deal with a leaking poboy and the sauce. It was a messy but delicious meal that immediately hit the spot on this trip to New Orleans. Consider coming here on your next trip to the French Quarter.

The overall experience here at Mulate's: the original Cajun restaurant in New Orleans was nice and casual. Since it wasn't busy at all while I was here, I didn't feel rushed and I enjoyed myself. It was neat to chat with the server, whom after looked at my driver's license to check my age for alcohol, small talked about Hawaii and her trip there some years ago. It was nice. The restaurant itself was clean and aesthetically pleasing, decorated with Cajun inspired items and it felt natural to be here - even when I'm from Hawaii. Lol Mulate's is located at 201 Julia Street in downtown New Orleans. They accept major credit cards and cash, which is nice or ya travelers who are on the go all the time. They have limited parking, since you're likely parking on the side streets or if you can find a parking garage, that's cool too. If you are like me that day, public transportation via city bus and street car are viable options too. There's always uber and lyft available to get you here to experience the original Cajun restaurant in New Orleans. For the most part though, the enjoyable part of the experience was obviously the eating. The ambiance of the restaurant helped a lot, knowing that I was there on vacation, which helped appreciate my time here more.

I probably spent about an hour here. I thoroughly enjoyed the étouffée and the roast beef poboy was definitely good. Not too salty but just right. The fries was good as usual and the alcoholic beverage was the icing on the top for my stomach and taste buds to enjoy. While Mulate's New Orleans is the original Cajun restaurant in New Orleans, the prices sure is a turn off, but as a tourist, it's what the city of New Orleans is known for. Gotta try it at least once. The service was good and friendly, as mentioned before. It was interesting to get small talk about Hawaii when random people talk about your hometown like it is a fantasy. Guess that's how my life is. Lol And so, I would recommend coming here, since they do market themselves as the original Cajun restaurant in New Orleans. Try the étouffée or the jambalaya. It's quite the adventure for your taste buds. When in New Orleans, you should come to Mulate's for a Cajun fun time. I know I did, but my wallet didn't seem to think so. That's probably my own gripe. It's spendy - just for lunch. I'm afraid of what's dinner.

4.0 stars for the overall experience. 5.0 stars for the food, of course. 4.0 stars for the service but 2.0 stars for the prices.

Support local!

text:
I've been to Tortas Guicho Dominguez twice -- once a few months ago (before I decided to stop eating beef/pork/poultry), and once very recently as a newly minted pescetarian.  My experience as an omnivore was *much* better: I split their signature massive "torta cubano" sandwich, which was a delicious beast filled with all sorts of meats, cheeses, etc.  (Don't be confused by the name: it bears no resemblance to a typical Cuban (e.g., medianoche) sandwich.)

On my second visit, I was happy to see veggie tacos listed on the menu ($6 for 3.)  I was not happy when the tacos arrived, and they were literally filled with nothing but a pile of shredded lettuce and the handful of typical toppings (queso fresco, a bit of avocado, some corn and  tomatoes) that come on all of the other meat tacos, with no extra sauce, seasoning, or substance.  Honestly, I think it would be better to not offer veggie tacos at all than to offer such terrible ones.  There are SO many ways to make decent veggie tacos. (Throw in some squash! Or lentils! Or even just a bit more avocado!)  Needless to say, these tacos are not at all filling.  I was with a big group, and another person in my party who ordered the veggie tacos actually ordered a plate of rice and beans after to fill herself up.

My guy (also a newly minted vegetarian) tried the Pamela Anderson sandwich, which is one of very few non-meat tortas on the menu.  It was pretty decent, but nothing very special (especially for the price tag.)  In general, the prices are around $7 - $10 for a sandwich or enough tacos to fill you, served without sides (and you'll have to pay extra if you want chips and salsa.)

I tend to hesitate before giving out negative ratings - I want to extend the benefit of the doubt to businesses.  If Yelp gave half-stars, this would be a 2.5.  But my lettuce tacos were just embarrassing. 

TL; DR version: Check this place out if you want a meat-heavy sandwich; avoid if you don't!

text:
I hate being the first to write a review and it not being a great one, but it's coming. 

I have gone to the Aveda Institute in Castleton for a couple years now and have had great luck with the rate of mistakes being about the same as any other salon, one ever at Aveda.  On this occasion I went to Empire because its much closer to my house, cheaper, and apparently Aveda's phones just weren't working. I regret my decision and should have just waited. 

First, I called ahead to see if I had to make an appointment and told I could do walk-in until 2pm. I showed up around 1:15 and was told I "might" get in and apparently it was a big issue but never given a yes or no, just that the students were at lunch and she had no idea who would be free. I waited about 8-10 minutes and was finally called back. 

Now I know it's unfair to compare one place so much to another in a review, but I just had high expectations by comparison. Normally at Aveda an instructor would come by to talk to me about what I want after the student does to make sure they are on target. This never happened and the student just got to cutting after she understood what I wanted. This didn't seem too alarming until I found out that she's only being cutting for a couple of weeks and didn't know how to do some basic ideas. Not too horrible, since where it really went wrong was with the instructor. 

The instructor, Karma, never asked what I wanted and just started to "correct" everything, which is normal, until I realized that the whole inch/trim that I wanted became more like 2-2.5 inches before I knew it. Karma told the student to not be afraid to cut, even when she didn't know how much to cut. After I said I just wanted a trim, just shorten what I already had. Karma never asked for more details and by the time she asked the student, she already chopped it off. The one thing I was avoiding was chin-length hair, and that's what I now have. But the issues don't end there, Karma then made the sides uneven, the student did the length I wanted on one side, but Karma chopped that off too. I later found that they were left uneven even after I clearly stated that I did not want uneven sides and I am not interested in that trend. While, yes, the back is nicely blended (by the student) but it's waaaaay shorter than I wanted. I have lots of stray hairs that were missed, had to correct one side myself, never had the point cut that I wanted, and my birthday is in 5 weeks, a big birthday. I'm pissed. I didn't know that just shortening everything by one inch was so complicated!

Yes, you can ask "what did I expect? It's students." And I agree, but history showed much better professionalism from instructors in general, why should I expect anything less at Empire? Now I will stick to where I am comfortable, where I'm listened to and in the same 1.5 hours my simple trim took at Empire, would have included a scalp and chair massage and mini facial at Aveda. I now have choppy hair that is way too short that I never wanted. To make matters worse were the behavior of the students. One male students had droopy pants, another was busy picking at her belly button staring into space, another acted like the clippers she used on a male customer were a toy, and I kept smelling BO from somewhere. Topping it off was two students complaining about being written up for behavior. I wonder why? I thought they were taught professionalism! 

This is a long-winded review, I know.  But, if you want to save some money and try a school, go to Aveda where they have more class time before floor time and much more checks by the instructor. You spend a bit more ($17 compared to $8), but it's way worth it and the drive. Empire is really good for guys with simple cuts or women with long hair okay with getting an incorrect length cut off, or if you really don't know the length of an inch. My husband might still try out Empire, but clippers are harder to mess up, right? I sure hope so. Schools aren't the worst idea for a decent cut, I'm just shocked how so many horrible things happened in this one trip. I really could keep going into more detail, but I just don't have the time. I'm just glad hair grows back, I just wish it were faster. Approach with caution and don't be afraid to speak up and listen. It's your hair after all.

text:
I'm typically not in the downtown area during a work day but I had Jury Duty (Yay me!) so I was excited to see on Yelp that Holy Hog was not too far from the courthouse. 

When noon struck, I rushed my way over to Holy Hog BBQ. I've heard many good things about their BBQ and wanted to finally try it. I ordered the pork rib dinner plate that came with two sides. I chose the jalapeno mac and cheese and the green beans and ham.

I ordered my food to go as I knew I wouldn't have been able to finish it all. I also only had one hour and the courthouse was a few blocks away so I had to plan accordingly. I sat at the bar area outdoor which was nice. They had fans hooked up, so it was breezy and I never felt hot. I do not like to sweat while I'm eating- it's gross.

I enjoyed the green beans as well as the jalepeno mac and cheese. I love green beans so it's really hard to mess that up, in my opinion. I enjoyed the heat of the mac and cheese, it wasn't too spicy nor was it lacking in heat because you can still feel the kick. And now the ribs...I was looking forward to the ribs, but I could tell it looked a bit dried. But I didn't want to judge without tasting them. I got the smaller end of the ribs, so maybe that's why it was so dried? But there were parts where I swore I was eating jerky because of how hard I had to chew -that was not pleasant.

Overall, I think there are better BBQ joints in the Tampa bay area. I wouldn't really recommend getting the ribs or at least the smaller end pieces, but the jalapeno mac and cheese was delicious and so was the green beans! I'll have to go back and try their brisket, because that looked good.

text:
I had walked by Aki several times and didn't pay it much attention but I found out they have an All You Can Eat (AYCE) option every day so me and five other friends went for dinner on a Wednesday night to try it out.  Four of us did the AYCE option for $26 each.  To put that price in perspective, two special rolls is about $24, so if you have any sort of appetite, AYCE is a pretty good option.

For those that don't know (since the AYCE menu doesn't show up on their website), it includes about 15 appetizers (pork katsu, shumai, miso, gyoza, sashimi, seaweed salad, spring roll, etc), 8 of their special rolls (plus another 8-10 that you pay an additional $2.50 for), pretty much all of their standard maki rolls, most of their nigiri, and about 10 of their hand rolls.  Plus a $6 wine and $6 large hot/cold house sake options which is pretty good.  

The food itself was very good!  We ordered the sashimi, gyoza, katsu, seaweed salad, shumai, and miso appetizers and everyone enjoyed theirs, especially the seaweed salad.  As for the sushi, it was also quite good, not too much rice on the nigiri, which had amply-sized pieces of fish.  The rolls were very tasty as well, both standard rolls like salmon avocado, as well as their special rolls.  I was very satisfied overall and didn't have one single item I didn't enjoy.

One gripe I had was the wait time after ordering.  They only had two sushi chefs on hand when I was there, which seemed under staffed given the large number of people there that night.  It is nice to know your sushi is freshly made, but our first course took about 35 minutes, and when we ordered a second round, it took them about 45 minutes.  All in all, it took about 2.5 hours from sitting down to signing the bill.  One other small issue I had was that I ordered sake at the beginning but it took several reminders for the waitress to finally bring it, but it was very good once it arrived.

Overall though, I would highly suggest this restaurant to anyone interested in AYCE sushi, but suggest they order a lot on the first go-around so they don't have to order a second time.

text:
I hate to leave bad reviews and seldom do but I was so beyond disappointed with my food tonight. I've had a lot of Chinese from many parts of the US in my 30 years but this by far was the worst Chinese I've ever had. 

The portion sizes were so small. The pupu platter was the most disappointing thing I've ever seen. Rangoons were chewy as was anything else that was fried. Spring rolls, wontons and shrimps were also doughy/chewy. Spareribs were not what I expected, legit two ribs. Chicken wings were the size of my thumb, super breaded and had about two bites on them. Two beef sticks which weren't that flavorful and looked undercooked. I've never seen a pupu platter (even if it's just for two) literally have just two of each item on it? Just me? I don't know, maybe they need to travel to New England or New York, even Georgia to see how slammed these Chinese restaurants make their food/flavors/quality and portion sizes. That is all I can say, everything was the poorest quality Chinese I've ever had.

I ordered chicken for the kids and it was literally chicken nuggets. I have the same chicken nuggets in my refrigerator as I type this, that I could of made myself. Which, I get it, chicken nuggets, nice to have on the menu but does no one serve Chinese style chicken fingers around here? Kids were so disappointed, which led me to complete aggravation because they are still hungry, so am I for that matter. 

I was just chewing on a semi cold flavorless, stale Rangoon and spring roll for what felt like 10 minutes , I'm hungry, my kids are hungry and to boot I'm $40 in the hole. 

Oh and it took well over and hour to deliver. Just sucks, I'm a single mom and I didn't really have the money to treat the kids and myself as it was. We were all ready to grub out, watch a movie and treat ourselves and most if not all of it, went to the trash or to my dog.

The driver (aggressively) blamed the restaurant as to why he couldn't find my apartment. Which was an online order, which I gave clear directions to, three times including a text to the driver. It's not that hard to find, seriously. I still had to run across my parking lot two buildings over, barefoot to get my crappy food.

I won't ever order from there again, sorry.

We have spent a few days in this beautiful city having planned and researched the places we wanted to eat and visit beforehand. And up until this review, we haven't had a bad meal yet but something was bound to go not as planned.
The music, atmosphere and architecture are on point, interesting and well done. I used the ladies' room and it was clean and well stocked. My husband used the men's room and said that there were no paper towels. Ok, that's strange because when we got there there were perhaps about 10-15 in the restaurant. Not that busy. Didn't anyone check the bathrooms before opening the doors?
We sat down to order. No bread or anything to nibble on while we wait. I only drank water, hubby ordered a vino verde by the glass which is on the menu. Vino verde is slightly green in color; it is served very cold and it is light and refreshing. They bought him a glass of Pinot Grigio; it was unmistakable. Not one for sending things back, he drank it anyway.
My husband ordered the pork chop, I had the shrimp and grits. The shrimp was in this great sauce but I couldn't eat it because there was no spoon on the table. We had to ask for it. Both dishes were very nicely prepared though. We shared a mixed green salad with a very light dressing, almost imperceptible, but still nice with pecans and manchego cheese. No salt and pepper at the table which means the chef is saying he thinks the food is perfectly seasoned & customers should  it mess with their food. Well, isn't that up to the customer to decide?! Don't pull that pretentious stuff. You are not in Paris or New York. There are a lot of great restaurants in this city that have earned a James Beard Award that put salt and pepper on the table! The restaurant describes itself as "Mediterranean". We asked for an expresó & were told they don't make expresó. We asked for regular coffee & they said they ran out this morning. So between this morning and this evening (a whole 8-10 hours later) no one thought to go to the supermarket (or Walgreens) and buy some coffee? Who is running this place, the little rascals? Amateurs! Ok, moving on. We ordered a decaffeinated coffee with creme  brûlée and an angel food cake with lemon curd & berries. The brûlée was fine; nothing extraordinary, just fine. The angel food cake was a hockey puck; it was dense like a pound cake and tasteless . It was dry and tasted store-bought: they added some lemon curd (or lemon flavoring, not sure), berries and whipped cream. I could not finish it. All said and done the bill was about $100 plus 20% tip because servers work hard and I don't  believe in punishing them. Management/Owner, pay attention! If you want your neighborhood "upscale restaurant" to really stand out, pay attention to the little things. If you are not serving expresó don't say the restaurant is influenced by the Mediterranean. Those people drink expresó all day long. Take a visit and you will see. If you are going to charge these prices, ($30 for one pork chop, the meat was two fingers wide by 4 fingers long & as thick as an average thumb--odd shape, I know), make sure everything else is on point. And no regular coffee?! So much coffee comes into this port! Come on, you can do better. Hate to say it but they missed the mark. Hope to give them another try in the future to see if this review makes any difference.

text:
I usually avoid going to restaurants with large groups.  It almost always brings out the flaws in planning and service, and sometimes, the kitchen.  If this were a small business, I wouldn't even review the place.  But because my grandson wanted to have his birthday party at the Cheesecake Factory, his parents planned for about a dozen of us to meet and dine there.

I hold these large national chains which host groups to a different standard.  They ought to know how to do it through experience.  So when they seat a large group with half the people seated on benches, the other half on chairs, that means the servers have to reach over the chair people to place the food and fill the water of the bench people.  I must have been banged into or had the waitress put her hand on my shoulder half a dozen times during the meal.  And I wasn't the only one.  I don't really blame her because she had to serve and didn't want to spill the food.  But she could have asked for help passing the food or excused herself for the contact.  It's a bad set up and the management is to blame.

Of course, with a large group, you always have someone get a foul up on their meal and so my son's meal had to be replaced meaning he didn't eat until nearly everyone else had finished.  

The portion sizes on some of the meals are ridiculously large.  You can tell by the number of take home bags that this is a strategy of the company to get advertising from the colorful bags that they wrap the take home food in.  At the table next to us, every single person had a colorful bag to carry around the mall property after their meal.

The only thing I enjoyed about the experience was that my meal was actually quite good.  (I asked and got mixed reviews from the others dining with me.)  I ordered the Chicken Riesling and thought it had a really good grilled flavor on the chicken and the wine sauce (with onions, garlic, and mushrooms) was delicious.

Apparently they have a "skinnilicious" menu for folks wanting to watch their calories.  According to my wife, they were still quite high in calories.  Again, the portion size is priced in the $mid-teens for most items so you just don't eat the food you pay for if you want to not gain weight.  

Sorry, I can't recommend this place unless you go in a small group and have a huge appetite.

text:
I recently had the opportunity to dine at NOLA while in New Orleans for a long weekend. Unfortunately, it proved to be one of the more underwhelming culinary ventures of the trip. In the end, this place is set on appealing to the low and celebrity-obsessed expectations of the touristic masses, not providing a novel and well-executed dining experience. 

Food: NOLA features a seemingly eclectic menu of Creole and Acadian cuisine with some occasional Asian and southwestern-influenced deviations. Overall, I was impressed with the menu offerings, but less enthralled with their execution. I opted for the duck confit and fried egg pizza for an appetizer, the roasted duck with whiskey-caramel glaze for an entrée, and the banana pudding layer cake for dessert. Although the dishes were all generously portioned and expertly presented, I found them to be painfully bland, with not even a hint of the culinary ingenuity you'd expect from a chef of this caliber. 

Service: Exceptional. We were promptly seated by the hostess upon arrival and greeted by our waiter almost immediately thereafter. Throughout the meal, everyone from the waiter to the bussers and management staff were friendly, efficient, and eager to please. The service was also impressively quick, but not to the point where we felt rushed.  

Atmosphere: NOLA is located in a renovated, three-floor warehouse in the heart of the French Quarter. The main dining rooms are located on the first and second floors, while private dining rooms, a bread and pastry bakery, and wine cellar are on the third floor. The restaurant touts its dress code as casual, but I felt underdressed in jeans and a polo shirt - most male patrons were wearing khakis and many were wearing ties. The clientele is mostly tourists, particularly large groups celebrating various life events.

Cost: Expensive by most standards. Appetizers are $5-$12, salads are $8-$14, entrees are $26-$38, sides are $5-$10, and desserts are $7-$8.

Other: Lunch is served Thursday-Sunday (11:30AM-2:00PM), while dinner is served nightly (6:00PM-10:00PM). Reservations are highly recommended, but walk-ins are welcome. Validated parking is available at the nearby Omni Royal Orleans Hotel. The restaurant has a centrally located elevator, so all three floors are handicapped accessible.

text:
I RARELY (if ever) give out 5 star reviews, so those who regularly read them know this is a pretty big deal. 

This place is very small, with maybe a dozen or so tables - very Philly BYOB. It's decorated minimally, but enough where the slight authentic Italian touches are noticeable, such as the somewhat exposed kitchen, rustic signs, and giant espresso machine. The tables are bare with the simple candle and glasses decorating them - this place lets the food decorate the table, not a fancy cloth. It is all breathed over by a not too bright, not too dark light that allows you to read the menu without chancing a fire via proximity to candle but dim enough so your sunglasses can remain unworn, even at night! It's quite loud in the place, given the life coming from the kitchen and the seemingly always crowded tables inches of each other enjoying conversation, but somehow people in are still audible when speaking to you - good acoustics indeed.

The menu is large enough where there is variety, yet small enough where you cannot mistake the place for a chain restaurant with too large a menu. What I liked about it, and while there were many, they did not seem to follow the whole traditional Neopolitan red sauce model that seems to have populated the menus of many of Philadelphia's Italian eateries.  They had for us a basket of bread with a very tasty garlic infused olive oil that could have been a meal in itself. The bread was very flavorful, if not traditional Philadelphian Italian and went perfectly with the large, spreadable chunks of garlic that have been soaking in oil for the perfect amount of time. 

For an appetizer, we ordered the arugula salad special. It was certainly a portion fit for more than 1, definitely for 2, maybe 3. It had very bright greens, and prosciutto diced small enough where you could take a few pieces in at once, but large enough where, if a piece was consumed, it did not overwhelm, but rather complimented the greens and the cheese, a sharp provolone that again, complimented both in color and in taste - a Reggiano would have been too sharp. It was all lightly tossed in a subtle vinegar and oil dressing that again, complimented but did not overpower. 
Main course saw us both getting pasta - I ordered the fettuccine special, with a light yet flavorful red gravy served with Italian sausage, and my date ordered the gnocchi, again in a ragu. My fettuccine was cooked PERFECTLY - a perfect al dente. The gravy was a beautiful color; a nice red with some small yet delectable chunks of sausage and beef.  My date's gnocchi was possibly the best I've ever tried - well cooked, in perfectly sized bites, and in a ragu that put others to shame. It was light enough where you didn't hate yourself afterwards, but filling enough so you know that you just had a damn good ragu. The portions for both were large - almost too large, but when you have good food like that, it's nice to see a large portion so you get to relive the experience the next day. 
For dessert we split their home made Tira Misu. Very light, well portioned, and flavorful, you could taste the coffee, chocolate, and creme in each bite. It was enough for two people to enjoy and to round out a great meal. They also serve espresso which, while nothing to really write home about, was not bad and definitely was the real deal.  

The service was good - our waiter was prompt without being annoying and was able to provide recommendations as well as take orders from memory, an increasing rarity. I did, however, have a few gripes. For service, there seemed to be different people bringing out our food at different times, rather than having the same server throughout our meal. One server should be it, maybe a food runner or another to drop off something, but one person takes the orders. Along with this, while they opened our wine, they did not pour, and they did not serve our red with proper wine glasses, but rather a white wine glass, though this is me getting nitpicky. Finally, they did not seem to have a proper hostess - it seemed to be whoever was closest to the door at the time, or the owner, so one may have waited by the door for a while before being helped. 

I'd recommend making reservations - I called (they aren't on Open Table) well over 24 hours in advance and they only had one table open at 8:30.

All in all Giorgio was a very enjoyable experience that I hope many will share and enjoy. I'd also like to save the best for last - our entire meal, appetizer to dessert, was only $58, so definitely take the time to try this little BYOB out - you won't be disappointed.

text:
Came here with my management team to celebrate ten years in business (night two of a three day celebration.) we came because here were tons of vegan options, including vegan cheeses and toppings - and we have a bunch of veggie eaters and vegans in our party. Let's talk about the pizza, pretty good, Neapolitan style, with the added benefit of not having to be in the dumpster fire that is Naples. The food came out quickly, which was a true mercy (so we could get out sooner). The vegans were all super happy with their food as well!

I hate to leave a review like this, because it's not really about the restaurant, but the night was just ruined by management's choices. 

In fairness, they did call me earlier in the day and say "we're going to have a band tonight, is that ok?" I did ask if it was going to be a concert style thing, or like a chill jazz band type thing, and I was told that they didn't really know, but how loud could it be considering it's a pizza place in a mall? How BAD could it be?

Really bloody bad as it turns out. This is a fairly post-modern, open style restaurant, with exposed ceilings and concrete floors. Acoustically it's probably be a tough venue to start with, but add the 110 decibel Casio keyboards, pseudo-rock guitar, and the yelling of the patrons to try and be heard by their table mates, it became a  cacophony.

I guess the loudness didn't bother too many other guests, they probably turned their hearing aids down. As a group of diners ranging from their forties to their twenties, we were the youngest customers in the entire place who weren't there with their grandchildren.

Not only was the band so loud that literally no one could hear anything (not even a waiter YELLING in your ear), but the quality and song selection was that of your average night at an open mic karaoke bar in a Chinese restaurant. It was just so weird... who was the audience? Where did all these old people come from? Do they know Pharrell's catalog? Are there a lot of John Legend fans in exclusively white, retirement homes?

The waiters did apologize for it, the bar tender actually swore and said "this is f...ing ridiculous" and the staff seemed genuinely embarrassed about the fiasco. We got our wine comped even though we didn't complain - it was that bad! 

I think this is probably a good place for lunch or dinner when there isn't a band. But it was literally a painful experience that damaged ear drums, completely destroyed even the possibility of conversation, and ruined dinner.

Let us know when band nights are rethought - we might be back.

text:
Bourbon Street for sure is a must see when you visit New Orleans but be aware that you will most definitely will see a whole bunch of "oh shit, did you see that?" going on!! ;)

I do agree with some of the previous reviews left that there is a different vibe going on during that day versus the night time Bourbon Street & to be honest I would not bring young kids to Bourbon Street at night at all! 

Bourbon Street is like no there place around...you'll see LOTS of people from all over & there are lots of clubs to go to & of course many places to buy alcohol from since it is legal to carry/ drink alcohol in the streets in Louisiana as long as it's in a plastic container..which I have to admit is pretty cool to do :)...alcohol to go..oh yea, baby!! 

Bourbon Street for sure will shock you if it's your 1st time visiting..1st of all depending on the time of day you visit there's a smell that hits your nostrils that is a combination of urine & nasty sh$t but then you'll be shocked visually by seeing the huge XXX Hustlers signs/posters posted up outside of Hustlers on Bourbon Street...( you should have seen my hubby the 1st time we went to Bourbon & saw the Hustlers signs..poor thing was so confused..should I look or not?!! ;)))))))) it was hilarious! 

NOW, having just described the above to you please don't be deterred from visiting Bourbon Street because amongst those damn freaky, freaky places there are some AWESOME & "speak to my soul" live music clubs on Bourbon Street that play jazz & zydeco that you have to experience at least once in your lifetime.

And there are also quite a few yummy food places on or near Bourbon Street (Oceana Grill being one of those places) & Bourbon Street normally is where you will get to see a lot of the NOLA street performers...from tap dancers to drummers using nothing but a bucket & drumsticks..now that's talent!! 

Last piece of advice.. just be safe & be aware of your surroundings when visiting Bourbon Street & just use common sense so you can fully enjoy & experience the famous Bourbon Street!

Side-note: As of 7/29/2017 there is construction being done to portions of Bourbon Street right down the middle of the street & it sucks!! Looks like construction is going on until the end of 2017. 

-Rebecca out

text:
I can't believe how many people on here are griping about Casa Video's late fees. Seriously? They charge you $.99 a day (might be more for new releases). Blockbuster used to claim your firstborn child if you returned a movie late. Casa's just extending your rental period for a slightly higher price. As for Casa Video itself, this is the best video store I've ever been to, and I've been to some great video stores. If it's available on DVD, they generally have it on DVD, and if it's not, they have it on VHS. The few times I couldn't find a movie, I asked at the front desk and discovered I'd been looking in the wrong section. For the most part the employees know right where everything is, which is mind-blowing considering the number of movies they have. And, while the hyper-organized nature of the place can be a little disorienting, it's nice to be able to browse the "Giant Monsters" section. Or the "Derek Jarmin"section. Or the "Documentaries Addressing Social Issues" section. You could have a pretty amazing scavenger hunt without leaving the store.

What else.... The DVDs are generally in good condition. The employees are all helpful, kind movie nerds. There's an unexpectedly vast soda selection. And free popcorn. And a video game section. And a porn section. They're open until 1am, and you can return movies right up until then on the day they're due. There's an after-hours drop box. There's some kind of rent-by-mail program, which I've never tried. And they link your account to your driver's license, instead of giving you another card to carry around.

All told, Casa Video is one of the best businesses in Tucson, and one of the best video stores in the country. We're lucky to have it.

text:
First time I went to Valentino, the food was legitimately good. The bread, which must be baked in house, was crumbly and terrible, but I was able to look past this weird, weird anomaly, and enjoy everything brought to the table. Inspired by this previous dining experience, and ignoring a recent report from a friend who said the food was mediocre when he just ate there, I took my sister and brother in law for dinner there last Saturday. To put it bluntly, I was completely embarrassed. On multiple levels.

First off, we only went there because most of our favorites were booked. When we walked in, the cook, who seemed to want to be the host, almost mockingly wished us a good meal, and then said, "well I will be the one cooking it." Okay. Weird, but okay. So we sit down to the expected terrible bread (I had hoped the last time was a fluke),  and it was as bad as expected. I mean seriously, this is some of the worst bread I have had in Philadelphia. It is dry, flaky, dense and bland. Everything Italian table bread should not be. 

The service was good, but we were constantly distracted by the table of women who took the BYO aspect quite seriously, they managed to consume half a fifth of sweet tea vodka, half a fifth of Sambuca, unknown quantities of wine, and all of this before eating. They were incredibility loud, and thoroughly obnoxious, which was only exacerbated by the fact that there was NO ONE ELSE in the place at 7 pm on a Saturday night. Well to make matters worse, we could hardly hear each other at our table, with them sitting on the complete other side of the restaurant, and apparently the staff had not thought out the fact that a party of 8 was coming at 7:30, and so they moved the women (bottles and all) all of the way across the place, directly next to us. At this point, we are sharing the restaurant with the loud, loud, loud drunk women and the party of 8. Seeing the commotion the women were causing, they moved them next to us, and the chef egged them on from behind the hot bar. Awesome. The one woman apologized while her evil step-sisters cackled. Terrible. On to the food! 

So we order calamari to start. It was some of the worst I have had. If you ordered calamari at J and J pizza, this is what you would get. The meat itself was like chewing on a rubber band, the breading was wet with old fryer oil and there was scant a seasoning in sight. The (dare I say) tomato dipping sauce had the consistency of pre-made bloody mary mix, minus the flavor. It was tomato water at it's finest. Okay, I am thinking at this point, the food was good last time, right? Am I losing my mind? Is there some alternate universe where I don't know what tastes good and what doesn't? The entrees will be good, right?

Wrong. The only entree the was even palatable (honestly) was the black ravioli stuffed with crab. Don't get me wrong, it wasn't great or even good. It was okay. However, the sweet potato gnocchi, that last time was light, sweet and savory, came out like a huge porridge bowl of creamed chipped beef, only with bacon and a sprinkling of gnocchi. It was one quarter mediocre gnocchi, and three quarters heavy cream and bacon. There was no hint of sweet potato, and the pancetta was so overwhelming my poor sister could hardly palate the sorry amount of dumplings present in this giant bowl of cholesterol. I went for the veal "Al Prosciutto e Formaggio con Olio Tartufato." Which was supposed to mean "pan seared and topped with prosciutto & melted mozzarella, drizzled with white truffle oil." What it really meant was "unevenly cut and dreadfully over cooked what might have at one point been medallions of veal but in turn became so chewy I didn't eat them, topped with a deli slice of cheese, a bit of chewy, salted pork product, and whoops, someone forgot the truffle oil!" The under cooked potato slices and the half al dente, half raw kale could not save this meal. So sad. Seriously, the times when I haven't finished what I ordered in the last 5 years, you can count on one hand (probably 3 fingers), and if I am paying, then it might just be this one lonely middle finger. I was beyond disappointed, and with all of the options in South Philly alone, I will never, ever, ever go back to Caffe Valentino.

text:
This review is based on my most recent/second trip to Mama Campisi's - July 4, 2010.  I did go a few years back and remembered really liking it but not much else.

My husband and I took my out of town in-laws for their first Hill experience after an afternoon at the Science Center.  I should have thought first and realized it was a Sunday and that nothing would be open.  That's how we ended up here.

Though there seemed to be plenty of room upstairs, we got seated downstairs, where the ambience is quite different - in a bad way.  Should have known after having to go down a rather dimly lit flight of stairs.  Glad we survived the journey.

Service, in general, was slow.  The girl that was in charge of refilling drinks and bringing us bread was really scatter brained.  The knife at my place was filthy but quickly replaced when question was raised.

After a long wait, we started with the toasted raviolis - ya know, to give my in-laws the true STL experience.  They were pretty tasty.  I've never had the "original" style toasted ravs.  Different, but I'd eat them again for sure.

After another long wait, we got out meals.  I got the Mama's Trio - nothing to write home about.  I would have been just as pleased - maybe more so - at the Old Spaghetti Factory.  My husband got the Veal Spiedini which was pretty good, but being a provel lover, how could a piece of meat smothered in provel not taste good?  He did comment that it was chewier than expected at times.  His parents got the Linguine Salsiccia and Baked Beef Ravioli.  They seemed to enjoy both.

At this point, I would have maybe gone for 2 or 3 stars, but then there was Keith.

First upstairs and then down with us, Keith stumbles down the stairs to interrupt everyone's dinner exclaiming how 4th of July is his favorite holiday, how glad he was we were here, etc.  Ok...maybe Keith is some strange owner or manager...?  We indulge him.  Then he badgers everyone into singing along to "God Bless America".  Most people continue to indulge him while I giggle.  He stops in the middle of singing to look at me and exclaim "Don't laugh.  It's not funny!"  Well, it's not anymore.  He did apologize for disrespecting me after the song was over, but the damage was done.  Oh, and Keith isn't a manager or something.  He just some random Sunday regular, as was told while laughing it off by our waitress.  

I wouldn't normally judge a restaurant by the other guests, but the fact that the waitresses blew it off like it was nothing instead of apologizing and that they didn't stop him after doing it first upstairs really peeves me.  It really ruined my meal, and I will NOT return as a result.  Thanks, Keith.

text:
Nice place, some drawbacks, but worth taking someone there for a visit.

My wife and I visited on an early Friday evening. We got there just at the right time - when we were done, about 6:15, there were people waiting outside.

It's a nice place, great atmosphere and the waitstaff is very nice. The decor is very comfortable. It feels totally out of place for the neighbourhood but that's part of it's charm, I guess.

My wife and I each had a lobster roll. She got Connecticut style (warm with butter) and I got Maine style (cold with mayo). Both of the buns were grilled so they were both quite good with a greasy feel on the outside. They were both smaller than expected. I should have looked at the pictures more closely on Yelp. I wasn't disappointed in any way, I just expected a full bun roll instead of a 5" bun. (guessing, I didn't have my tape measure with me)

UNFORTUNATELY there was a big downside. Both of the rolls were found to have lobster shell in them. For $28 I expect that the chef(s) would go through everything and make sure that there was nothing there that you'd have to pick out of your mouth while you ate. 

I also had the clam chowder (again, smaller portion than I'd anticipated, about 1 cup or so) which had super nice, soft clam strips but, again, unfortunately, there was some grit/sand in the chowder which was off-putting.

The rolls come with house made chips which my wife stuck to, I opted to pay extra and get some fries, over (crispy) done. If I'm not mistaken the fries are not fried, they are baked. Over-done meant that they were baked for longer which just made them hard throughout. Could be wrong on the cooking method, but I don't think I am.

All in all, meh, decent but not spectacular. Nice place but more suited for the millennial crowd. 

5 out of five for atmosphere
5 out of five for waitstaff
2 out of five for the rolls with shell in them at $28.
2 out of five for the gritty clam chowder.

(Neither of us ordered it but they have lobster bisque, which I'm guessing is very nice. But you have to pay ($12?) extra if you actually want lobster in it.)

text:
Back to Cuba is a simple storefront in the parking lot of a gas station, serving some traditional Cuban fare. They do have some colorful Cuban decoration up all over, but it's pretty quiet inside. There are a few tables and you order at the counter. I got the bistec palomilla, which comes with a big bowl of black beans, white rice, and sweet plantains. Also tried the empanadas, one chicken and one beef, and shared a Yerba Mate soda. 

My steak was a 2/5 in terms of taste, but it was a good portion. It was really thin and limp, but cooked well. It sufficed, but I've had better, heartier Cuban steak. The black beans were badass, though. I could've had a meal of just that. Rice and sweet plantains were standard, liked both. 

The empanadas were really big, but about halfway filled with meat. Both were good, but I liked the beef one more. 

The soda was good! I've never had one quite like this. It didn't really taste like Mate, but it had a tea aftertaste that I thought was refreshing. At 42 grams of sugar a can, though, yikes. 

My boyfriend got a fish plate and that was a good one. I think it was better than mine. It was a thick filet covered with cheese. I recommend that one over mine.

text:
Was really excited to try this place as the menu sounded promising, but unfortunately it wasn't what I'd expected...

(Was also one of the people who read the Sauce magazine article about how fantastic this place is. In the article, they mentioned the She Crab Soup which is something I haven't had in a long time. I recalled enjoying it at a restaurant back in my hometown so I decided I had to go to the Libertine to try theirs.)

My boyfriend and I walked in and the hostess told us the only available seating was either the bar or outside. We opted for the bar. It was actually quite dead in the restaurant itself but maybe they had tables reserved for later on. 

The bartender was friendly and answered my questions about the drinks and food. I told him I wanted a rum drink but the only rum drink on the menu had other ingredients that didn't sound appealing to me, so I told him I liked sweet rum drinks with slight tartness and fresh herbs. Using the aforementioned criteria, he whipped me up a custom concoction. It wasn't....bad....per se. But it also reminded me of cough syrup or some kind of medicine. I drank most of it but didn't order anything else. Sadly, that was the best part of the whole Libertine experience. 

I ordered the She Crab Soup but I couldn't decide on anything else. There were other things on the menu that sounded good but after figuring out the portion size by asking the bartender and comparing that with the price, I decided I didn't want to spend a lot of money on a small amount of food. But I figured if I liked the soup, I'd try something else on the menu. 

My boyfriend is a very picky eater and his diet typically consists of bacon cheeseburgers from fast food places, pizza, and french fries. That being said, I thoroughly warned him about the Libertine's menu prior to arrival. He knew what he was getting into. We reasoned that they could probably prepare their Diner Burger sans all the weird ingredients listed on the menu... the bartender said they could do it, so we were hopeful.

Unfortunately the burger had some kind of weird spicy pickle-smelling sauce on it (he HATES pickles with a passion, and I don't mind them but I can't digest spicy food.) This was NOT listed on the menu at all. We had no way of knowing it would arrive with that weird sauce. He took one bite and immediately felt ill. I am glad I didn't take a bite or I'd have to miss work the next day! The burger went unconsumed.

Sadly, the She Crab Soup was a huge let-down too. I don't understand any of the rave reviews for this dish. It was so bland! Part of why I love this kind of soup is due to the sherry adding an extra layer of flavor to the dish, but not true at all with the Libertine's version. The sherry is in the form of little "pearls" similar in appearance to large fish roe (such as salmon roe.) Eating those separately was unappetizing and mixing them into the soup did nothing to rescue it from blandness. The spring rolls incorporated nothing to the dish whatsoever. I ate one and was nonplussed that they were added at all. Overall, a huge disappointment.

My boyfriend and I ended up getting into a heated argument about what to do since the food was so unexpectedly terrible. I ended up feeling very guilty for ever suggesting we try their food. Couldn't handle the stress any longer so I walked out and asked him if he could pay for the drink. Found out later they did not charge us for the food we didn't like, which was nice of them. I feel bad giving such a low score because the employees were nice and service was pretty good overall (aside from not telling us about the spicy pickle sauce on the burger) but it was really just a bad experience in general.

I may return someday to give them another shot, but not anytime soon. :(

text:
Attached to Garneau Pub, this Pizza place has been a long time favorite of mine and my family. While my mother was a poor student at the U of A some thirty years ago, she used to go here for a celebratory pizza once in a while. I believe it has been owned and operated by two brothers for at least these last three decades; it has remained seemingly unchanged all these years and is time stamped in my memory growing up. We used to come here and gather with my extended family to celebrate certain events or just to enjoy each other's company and some pizza. I think its central location, inexpensive menu, great pizza, large amount of seating, and also that it is rarely busy, were all factors that contributed to our increasing fondness for the establishment. 

Food: Unfortunately, I cannot be a very good judge of most of the menu. All I have ever ordered here is pizza so I will have to base my rating mostly on that. I will say that it is unequivocally my favorite pizza, ever. It has always been consistent. The crust is browned just slightly, and the dough seems to be fluffed a bit so the crust is not dense but light and crunchy; but not thin. The sauce is balanced, and the toppings and cheese are great. It's not greasy pizza. I don't know if I'm doing a good job of describing this. Maybe it's only good because I've grown up loving it. I would say it is worth a try. The rest of the menu, I can't speak to.

Atmosphere: The place has had the same furnishings for a very long time, but it is always clean and well maintained. I never see it busy in the restaurant, which in a way is a plus because I know I can always go there and have a comfortable table and service right away. 

Service: The service is typically friendly and efficient. It's not really a focal point of the place but I have never had poor service here. I will however, include as a special note one elevating night. We came here a couple years ago spontaneously after my sister completed her convocation at the U of A. My whole family exuberantly trotted through the door ready to party and one of the owners seemed touched we chose his pizza place as our spot to celebrate this special occassion. He bought us all drinks and joined in our celebration.

Overall, I would rate Plato's with 4 stars because I need to compensate for my own personal bias. To me, it is my favorite pizza place that I have spent many evenings with loved ones. To another, it may seem like a dated and avoidable restaurant attached to a pub. I think it is worth trying for anyone looking for a casual place to sit down and have a pizza.

text:
The following series of events took place on Saturday, November 23rd, 2010 upstairs at Bailey's.  This is the first 1 star review I've given on Yelp.

We showed up at 645 to find seats for the UFC fights that started at 9pm.  Every possible seat in the building was taken.  An employee, perhaps she was a manager or a supervisor put 2 small tables and 6 chairs on a side wall for us.  While she was setting up the following words came out of her mouth "that group over there offered me $20 for you table."  I guess first come first serve does not hold true at this bar.  Needless to say we got the table and ignored her request for a bribe.

 While we waited for 4 more members of our group to show up, the same employee came by twice and uttered the words "if your group doesn't come soon I will have to take one of your tables."  About ten minutes later she took 1 one of our  tables and 3 of our chairs.  

During the course of the above events about 30 minutes passed while we were waiting.  I noticed 2 servers rushing around the entire room.  The table that was taken from us was given to a group of 3 whom appeared to know her.  She got them drinks and food, while walking past our table a total of 5 times.  She did not ask us if we needed anything.  After the rest of our party showed up, we again gave them the benefit of the doubt and waited another 15 minutes before we gave up and left. 

Now I understand that Bailey's is a sports bar, and I also understand that Saturday was a big sports day, but you would think that a SPORTS BAR of all places would be able to handle the expected rush of so many major sporting events.  

My last visits to Bailey's for sporting events was quite successful.  We received decent service, they've upgraded all their tvs, and they've added an HD projector.  

I'll chalk it up to poor management and a miscalculation of the day's events.  I hate to say it, but I'll probably be back since they're one of the only bars in Nashville that show UFC events.  Hopefully my visits will be few and far between.  I can't help but have a bad taste in my mouth after the experience we had with one of their employees.

The menu is way too large. Reminds me of Restaurant Impossible where Chef Irvine talks about how it's hard to focus on quality when there is soo much quantity.  

Breakfast includes complimentary apple cinnamon, banana nut and blueberry muffins. We had a frittata and an omelette. Both was way larger than necessary and way greasier. Would much rather smaller items of higher quality. 

Burgers are ok. I happen to have ordered the 2 items that contain the onion marmalade - the pierogies and the sweet onion and goat cheese burger.  It was tasty but seemed like it might have been jarred, like one of those Harry and David relishes.  I've since learned that it is, indeed, made on premises.  Pasta dishes have way too much pasta and not enough flavor. Make your own Mac and cheese I found a bit odd. Even the base Mac and cheese has too much truffle oil. Truffle oil is in many items - as if it is the trendy ingredient and they want to showcase how trendy they are. 

We have their frequent dining card, but unsubscribed from the emails as we never seemed to be able to get there on weekdays or take advantage of the specials. We've collected about 8 of their $5 metro bucks but find them hard to redeem (one at a time, weekdays only). They do have a nice birthday special and rewards program.

Really want this place to be better than it is. Maybe pare down the menu and focus on key dishes consistently prepared.  Don't try to please everyone all the time with every possible kind of dish available.  Focus on what you do well!

Edited to incorporate corrections provided by John G (on muffins, onion marmalade and rewards).  My intention is to give my honest, obejctive and accurate opinion and I appreciate the feedback and chance to make corrections.  All good will here.

May I suggest the Sangria? Doesn't matter what color, they are delicious. 

The decor in the restaurant is fabulous and I strongly suggest stopping by the original in Ybor if you have not done so. The others are great, but this is an Institution and is worth the visit.

Stop by, you will not be disappointed.

My partner and I drive around hungry on Friday nights wishing for quiet place that has real food at a decent price and isn't trendy or 'chain' in any way, shape or form. If I have one more meal with 'looks like food, tastes like over processed, over salted,  underwhelming drudge- I'll bark! We were actually going to go eat at Ikea because, hey, it's cheap and the swedish meatballs are good and we could walk around afterwords and look at stuff we don't need. But I digress. This place is a GEM. It is a hole in the wall and the food is great. The decor is left over 50's and just barely hanging together. The giant hammer head shark actually lives in the entry way by himself. Too bad : (  
We  had the $20 sushi plate, edamame, shrimp shumai, and Jahp Chae (neither of us had that before-YUMMY!) We split everything and had hot tea in old 'almost fiesta ware' coffee cups. The sushi portions were generous, fresh and tasty. 
I had the feeling that if I could see out of the old blue nylon open weave curtains, I'd be staring out at the board walk and the ocean, atlantic city circa 1935. I can't explain it, but the city was far away and I wanted to light up a cigarette in a long cigarette holder and order a mixed drink. 
One reviewer talked disparagingly about the music. I think that was part of the spell. It came in almost under the radar from the back- we recognized everything, I kid you not-the mexican 'frito bandito' song  by some lovely mariachi band (sorry, I don't know what it is really called), Liberachi, the Carpenters ('just like me, they long to be, 'close to you'. So smarmy it almost makes you choke, but in that good way) and I forget what else but it was funny.   
I can't wait to go back. Don't look down at the rug, it's better days were 30 years ago. The waiter was so sweet, I wanted to be rich so I could hire him as my house boy. Now, some of you might think that sexist, classist and politically incorrect, but believe me when I say I mean it in the nicest possible way imaginable.

My husband and I were immediately greeted and sat and a friendly waitress came over to get our drinks in. We beat the dinner rush, so the waitress was very attentive and helped us make selections off the menu and answered our questions. Sadly, by the time she got our order in, it was like she disappeared. Granted, it got busier, but she hardly stopped at our table at all, and as we had ordered the chocolate soufflé at the same time as our meals, we wondered if she would remember to bring it to us. 

She did, eventually, very hurriedly cut into the soufflé and poured the accompanying sauce into it. If she had asked, maybe she would have known not to do that since I don't care for bourbon sauce, but she gave us no chance to ask what it was or offer us to do it ourselves. She was then off again and only stopped by the table to hand us the check. She clearly noticed that I had scooped out a big serving of the soufflé but left it nearly untouched on my plate, yet she didn't even ask if I liked it. 

The atmosphere of the place is awesome, I really liked it as a whole! Relaxed and fun. The service started out great, but, sadly, didn't follow through. 

The food! I had lamb chops which were delicious. Very happy with my meal. My husband was happy with his gumbo for an appetizer but felt like there was a little something missing from the jambalaya, to tie the tastes together. Overall, we would give the food (excluding dessert) 4 stars. The dessert, however, was sub par. Every time I see a chocolate soufflé on a menu, I get excited! Not everyone makes them, because they're special! This one, to my great disappointment, was not special. It was bland, and the texture was nothing like any soufflé I've tried before (supposed to have a thin crunchy shell, a light and airy filling, and finally a chocolate lava middle), but instead it was like a microwave brownie (not even a good one). I'm a huge dessert person, chocolate being my absolute favorite, and this was just not good. Add on the bourbon sauce that the waitress poured in there without asking if we would like it, and it totally sealed the deal. I took a few bites, hoping for it to get better, but finally gave up.

text:
I have pondered writing a review all day, because I really hate to ever be negative, and I truly respect the restaurant industry and the fact that sometimes there's just an off day. I'm hoping we just encountered a day where they were short staffed because someone called out, but our whole experience left us puzzled. 

We have heard nothing but great things about Jake's and have talked about trying it for weeks. Finally we decided today would be a great day to go for some brunch before Christmas shopping. My husband and I dine out frequently and we have had some terrible service lately, but we were hoping this would end the streak. 

We walked in and weren't sure if we should seat ourselves or wait to be seated. There were about five other tables of customers at the time. Three of those tables already had been served. We were promptly greeted and asked what we wanted to drink. There were no drinks listed anywhere so we just asked if they had a few beverages and they were brought out promptly. 

Then...we waited...and waited...and waited. It was over 25 minutes before our waitress finally came to our table. This was not the same person who brought our drinks. She came over and said "I'll be with you in a few minutes" and we waited some more. She was clearly in the weeds, but I couldn't figure out why. I was a waitress for 8 years and I know what it feels like to be swamped, but aside from one other table waiting for their food, we were the only table waiting for service. 

I watched the pace of the food coming out of the kitchen. One dish would be brought out while the others at the table would wait for their food. This lead me to believe maybe the issues were stemming from the kitchen. I'm still unsure. 

We finally ordered and our food came out about 15 minutes later. My omelette was first and my husband began eating my food with me while we waited for his. His chicken and waffles were brought out, missing the whipped butter and spicy syrup described on the menu. The waitress placed it in front of him and said, "Do you want syrup?" We both looked at each other because we thought it was silly. Who wants a dry waffle? Do people like dry waffles? Maybe they do, but I digress. She grabs a typical restaurant style container of syrup from another table and leaves. About five minutes later, she brings out the whipped butter and spicy syrup and says, "Here's some of the butter and spicy syrup that goes with your waffle" 


All in all the food was decent. I can't complain about that. Nothing to rave about, but definitely not bad at all. 

When we were done our server asked us if we wanted anything else. We said no. She disappeared. We were the only people there. She came out a short while later and began wiping down tables as we sit and stared at each other. She finally came back and asked if we wanted anything else...again. We asked for the check and she promptly brought it over. 

My husband and I have had four course dinners at fine dining establishments that took less time than this breakfast. No lie. 

We are not hard to please and we never complained once. I just decided to write this review because I was wondering if anyone else experienced anything like this or if it was just a fluke and we should give it another try a different day.

text:
The Raven (this pertains to the bar only)
The good:  The raven is a quaint hotel/restaurant/bar that has been an LGBT/New Hope institution for decades.  The two bar areas are not without their charms.  The front main bar looks like a traditional tavern and the back bar is a piano bar that boasts a very talented pianist.  The crowd at the Raven on a typical Saturday night is a pretty good mix of people of different ages, races and genders (including non-binary) though most patrons are middle aged white guys such as myself.  There is a room that is a dance floor and a back patio area that is used by smokers.

The bad: It is hard to find an ideal, comfortable spot at the Raven.  You can sit comfortably in the Siberia of the booth section, but if you do, you're very much in the hinterlands.  The main bar is long and narrow.  You can sit on one of the overly wide, un-cushioned hard bar stools (if you can get one), or stand against the wall and have every passerby knock into you.  The back piano bar often gets very crowded.  The décor of this room could be considered either "fun Gothic" or straight-up cheesy.  The bartenders are generally efficient, but their attitude ranges from neutral to surly.  The on-tap beer selection is four of the worst beers available (the best of which is Yuengling, which means a portion of your bar tab goes to support Donald Trump).  The very worst aspect of The Raven bar is that they serve their draft beer in plastic cups.  Drinking beer from plastic was OK when I was a teenager sneaking drinks at a kegger, but as a paying adult out on a Saturday night, it's just gross.

The bottom line:  If you live in the immediate New Hope area, I can see why this would be your regular night out spot, as there are few, if any, other gay bars near-by.  I could also recommend the Raven as a cool place to visit just to see what it is all about.  Personally, given my geographic location, I'd rather drive the 45 minutes to Philadelphia, and pay for parking, than to travel the half-hour to New Hope for this mediocre bar.

I have been going to Dr. Canatella's office since it first opened.  There are a number of things that keep me returning.  

(1) Professionalism ... There is nothing more frustrating then going to a doctor's office and waiting.  EVERY appointment (which I go twice a year) has always been on time.  In addition, the staff is very welcoming and knowledgable.  It amazes me that they remember details about me ... For instance, I am not the best at taking x-rays (I am a gagger - gross, I know).  Rather than making me feel uncomfortable and reminding me of the unpleasant reaction I have, they insert a smaller x-ray sensor making the experience much easier.  I have seen a few of the hygienist ... and liked all of them.  Unlike prior dental experiences, I don't feel as I must request a particular hygienist.  This helps me when scheduling!  The best is hygienists are sure to peek in my operatory to say hi if I wasn't their patient that day.  There is something said of the personal small touches.

(2) Cleanliness ... The office is very modern with beautiful lake views.  Each time, I go to the office it is tidy and clean.  The 10 second rule would definitely apply if my child dropped his cookie on the floor.  Mommies understand what I mean!  

(3)  Online Scheduling ... I always have my iPhone in hand and with little ones, I never know my schedule.  The online scheduling on the website makes it is easy to schedule an appointment through email.  My job is not the type that I can stop and make calls during the day so this is an added bonus for me!

(4) Spa-like ... Maybe all dentists do this, but I don't recall this experience prior to going to Dr. Canatella's office.  During the cleaning you can have your back massaged, listen to music or watch a movie.  For my winter appointment it was rather chilly - I was offered a blanket.  My favorite is the warm towel that you are given when your cleaning is over.  I was speechless the first time - now, it is an added plus to go back.

As you can tell, I strongly recommend this dental office to all living in New Orleans ... or even Baton Rouge (where I live).  I drive 2 hours total to/from NOLA to visit Dr. Canatella because I know I can't beat the service.

text:
Flying Pie marked its return to Broadway Avenue with the opening of their new store at the former Buster's location. For years, Flying Pie operated a hole-in-the-wall shop next to the Suds Tavern. They left that location after they were evicted due to someone buying out most of the businesses along that strip just down from Boise State University. That company's plans were disrupted when it turned out Cobby's had a long-term lease and they weren't able to get that last building. Meanwhile, Flying Pie had gone and was later replaced by the Pie Hole.

The Buster's location gives the Pie a lot more room inside -- room for at least 100 diners -- and they've added an outdoor seating area, a first for the Flying Pie. There's even an outdoor standup counter. 

The Pie hosted a soft opening Sunday (ahead of their 3 p.m. Tuesday grand opening) as a benefit with the $10 cost donated to the Life's Kitchen program, which teaches culinary and life skills to at-youth risk. That program does a wonderful job.

During three serving times, each accommodating 100 diners, Flying Pie debuted a new personal size lunch pizza with a thin artisan crust. I found the crust superior to their regular dough. It had a lighter, crisper texture.

There were also new pizza offerings, including a Thai chicken and an El Diablo, with Basque chorizo and Cajun andouille sausage and a habanero sauce. Both were excellent, along with a roasted mushroom pizza. 

The building is unlike any of the Pie's other Boise and Meridian locations. it has an industrial look, with lots of stainless steel and even a roll-up garage door that I imagine will come open when the weather warms up. Also new for the Flying Pie is an outdoor seating area and a stand-up bar with a fire pit over the edge of the counter.

The downside will be parking. There's limited lot parking and nearby businesses and apartments have signs telling customers of the former Buster's at that location not to park in their lots.

This location looks like a winner. Welcome back to Broadway Avenue. You've been gone too long.

I returned for lunch two days after the official opening and had one of their artisan pizzas, which I learned will only be served at the Broadway location. I ordered the Carnivore, with red sauce, pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage, linguica, mushrooms, red peppers & sliced red onions on the artisan thin crust.

The pizza was great. I didn't realize they were offering table service at this location. No more listening for your name to be called and going to the counter. They also brought metal silverware wrapped in a napkin and at least two employees walked the floor, talking with diners and asking whether they were enjoying their meal.

The Broadway store is using a gas oven, different from the electric ovens used by the other locations. It fires hotter and cooks the pizzas quicker.

I downgraded my rating after a disappointing lunch experience. I ordered a Carnivore on the thin crust exclusive to the Broadway store. 

When the pizza arrived, it was lukewarm. That meant one thing: It came out of the oven and then sat forgotten for 10 minutes before it was brought to my table. That's the only explanation I could fathom.

The temperature was more like it would be if you had a few pieces left over at the end of the meal, not at the beginning.

The layout has a cool speakeasy-like feel to it, almost like a mullet -- business in the front, fun in the back. Low lighting and brick walls create a secret-like hangout with a chill vibes, more like a coffee house. 

Overall, Avid is a nice hangout to enjoy a beer or two with some good company. With about a dozen beers on tap, I tried some beers produced in-house. The Reciprocal Cherry Fruited Sour was light, tart, and refreshing. The Bittah English Bitter was consistent, while the #Brown Ale had a nice balance of malts and hops. 

In an area filled with breweries up and down First Avenue North and South and Central Avenue, Avid is a sweet spot to enjoy some local craft beers.

text:
The Drivers Licence and Vehicle Registration Offices at Deer Creek Center has a confusing set up.  The testing center for driving permit and licenses is in the Department of Revenue building at one end of the strip mall, and you have to hustle a fair distance to the center of the strip mall to another office to get the actual license, permit, or vehicle registration licenses and documents.  It's ridiculous, but you do get decent customer service at this location compared to some of the other licensing locations.  This is also a popular location for first time drivers taking the drivers test.  A decently safer driving route than some of the other locations have to offer.

FYI...  When you are registering a car, you need to bring:

~a personal property tax receipt or waiver
~proof of insurance
~car title
~bill of sale (must be notarized if sold for an amount below fair market value)
~safety/emissions test certificate from an authorized auto shop (depending upon how recent your last test was)

If you already have a current paid personal property tax receipt, bring it and you are good.  But, if you are new to Missouri or have no personal property, you will need a receipt or waiver. . 

When you are getting a license or permit, you  need to bring:

 Birth Certificate/passport, Social security card and proof of residence like bank statement or utility (not phone) bill.  They are very picky about this and most people have to go back twice because of incorrect proof of residence.  Minors can have accompanying parents bring their proof of residence.

 It would be nice if these offices had better info about what to bring before you show up.

text:
The Priceline mystery hotel deal is like a box of chocolates, you never know what you're going to get. However, sometimes you have a clue based on the price of that mystery deal. 

I didn't let William Shatner see me sweat as he negotiated this $49 deal. Fortunately, it wasn't a barbed-wire-fence-around-the-property kind of hotel. It was nicely landscaped, included a small outdoor pool, workout room, free wifi, breakfast and a king room with a mini-fridge and microwave. At $49, I wasn't expecting this hotel deal to be a hand-painted Swiss truffle with a buttery-rich ganache filling. I figured the closest I would get would be something like a packet of cocoa powder with the name Swiss Miss stamped on it.

The free breakfast wasn't anything spectacular but it definitely added more value to this bargain. It included hot items like pre-made cheese omeletes and sausage links. There was also a big, steaming pot of plain oatmeal with butter and toppings like syrup, brown sugar and raisins. Some fresh fruit including apples, bananas and oranges. There was also a waffle maker, cereal, milk, yogurt and bread for toast.

The staff was pleasant and friendly. Every interaction was positive and they were helpful and efficient. 

The location was perfect since there were plenty of attractions just a short drive away. It was a relatively comfortable stay while in the STL area.

Not bad for a mystery Priceline deal. And, you can get some real chocolate truffles with the money you save.

The decor and layout of this place is both unique and nice, and we were all eager to get some food and drinks. We properly assembled our sandwiches, took a bite and immediately set them down.  The breading had no flavor and the fish was bone dry.  They also put the smallest amount of sauce on the bread (which was too thick and over-toasted) as they possibly could have.   We sent them back and both got cheese steaks instead. All that aside, the waiter started off being fairly attentive despite it being busy.
