text:
I have taken 2 classes at lithe and have mixed feelings about the classes. On one hand, I like that form was emphasized and a lot of exercise was focused on core stabilization. I felt that the instructers were energetic and attentive. The facility was clean and modern as well. 

My first critique is the language and descriptions used on the website. One class is described as helping you "return to your 23 inch waist." This is an unhealthy (http://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/educational/lose_wt/risk.htm) and unrealistic expectation that should never be advocated for by fitness professionals. A healthy waist size for an adult woman should be less than half her height, which means a 23 inch waist would be appropriate for someone roughly 4 feet tall. Another ridiculous claim I saw was that a certain class would help to "re-texturize" your skin tone. Though exercise in general may help to give skin a younger appearance, it's irresponsible to claim that one of their classes will specifically re-texturize skin. There are so many well documented reasons to exercise, that there should be no reason to make false claims. I also think the language that is used in the descriptions of the class are condescending to women. As a place that seemingly is all about strengthening and uplifting women, naming classes "high mini" and "skinny jeans" seems contradictory. Also, renaming classic exercise moves such as a heel raise to "stiletto" is another example of the condescending language that doesn't sit well with me. Clearly, this place is targeting adult professional women (at least the price tag would imply this). I have exercised my entire life and teach exercise as well. Women do not need their exercises renamed in order for them to understand them. Its exhausting to think that you have to re-learn another exercise dialect to feel comfortable in the class. As a female health profession, I find this language insulting. 

As for the classes, they were nice for light strengthening and core stability, but if you want a good sweaty cardiac workout, this place is not for you. I barely broke a sweat in both classes (one class was described as having a cardio component). Lithe might be ok as a supplement to a cardio routine, but for me, it does not fulfill all my exercise needs and is not a good value for the money.

text:
I've been to Nashville several times, including trips with each of my three kids individually on separate occasions (college visits, tagging along during conferences, etc.). It's the only place that has that distinction in our family history. The one place to which I have taken each of them without fail while there was the Hermitage. On our recent visit with my wife and grandson (who happens to be named Jackson, for no reason related to Andrew), our venture to the Hermitage was the fourth visit I have made to this enjoyable site.

A visit to the Hermitage can be dissected into five parts. The museum provides a great overview of the salient facts concerning Jackson and his times. The grounds facilitate an enjoyable fresh-air experience. The servant quarters provide insight into the slaveholding culture of the day and the microcosm of Jackson's participation in that institution. The gardens provide a more aesthetic aspect to the adventure. Within the gardens is also the family cemetery, providing additional pieces to the puzzle of Jackson's family history. Finally and foremost is the main house, which is unquestionably the highlight of a visit to the Hermitage. It's all extraordinarily interesting.

The museum itself is at the point of entry. It gives you the chance to establish a working knowledge about Jackson, his life, his family and those associated with him. What you see here will broaden and deepen the learning experience when touring the grounds. There was clearly a lot to admire about the man, but also a lot of things that cast him in a negative light. How you judge him, assuming you feel compelled to do so, depends on the weight you place on each of his respective actions and achievements, both positive and negative.

The grounds are amazing! Setting aside the historical significance of the place for a moment, if you are there on a nice weather day, just sitting outside and/or strolling the grounds can be an enjoyable experience by itself. I have been fortunate that each of my times here have been during beautiful autumn or winter weather, with crisp but moderate temperatures and copious sunshine. While such things are unfortunately out of our control, I can only say that the lovely weather has added greatly to my enjoyment during each visit.

The on-site historical re-creation is superb. The workers are "in the day" (i.e., they don't pretend to be living in the past while you observe and interact with them, such as they do at Plimouth Plantation, for example). But they are in period costume. On our last visit, we were able to observe the re-enactment of a duel. Learning about the ritual of dueling (and it truly was a ritual) provided a fascinating window through which to view an aspect of the culture of Jackson's time. Activities such as these add greatly to the enjoyment and learning experience of a visit to the Hermitage.

Roaming the grounds can be an eye-opening process. The slave quarters provide insight into the less discussed portion of the Hermitage's history. More recent interpretation among the documents in these buildings is quite illuminating and worthwhile.

The gardens are a nice diversion as well. Not only do they provide an aesthetic break, it is also there you'll find the tomb of Jackson, his wife Rachel and several family members. It provides a bit of insight into family history.

The house is the highlight of the tour. I'm a sucker for well-preserved historical houses, but the history associated with this one makes it particularly special. The furnishings are beautiful and the guides do a very good job with the interpretation of what you see when walking through.

In the end, it goes without saying that Jackson was a complicated man. His treatment of Native Americans as President and the fact that he owned a large number of slaves in his private life were two hugely negative scars on his legacy. Like physical scars, such character disfigurements can give someone an initial repulsive appearance. But it's only when we take a deep breath and adjust to that first impression that we can move past it to see someone like Jackson in totality; that is, with a rational eye. Once we see the good and the bad, we can synthesize an entire, often complex, picture. But good or bad, it's all history. The issues at hand do not constitute the man and the man is not the sole embodiment of those issues. This place helps a person to assimilate a collection of facts that are contributions to the aggregate that make up the mosaic of time.

text: On 12/11/2021, I walked into Gerstle's at 6p. There were about 30 people in the place. I sat at a table for 30 mins & not one person from the staff approached me. As I sat there, a waitress immediately seated a party of 5 on the porch area, and took their order. I went up to the bar to ask for a menu, as it was very apparent that, since I was not in a "large" party, I was not a priority. As I was standing at the bar, waiting for a menu, I witnessed the bartender (Noelle) arguing with the bar back. The waitress that had ignored me for the last 30+ minutes, went behind the bar, and Noelle started going off on her. I finally got the menu and went back to my table. I sat there for another 20 minutes without ANYONE acknowledging that I was even there. I went back to the bar and asked if I could place my order.  Noelle took my order, but acted like I was noting but a nuisance with the fact that she had to stop and actually take a paying customer's order. While standing there, I noticed a sign that threatened customers that if they walk out on their tab, a 25% gratuity would be added to their final bill. If people are walking out on their tabs, maybe it's not the customer, BUT THE STAFF that is the problem! Once my order was taken, I went back to the table. It was now 6:45p. At 7:00p, a man came up to me, put his hand on my shoulder, and stated, "I need you to move. This table is reserved."  I asked if he was the manager, and he stated that he was. His name is Michael, and he is (apparently) the GM. I stated that the table was in no way marked as "reserved", I would move, but I wanted to discuss the poor service that I had already received. All he could do was state "the POS system has been down for an hour."  Okay...not really MY problem. What is shocking is that if the POS system goes down, there is no "Plan B". There are no duplicate order tickets. They write down the orders on register tape. The time was now 7:15p. I moved to another table and sat there for another hour. Michael walked by, noticed that I was in the middle of writing a review, and asked me to be "nice". Now, the time is 7:45p. I had already been in the restaurant an hour and 45 minutes...and I still did not have my food order. Meanwhile, the table of 5 on the porch, had already eaten and left. Michael walked by again, and I asked where my order was. He stated, "The POS went down for an hour, and we have 40 handwritten tickets in the kitchen."  8pm, the large group showed up at the "reserved" table. Immediately, they were met with 2 waitresses that took their orders. One by one, I see their food being brought to them. I was still waiting.  8:30p, my food was finally brought to the table. I had ordered the BBQ Pork bowl & a cheeseburger w/onion rings. When the waitress brought the food to the table, there were no utensils. I asked for utensils, and she ran to the kitchen and comes out with about 20 forks in her hand. She then proceeded to grab each for by the prongs & distribute them. She did NOT sanitize her hands prior to touching the utensils. When looking at the food, the pulled pork was extremely dry and overcooked, and upon tasting was extremely salty. The temperature of the food was luke warm. The cheeseburger came with no cheese, was burnt & very cold, the lettuce & tomato were wilted & warm. The onion rings were also overcooked in dirty oil. I honestly thought I would be able to salvage the onion rings, and asked for a "to go" box with Noelle. It was 8:30p. At 9:30p, I decided to ask Noelle for the box again.  Her reply, "Well, we're busy!" and walked away. I watched 2 waitresses running around appeasing the large group & ignoring everyone else in the area. Around 9:30p, I finally got the attention of Michael and said, "I asked for a box over an hour ago. All I want is a damn box, pay my damn bill and leave this place!"  Michael (literally) gasped, and stated "Ma'am you don't need to cuss. It's very unprofessional."  I'm a paying customer. If anyone was unprofessional, it is the staff at Gerstle's.  I also spoke to the Owner, Erik White. He is the worse business owner I have ever had the misfortunate to speak too.  He lied and stated he was at the venue that night.  If he was, you would think he would have jumped in to help out his staff.  But he didn't. Truth is, he located in Louisville, KY and could care less about his restaurants.  He was pissed off that I called him on a Sunday to let him know about his restaurant. A REAL owner would work on fixing the issues, not laughing at the complaints the way Mr. White did. He honestly didn't care. All I got was excuses from being understaffed and how lazy his previous workers are, by not coming back and "collecting unemployment."  Maybe, they didn't come back because the owner & management are ignorant, selfish, and inept in how to run a business?  Don't waste your hard earned money at a business where the owner doesn't care about the customers!

This is the west end location of The Rice Pad, which has had a restaurant on the north side for some time. The menu is quite extensive, and full of Chinese and Vietnamese goodness. There are noodle soups, beef and chicken dishes, vegetarian items, and just about every combination of rice and noodles you can think of.

We started our lunch with an order of green onion cakes. Two huge cakes were served to us in a large soup bowl. The cakes were light and crispy on the outside, but soft and chewy on the inside. Excellent flavour and texture.

I had grilled beef on noodles with spring rolls. The beef was thinly sliced and grilled to perfection, albeit a bit on the smoky side. This smoky flavour and smell penetrated the noodles as well. It was not bad, just a bit exaggerated. Otherwise the meal was great - a goodly portion, lots of noodles, and the veggies were crisp and fresh. 

My companion had ginger beef. Although there is a ginger beef on rice, he opted for the meat straight up - I guess he was in a beefy frame of mind. The portion was huge - he could barely finish it - and the ginger beef was extremely crispy. He said he prefers it to be softer, but I think that is a matter of personal taste rather than the quality of the meal.

With a spacious interior and friendly service, The Rice Pad seemed to be hopping with business. The staff there were extremely talkative, with several of them asking us how we enjoyed our meal, and encouraging us to come back. If I find myself shopping in the west end again, I just might.

I don't think I've ordered it again in fact! Orange tofu, sesame tofu and general tso's are all guilty pleasure good if you like that sort of thing. But this isn't what this place is about. They're just a consistently good Chinese take out restaurant, so here's  what I can say, they always offer friendly, very fast service and of course, great food. As one Yelper said, don't get fancy here but just order what you normally would from Chinese carry out. We have yet to be disappointed with anything we've had delivered. I know I just said I wouldn't recommend anything specifically, but I can't be trusted and will say their Mei Fun is great. Light, delicate and noodles are always cooked perfectly for me. So if you know what this is and like it, give it a shot here. Just saying. They offer a sample of any soup you'd like to try as well. I liked the sample cup and mini spoon. It's all in the details, and they do that well here. Overall, I think this is a great addition to Goleta. text:
This place is really great. I'd seen it a few times in passing and always wondered what the food was like, and just the place as a whole in general.

Just to give you an idea of the mood prior to going to Cork last night: It was pouring down rain, it had been a long and stressful week at work, and two people I'd known had just passed away, one of which was a tragic and unexpected accident that very morning. Sean was feeling as depressed as me, since said person happened to be a good friend and co-worker of his. Overall, a pretty depressing mood we were in.

Since we had no food in the house, we decided to venture out. Stopping by the bakery next door warmed our souls (especially the smell), and then we headed over to Cork. They told us we could sit anywhere so we sat near the TV so Sean could watch the game. At least one TV in here to watch the game on = big time score for him. It wasn't very crowded at all for a Friday night due to the weather.

Our waitress (Fran, I think?) was super nice and friendly. She was really prompt, answered all of our questions, and was able to give a wine flight recommendation based on what I told her I like. She even brought out more mint chutney sauce for the lamb chops when I asked if I could have more (that stuff was so amazing.)

A delicious wine flight, lamb chops, and eventually, live music warmed my soul. I don't usually give 5 stars to a place I've only been to once unless it is really awesome, but I had a good time here last night. There were a few things that could be improved upon but they were fairly minor (tables were a little sticky and my wine glasses kept getting stuck, etc.) but really nothing that would ruin the experience for me. Also the music they were playing before the band showed up was another rare occurrence of songs that both of us enjoy equally. The band consisted of two dudes with their guitars, which I liked.

Price-wise, I think Cork is pretty fair, The lamb was $15 and I got two small/medium sized chops plus a huuuuge scoop of delicious quinoa and tasty mint chutney sauce. That plus the three different wines in my flight was more than enough to satiate me. The flight was around $10, if memory serves me. Really not a bad amount, in total, for good-quality food. 

I definitely want to come back here and try the scallops sometime soon...those sound good, as did the pear and prosciutto pizza.

Thank you, Cork, for making a really crappy night/week in general a bit better. :)

text:
15-20 years ago, I probably visited YaYa's somewhere in Tampa Bay about once every two weeks.

I thought they had completely disappeared. Then recently I became friends with a former GM of a former YaYa's store that I frequented and we started playing golf together. He told me about this current YaYa's location and said it was same concept, but did not know much else.

Since I had an errand at the Great Bay offices nearby, it was a good excuse to take a look inside a YaYa's for the first time since I last dated Caucasian blondes.

Logo is similar to the old look, although the orange and green colors scheme has been replaced and the menu has exploded with many more items and at higher prices. 

The grill right behind the counter looks exactly the same and the smell of that flame broiled chicken as you enter the restaurant is amazingly familiar.

For nostalgia purposes, I wanted to order that two piece white chicken dinner with the pita bread, honey butter and mashed potatoes and gravy...but I simply was not that hungry for lunch. 

Still, I remembered that amazing salad dressing from the 20th century and the lady behind the counter held up the packet and said it definitely still existed. So, I ordered a chef salad and even found that the taste of their lettuce was exactly the same as before. (Yes, I know that lettuce is lettuce in most cases. However, they must still buy the exact same kind as 15-20 years ago from the exact same distributor.)

The chef salad featured the cold shredded chicken, rolled fresh ham, cheese, tomatoes and onions. (I added banana peppers and croutons to it once I got it home as I know how to season my salads to my taste) Combine that lettuce with that dressing and that cold chicken and it was a total throwback lunch for me.

The man and woman behind the counter were cordial, attentive people who seemed to appreciate the return of a former customer. It also amused them that I was taking photos of the current menu and sending it to the former GM of the store that was about a mile or so away down fourth street where the Krispy Kreme now exists.

Sure. Now that I know YaYa's isn't a ghost, I'll gladly come back to visit these nice people at this store when I make trips across the bridge. text:
Having been to Reno only once before, I was excited to see what Reno hotels were like in comparison to Las Vegas. The last time, I only drove through downtown and never got to see Excalibur, Circus Circus, Silver Legacy etc. This time was different. This time, I was here for Kiwanis convention.

The rooms in the hotel are very nice and seem to be newly renovated. They feature flat screen TVs, very comfortable beds, and wonderful showers. The biggest downside: no free internet! If a hotel can afford free parking, I don't see what's so hard about free internet. Sure there's 39 floors to take care of, but with all the slot machine earnings, I'm sure they can afford it. Plus, they would make Cisco very happy. 

The casino area in the hotel is pretty awesome. The big dome and whatever the hell the thing in the middle is add a colossal feeling to the whole place. I'm not a big fan of people smoking everywhere, so that was the downside. However, that's expected with every casino, right?   

Food options in this hotel are pretty terrible. Everything is just typical crappy American food meant for the people who come here to gamble their lives away. Not impressed at all, but it seems like that's expected of Reno.

The hotel lobby is wonderfully decorated and was able to accommodate a large group of us when we needed to meet up to go somewhere. The convention facilities are very expansive and worked very well for the Kiwanis convention. Although it takes a while to get to, the exhibition hall we used was great, and even came with free water.

The one thing that disappointed me the most was the pool. For a hotel  of such caliber in such a hot location, I expected more than a 3 1/2 foot deep pool smaller than the one in my condo complex. Even the jacuzzi barely fit 6 people in it. My #1 relaxation method is swimming, which I was not able to do here after a couple of hectic days of running around everywhere. This is where the hotel pretty much fails. Free parking is always good, though :-)

text:
I used True Friends Moving for a local move within Nashville.  I would probably not recommend using them to anyone. The move took far too long and I was not impressed by the moving crew.  

The good:
- They showed up nearly on time.
 
- They have most of the materials that they needed (pads, shrink wrap, hand trucks)

- They made a good effort to not damage anything. 

The bad: 
- I was charged for mileage from the movers location, which is something that was never discussed. (this also never came up  with any other local moves that I've done in other cities.) So basically they decided to charge me for an extra hour, just because. I live in the city -- if I were moving within the suburbs, this would make far more sense. This also never came up in any of the estimates -- like when I gave both addresses.  It felt like a scam. 

- There was a long and surprising list of things that they wouldn't put in the truck. Like computer monitors. Or cleaning supplies.  Or, allegedly, CF lightbulbs.  These seem like things worth mentioning when you book a move ("by the way, we won't  move a long list of things that nearly every person will own. ") 

- The movers weren't prepared for some common problems. For example, we had to pull the feet off of my couch to get it out the door. I had to provide the tools and do the work. I should also mention that the movers just kind of hung around with the stuck couch for about 20 minutes before I had to push them to find out WHY they weren't doing anything. Rather than saying something upfront or working on the problem on their own.  

- Communication was a major problem with the movers on the day of the move. For example, they closed the truck up when there was still more to put into the truck. 

-  The movers weren't particularly motivated.  I felt like I was pushing them to work faster as the day went on.  

- During the move-in, one of the movers stayed in the truck for reasons that I still can't discern. One of them did a pretty good job moving everything into the apartment. At this point I was also doing some of the lifting because I just wanted it to get done.   The other one apparently took an hour and change to unload a 16 foot truck that was loaded out in under an hour. And then there were frequent conversations between the movers on minor issues -- how to move things, how to carry things, etc. The second mover was effectively not present during most of the movein.  

- Parking was an adventure, wherein I lost  the movers on several occasions when they had better ideas on where to park. Effectively ignoring instructions. I was willing to let it drop based on not actually driving the truck. But once I saw the bill. I changed my tune.  

- This is minor, but they left trash in my old apartment. I had a trashbag set up for cleanup -- and there was a used powerade bottle on the floor. It's not the end of the world, but it does scream of lack of professionalism. 

Ultimately it felt like I had a single mover for the move, and he wasn't terribly experienced.  I'm unlikely to ever use these guys again -- or suggest them to any true friends.

As much as I'd like to say that Brew Brothers was part of our plan all along, the truth is that we only really came here after our attempts to check out the vendors at Wing Fest failed pretty hard. Along with their half dozen or so house brews on tap, they have a nice mix of typical brewery eats (starters, salads, sandwiches, burgers, pizzas, BBQ, etc.).  Since we were torn on trying a burger or the pastrami sandwich, one of my friends and I ended up getting both to share.

-- CRISPY THICK CUT ONION RINGS with a Sri-Ranch-a Dip...$7.50
(https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/brew-brothers-reno-3?select=ki7utlJeZD-MyeN_kf1ihw)
I really wasn't expecting much, but this was actually pretty decent!  The breading wasn't too thick (or thin) and it had just the right amount of crunch to every bite.  Also, even though the onions themselves were a little dry, the dip helped a lot (plus, it had a nice, subtle kick to it).

-- BISON BURGER - Lean Ground Buffalo Patty, Green Leaf Lettuce, Tomato, Onion, Pickles, Mayo, and Choice of Cheese (Cheddar)...$11.75
(https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/brew-brothers-reno-3?select=ECScYDxRxT-PMeg80PCaDg)
As hefty as my first ever bison burger was, sadly, it didn't amaze.  While the overall taste of it was fine, the burger just wasn't as satisfying as I had hoped.  It wasn't shocking that it wasn't very juicy (bison is pretty lean), but I didn't expect it to be so crumbly either (just dry, not overcooked).  

-- HOT PASTRAMI PRETZEL ROLL - Thin Sliced Warmed Pastrami, Swiss Cheese, Pickles, and Whole Grain Mustard on a Toasted Pretzel Roll...$9.75
(https://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/brew-brothers-reno-3?select=MUiujxuQT4qd_HwZ6x_Jrw)
The fries on the plate were great, but the pastrami sandwich was awesome!  The pretzel bun was terrific, there was lots of melted Swiss, and they didn't overdo it with the mustard.  That said, the pastrami was clearly the star; plentiful, juicy, tender, and very well seasoned.  So good!

Featuring DJ's and various bands on a nightly basis, Brew Brothers also doubles as a nightlife spot (the place is pretty big).  However, since we never passed by it that late at night, I can't say how busy they get.  If their drinks are as cheap as their house brews though (just $4 a pint!), they might not be a bad spot to sit and enjoy a round while listening to some live music.

All in all, based purely on the burger and onion rings, this would probably be a three star review.  However, between the pastrami sandwich and the cheap beers, it's an easy call to round up from THREE AND A HALF STARS.  I'm not sure if I'd ever make a point of eating at Brew Brothers again, but they're far better than some of the alternatives here.

text:
Indianapolis Motor Speedway Hall of Fame is somewhat disappointing do to complete lack of imagination.  If you are a huge fan of the Indy 500 and have followed all the race car drivers over the last 50 years this will be a meaningful stop for you regardless. 

There are many Indy winning cars on display here with a paragraph describing their unique qualities. One of them is number 32, the winner of the 1911 first Indianapolis race. There is a nearly exact replica this car at the Coker Tire Museum in Chattanooga Tennessee. The current special displays July 2018 are an homage to the Unser family. Most of the non-car displays are about trophies and winning. 

There is nearly no discussion of safety developments or even mortality on the track. In fact there is little engineering discussion whatsoever. Unless you count the almost insulting animation in the zone 4 room demonstrating what a 4-stroke engine cycle is. My thought is if you don't know what a four-stroke engine is already, you probably aren't that interested in racing and won't be in this museum.

Unlike many museums, there is very little effort to draw the non-enthusiast viewer into the topic. Unless you're already interested in race cars you'll probably think this is just another car showroom. There are so many missed opportunities!

text:
Oof. This review is peak first-world obnoxiousness but we're already here so... my kale wasn't massaged. I know.

To be fair (to me), I warned you that this is peak first-world but things are what they are. When eating at a vegetarian food stand in a trendy setting, one has certain expectations about the experience. Since vegetarian/vegan =/= gluten-free, I always make an effort to find out which of the healthy offerings are available to me, as someone with a problematic belly. I was in the mood for a sandwich but the bread offerings weren't playing nice so I went with a salad. 

Kale salads aren't exciting or adventurous but they're good go-tos when seeking something healthy. This salad came with the usual suspects of cucumbers, onions and (red) peppers. The fancy element came from the abundance of cranberries and almonds. I requested the house dressing. So... what's the problem? The problem was the star of the salad: the kale. Kale is a particularly aggressive green. It's not like argulua or spinach. You can't just serve it on a plate or in a bowl. You have to massage it. That means you have to rend the leaves from the stems, douse it with a ton of oil/liquid and hit it with salt/garlic/black pepper/some sort of seasoning. Then you need to get all in and work the kinks out for a good ten minutes. Otherwise, you have rough, tough, hard to chew, not fun to swallow and not great to digest roughage. The texture/consistency of well-massaged kale is soft and lightly wilted. If your salad looks back at you with an attitude, it's not massaged. It is tense.

My salad was a teenage driver in a monsoon at night. Adding insult to injury, I didn't get a fork with my salad so once I found seating in the madhouse that is the Indy City Market and sat down, I had to get back up, work my way through the crowd, go back to Three Carrots, and pick up some plastic silverware. By the time I got back to my seat and started eating, my group was done eating lunch and I had* to stuff leaves of rough, tough kale into my mouth and join the exodus. I enjoyed the dressing. I liked the cranberry and almond elements (taste and crunch). Everything else... was ok. It could have been better. I get it: lunch rush is an in and out type of deal. Lesson learned. Save the massaged kale for slow dining. Got it.

*First-world, folks.

You hurt my dog.  You refused her the proper care and checkups she should have had as soon as *I* discovered a lump on her side.  I BEGGED you people to do a proper workup and checkup to find other tumors. text:
When it comes to breakfast in Reno, I'm sure there's tons of mom and pop diners that are unknownst to Californians. However, with Yelp's help, I was able to find Peg's and it's been a great find. If you want an authentic American breakfast with some Southwestern flare, Peg's is it. Peg's is up to five locations now, but I've only tried this location - the original. Street parking isn't too difficult even on weekends, yet there's an available parking garage.

On my first visit to Peg's, we were quickly seated in the busy diner. I was served a hot cop of joe and our waitress handed us our menus. After looking at all the Yelp pictures the night before, I went for "Peg's favorite breakfast", the Peg's Glorified Huevos Ranchero, a selection from their Monterey Skillet Breakfast. Each skillet is served with olden hash browns, pico de gallo, cabbage slaw, fresh pinto beans and warm tortillas. One word: delicious. It was everything I wanted and more. They even include a piece of fresh fruit, which I barely touched after finshing my skilled. 

On my most recent visit during Hot August Nights, I debated between the tamale & eggs skillet or the breakfast burrito skillet, and went with the latter. Given that I've never tried a breakfast burrito, why not let Peg's serve me a breakfast burrito monterey skillet? The burrito was stuffed with scrambled eggs, ham, onions,
green chiles, cheddar and ranchero sauce. I was unsure how big this burrito was going to big considering how much food the skillet already is and I can safely say I had a hard time finishing my burrito. Not necessarily the best burrito, with a little too much egg, but overall, another fulfilling breakfast with great sides. 

Both times I've gone, I've been given great service. After a night of heavy drinking, a breakfast at Peg's is the perfect thing before hitting the pool and loading up with beers. Expect to spend $30 for two people including drinks. Food is great, staff is great, and prices are a little more than most diners, but you get tons of food, all of which is delicious. I may have just traded in my usual breakfast at Hash House for breakfast at Peg's.

Overall: 4/5

text:
My wife and I spend spent two nights in this property, three days apart.  The first night was barely acceptable.  The second night was a disaster.

General comments:  This property is dirty and dark.  The floor in the breakfast area (and in front of the registration desk) was sticky from spilled food from 7 a . m. until after 3 p. m.  There was spilled food throughout the breakfast area every time I checked.  There was very little variety and the food that was offered looked awful.  Waffle battered was splatter all over the place.  There were no serving pieces in any of the jars of raisins, sugar, or other items to be sprinkled on cereal. I could say more but I think you get the picture.

There seemed to be a very large staff available in the morning but I saw no evidence of them working.  Instead, they were having a fine time talking with each other.

The carpets in the   rooms look like they have never been cleaned.  The rooms smelled musty, there was a large red stain on the white comforter  in one of the rooms we were in. There was a scarcity of kitchen items  in all of the rooms we were in.

The rooms offered the comfort and atmosphere of a 1960s college dorm or maybe a cheap music camp for teenagers...uncomfortable seating, a desk placed against a window that allowed the sun to glare into my face and tiny televisions.

Those are the general comments that apply to both nights we stayed there. The specifics of our second night are considerably worse.

We arrived for checkin around 3 p. m.  Monday July 6.  The floor in front of the check in desk was so sticky I kept doing a little dance so that I would not permanently stick to it.  We were sent to a room in a reasonable amount of time...and saw when I unlocked the door that the room had not been serviced.

Not a good thing, but not a disaster.  And the desk clerk was up pretty quickly with a set of keys to another room.

The disaster started around 10 p. m.  Our room was over the patio/entrance to the swimming pool. There was a large group on the patio, making a great deal of noise.  My wife called the desk and was told by Trey the pool and the patio closed at 11 a. m.  Not great since we had an early flight from IND to SFO the next day but reasonable.  I called again at 10:50 to confirm that the patio/pool would shut down at 11 p. m. and was assured by Trey that the people on the patio knew they had to close down at 11 p. m.  So when things did not shut down by 11:10 I went down to the desk to see Trey.  He explained the parents on the patio had asked him to keep the pool open and he had agreed.  He also informed me that the patio was a "public area" and that there was nothing he could do about the noisy party.

I went back to the room, conferred with my wife and called down and got a new room.

A whole lot of inconvenience and unhappiness could have been avoided if had Trey dealt with us honestly from the beginning.  We could have asked for a new room an hour earlier if we had been told the pool was going to be open late and the party on the patio did not have an end time.

All of this is totally inconsistent with my experience with Residence Inns.  We have used these properties in multiple states for at least the last 10 years and this is the first negative experience ever.  In fact, we spent the night in between the stays at this property in the Residence Inn in Columbus, IN and had an outstanding experience.

If I could give a lower rating I would. The representative from Interval International tried to talk us out of staying here. We needed to use the time by a certain date and said "how bad can it be?. We had never been to Reno so we thought it would be a new experience. Well it started with the "computer check in", why have it when there are live people not 10 feet away? When Kathleen checked us in, she informed the concierge, Tammy, that we are a married same sex couple. She said that there would not be a problem if we were going to the sales presentation. We signed up for the 90 minute presentation (another way of saying they are going to pressure you to buy their service) due to the "perks" from QM Resorts  We are owners of another Resort in Colorado and knew the tactic, but the free offer tempted us to go. We got the room keys and went to our room. It was clean and had the smell of freshly used cleaning products. To our dismay, the place was over rated having 3 stars. The appliances and furniture are dated and uncomfortable. The master bedroom only had a queen size bed, and the 2nd room had 2 twins. We were expecting a king with at least a queen in the 2nd room. The beds are so old that they have the grooves in the mattress on each side. The bathroom was not connected to the master bedroom as advertised and needed repairs. Caulking around the tub, filling in the cracks in the wall and the ceiling would certainly help visually. The closets had 3 hangers each, we were going to be spending a week there, not acceptable. No place to hang wet swim suits. The couch is not only outdated, ugly but very low to the ground and the cushions are sunk in to the point that it is nearly impossible to get up.

We were going to use the hot tub the first night and could not because there were 5 kids under the age of 10 jumping in and out of the hot tub. They were spraying each other with water cannons and generally running amok. The parents were either not there or were not watching the kids. We decided to go early the next morning and found the hot tub open and within 30 minutes the peace and quiet was ruined. We got out and got dressed for our presentation. We were greeted by David Lemus (a Broker and Salesman). He greeted my wife by her name and asked several times where her husband was, Where is Mr xxxx? Kathleen introduced me as her wife and he chuckled and said it again. I corrected him but no apology was ever offered. He led us into the lounge and said he would be back, it was 10 - 15 minutes before he came back and started his script, but he was fumbling and often unable to show us the iPad movie. He only talked to Kathleen and ignored me for the most part. When we told him that we were members of Interval International and owned 2 timeshares in Colorado, he said that the place was not very good, old, and was generally unacceptable to vacation. We tried several times to correct him and he continued his rant. We showed him the rating in the catalog and he still tried to badger us. He went on to show us what we could sell one of our units for and gave us a very low-ball price. Then he went on to the harder sell and kept pushing us without giving us all the information we needed to make the decision. Another gentleman, whose name I failed to get, asked us what we thought about the offer. We told him about our experience and he made a very sincere apology for his co-worker. He explained the rest of the information we needed and was not surprised when we said no. 

This is only day 2..... I am not very excited to see what else will happen for the next 5 days. If we weren't going to be away sightseeing as much as we are, we would leave!!!

If for nothing else, we will NEVER return to this resort. We highly recommend that people trust what is written in Yelp, we are not making this stuff up. DO NOT USE THIS "RESORT".

Oh, by the way, their internet service is NOT SECURE. You have to use their password but it is a joke. I could not get on the web without having to try 2-3 times for each search. It surely was not able to download a movie or anything that required any amount of data use. I ended up using my MIFI and burned through a lot of my data plan.

We left 2 days early. Love Reno and the sights around the area and will return but NOT to this resort(?).

text:
I'm not sure I've ever left a review on Yelp, but after my experience with Nashville 4D Baby, I felt compelled. 

My husband and I were elated when we found out we were expecting. I didn't think any part of me could wait until the anatomy scan at 20 weeks to find out the sex of our baby. Because I was so impatient and excited, I booked an elective ultrasound for the day I hit 15 weeks. We drove 1.5 hours to the West End office for our 11:30am appointment. We showed up at 11:20am and there was no one there. The doors were locked and it took 2 calls for anyone to answer the phone at the office. The girl on the other end of the line said the tech must be running late. No problem, we understand. Of course it was 27 degrees and snowing on that day, so we were stuck outside for 15 minutes waiting on the tech to show up. Finally, she pulls in and gets out of her car. We were standing on the front porch of the office and she didn't acknowledge us once. Not even a "Hi, how are you?" or "I'm so sorry I'm late!" Even after we got into the office she handed us a form to fill out without so much as a "Woo, it's cold out there, isn't it?" Nothing. At this point I was getting pretty annoyed at the lack of hospitality and kindness. Still, we spent a pretty penny in gas money just to get to the appointment, and I didn't want to leave empty handed. 

We headed into the ultrasound room and got down to business. After 5 or so minutes the tech finally warmed up to us a little bit and started showing at least a little bit of personality. We felt better about everything, and after we left we decided that maybe she was just frazzled from being late to work or something going on in her personal life. We were overjoyed to find out we were having a baby boy and we couldn't stop staring at the printouts of the scan. 

After getting home with our CD disc of images, we realized that our Apple computers couldn't open the discs. I tried on my iMac, our Mac Book Pro, and a friend's Mac Book. Nothing worked. It kept showing up as a "unreadable" disc. I gave 4D Baby a call and they were very kind in offering to send us another disc, free of charge. I waited for about one week and then the disc showed up. Same thing, unreadable. I gave them a call back and was met with "Well, maybe it's your computer" excuses. Well, if it were my computer then why did it do it on 3 different ones? (Come to find out sometimes PCs compress images on a CD in a way that Macs have a hard time reading - Understandable. And not their fault necessarily). 

The following weeks were back and forth phone calls between me and the 4D Baby offices. I didn't have access to anyone with a PC computer as all of our family and friends use Apple, so I asked if they could just email me the images that way I could have them (afterall, I did pay $100 to have the images) and they said sure. Days passed, then weeks. After them promising on multiple occasions to send the files and then to follow up with me, they never did. Now I'm 27 weeks pregnant and still never received the first digital photo of our baby at 15 weeks. It's frustrating to have waited this long and still get nothing, especially after paying what we did and driving as far as we had. 

Had it just been the lack of friendliness, or just the disc debacle, I probably would've let it go. But I feel disappointed with our experience with 4D Baby considering all of the above. We're hoping to do another ultrasound in the coming weeks to see the baby all filled out, and hopefully to get a face shot, but I won't be booking with this business. Despite being totally hormonal at this point, I'm certainly not an unreasonable customer in hoping that I'd actually get what I paid for. I'll give 2 stars simply because it was such a treat to know the sex 5 weeks early, but otherwise I'd give 1 star.

text:
Hmm - I just had a perfectly fine lunch at Zama, but I am honestly not sure what all of the fuss is about.  

My lunching partner and I were seated quickly towards the rear of the largely empty restaurant.  Our table vibrated noticeably throughout the meal, which was not a huge deal but was distracting enough to mention.  The decor was nice and simple, with a lot of light wood and whimsical touches.  We were quickly provided with water, menus and an explanation of some special items by our waiter.

Between the two of us, we had miso soup, assorted sashimi, and three rolls (spicy crunchy tuna, smoked salmon and fig, and yellowtail mango jalapeno), and everything was good to very good.  The yellowtail roll was, by far, the best.  The smoked salmon and fig worked better in theory than it did in execution.  We also had some Japanese beers, and were tempted into assembling a trio of mini desserts (yuzu creme brulee, fig and brown sugar tart, and a chocolate bread pudding).  The desserts were surprisingly outstanding, and almost tempted me to up the review to four stars.

However, I just can't do four stars for this experience.  For a ~$100 lunch for two, I was not particularly full when I left and the only food item that really made me ecstatic was the yuzu creme brulee.  The beer list was uninspired, and the by the glass wines were arguably overpriced.  They were also unwilling or unable to accommodate the fairly simple request of having a few pieces of sashimi brought out at the same time as the soup.  

At the moment, I would rank Zama behind Fat Salmon and Umai Umai for my mid-range sushi needs.  That being said, I would have no problem giving Zama another shot, and will update if i do.

text:
I stopped by FedNuts at around 3pm yesterday for a quick late lunch after getting into Philly on the train.  I wasn't planning to stop by, per se, but since I didn't have any cash on me, I couldn't hit the food cart I wanted to try.  I decided to try FedNuts instead since it was located between the train station and the location of my meeting and I have a soft spot for fried chicken and donuts.

Given that most of the chicken comes by the half or whole bird, I decided to go with the chicken sandwich ($6.75), which consisted of a chicken breast, spicy sauce, and pickles, reminiscent of a Chick-Fil-A sandwich.  It was a bit greasy, but was quite delicious, easily beating its fast food cousin.  The chicken was crisp on the outside and moist on the inside, as good fried chicken should be.  The spicy sauce added a nice kick, and the tartness of the pickles cut the richness of the rest of the sandwich nicely.

Since all of the fancy donuts were out at the time of my visit, I also ordered a strawberry lavender hot and fresh donut ($2.50).  True to its name, the donut was served hot out of the fryer, and the smell was quite intoxicating, so I didn't delay to nosh on it immediately while waiting for my sandwich and while walking to my destination.  The donut was a bit different than what I expected--rather than being glazed, it's coated with a sugary mixture incorporating strawberries and lavender seed.  While I enjoyed it, I'm not sure that it's worth 2.5 times the price of a donut at Beiler's, which has the best donuts I've ever put in my mouth, bar none.

Overall, I enjoyed my tasty and reasonably-priced (albeit unhealthy...) lunch from FedNuts.  Though there were only two employees working at the time of my visit, they were friendly and efficient--my order came out in about 5 min.  Though I'd return to try the chicken (which I understand comes with different rubs, etc., for regular orders), I'll stick to Beiler's to satisfy my donut cravings when in Philly.

text:
Honestly, I've tried so hard to love Noble Pie. The atmosphere is relaxed, the decor is unique, and the location is convenient and historical. The place is often the site for local music and events, and the clientele is interesting and polite. The food is generally pretty quality when done right, and the names are creative in that independent-and-quirky-restaurant sort of way. 

However, the service leaves much to be desired. I have only ever been greeted enthusiastically (read: politely) a couple of times, and those were usually times that I or someone I was with knew the person behind the counter. There is a clear view into the kitchen in the back, where it's almost painfully easy to see the ever-changing cook crew lounging about, fucking around, or being a little too friendly with the food (not the most sanitary bunch). 

The wait is long. I'm a patient person. I have no problem waiting for my food when it's quality stuff. If you're willing to brave a wait, it might be worth it to you, but I'm just saying: be warned. An order of wings and a pizza will set you back about thirty to forty minutes. It's not excessive, but it is a while to wait in a restaurant.

Now for my own experience. Nobly Pie advertises themselves as vegan friendly, which lends a great opportunity to Renoites and visitors who have alternative food tastes or food allergies. I happen to be one of those people. Unfortunately, on no less than three occasions, I have placed very specific orders for totally vegan pizzas (which are NOT cheap even regularly, mind you), only to be disappointed by genuine non-vegan cheeses, milk-based sauces, or full blown meats topping my pie. Now, with the extra prices garnered from toppings, it's generally easier to order a specialty pizza and simply modify it to be vegan. That being the case, I can see where a cook might make the wrong assumptions based on the name of the order and mess it up somehow. Or, you know, any number things. Maybe it was an off day, maybe they just forgot. But three times? You know way they say: three strikes, and you're out, Noble Pie.

text:
I secretly long to live a sitcom-worthy life. I fantasize about being able to go to a place and have everyone know your name and remember what your favorite drink is or what kind of food I order every time I go there.

Well, this place isn't it, but we're trying. 

Pint Downtown is a busy pub, not really much for dancing, but definitely a place where you can watch a sporting event with ease or hang around with your friends for an extended period of time without being interrupted constantly by a server (unless it's a really busy night and this girl is trying to finish her shift so that she can leave). 

I only come here on Wednesdays for girls-only wing nights, and the place is almost always packed, but nobody seems to be too upset or surprised by it. They have 40 different kinds of wings and beer is available in table-keg form, so we realistically only need to see the waitress 2-3 times in a night (once to order the keg and wings, twice to order another keg and a second round of wings, and the last time to pay). This works out well because the waitresses here are an endangered species, and it usually isn't hard to find guys who want to buy drinks for a table full of girls if we run out for a bit. 

I tend not to get too strung out about absentee waitresses in a pub setting when we can just walk up to the bar (where the bartenders can't run away from you) to get another drink, or tell the waitresses to get out of the back room and carry the table keg to the table for them. It's a little more annoying when you'd like to pay and they're nowhere to be found (and when you're trying to establish rapport to create your sitcom, it would be so much nicer if these women just worked in your favor), but it just leaves you with a little more time to converse with your friends. It's busy, I get it.

At the end of the day, the wings are good, the beer is plentiful, and maybe after we go there every week all summer, these girls might at least recognize our faces (and if we're really lucky, which wings we ordered).

text:
I went here today for bikini waxing services. I don't think I'll go back. 

When I walked in, I hate to say it, but the place kind of smelled like a dog grooming salon. I wonder if they have ventilation issues or something. It was aesthetically very pretty and looked clean, but I was a bit put off by the smell. The receptionist was busy checking out other clients and talking with someone she appeared to be friends with, so it took a minute to get me checked in.  I wasn't really warmly greeted and the receptionist went right back to talking to her friend rather than welcoming me, a new client.

I was on time for my waxing appointment, and the waxer was running behind, but no one bothered to tell me, or even check in to see how I was doing during my wait or apologize for not running on schedule. No one asked me to take a seat or offered me any coffee or water from their refreshment area until a random stylist came up to me after I had been waiting for about 10 minutes already. 

When my waxer came out, she was visibly flustered because she was running behind. I kind of felt bad for her. Granted, I was using a Groupon for waxing services so I'm sure that's why she was so busy. She was very nice throughout the whole appointment.

She led me into the waxing room, which was nice looking and private. She had me take off my shoes and pants with her in the room, which I thought was a little strange. When I have gotten waxed before  I was given a few minutes of privacy to do this. 

She had me leave may panties on to wax as well. I guess some people do it that way, but again, I had always had my knickers off before when having this service. Then came the reason I won't return: She used the same metal spatula to apply all my wax and was "double dipping" in the wax pot. If I wasn't in such a rush to get this done for a special occasion and I hadn't bought the groupon already, I would have ended the appointment. That is extremely unhygenic. Now I get to spend the next week or so praying that I don't get a skin infection or anything. I was also bruised just a bit, but not much. My waxer also told me her last 2 appointments directly before me were also for bikini services, so all I was thinking the whole time was "ew" and "man, I hope those other 2 girls showered as thoroughly as I did before their appointments."

I can't speak for their other salon services, but for what they charge for a wax, to be treated the way I was and for the waxing to be unhygenic like that I feel ripped off. I'll probably call and complain about the 'double dipping,' because that just shouldn't EVER happen. The only reason this place gets 2 stars is because it did look nice, the waiting area was comfortable, and my waxer was very sweet and friendly.

EDIT: I called the salon and expressed my concerns about the waxing method. My waxer called me back promptly and informed me that they use NuFree waxing product, which is 'self sanitizing,' allowing them to use one spatula per client (I did forget to mention a new, clean spatula was used on me). I did look it up online and was able to find a scientific published study that seems to back up this claim. Still, based on my other experiences there, I don't know that I would go back.

I would have taken a picture to post, but my cell phone camera is awful- but trust me, it is weird, long and flat with little fork points at the end.  The spoons are actually larger than a standard kitchen ladle and hard to use.The seating as someone else mentioned is uncomfortable and you get the feeling was chosen for looks rather than comfort for the diners.

The menu itself is weird. I am a huge fan of starters and there was actually nothing on the 2 page long starter section that I wanted to try. We looked at it about 5 times trying to come up with something that sounded OK, but everything was just weird and there was really nothing appealing and really nothing Japanese, at least not traditional Japanese that I could see. Other than the starter menu, there are but 4 soups to choose as your main course and that's the entire menu, apart from the pie.

The service- It was OK, but again a little weird. We were first told about all the drinks that they were out of, and it was a long list. Then they explained what the 2 mystery bowls of spices were on the table and I seem to remember something about chia seeds and salt....and the rest of the service was fine, but you get the feeling that they would like to scrape you off their boot as quickly as possible.

The Food- Oh dear! If the rest of the situation does not make you turn and run for the door, the the food will surely keep you from coming back again! We both ordered the Ramen Soups. I ordered the Veggie and he ordered the house Ramen which had pork in a chicken broth along with various veggies and mushrooms. Mine came with Tofu, an Egg, and veggies. The soups were TINY!!! I am used to Ramen soup. I love Ramen Soup!! I was so excited that Ramen soup finally made an appearance in NOLA. But, my friends, this is not good Ramen. It really is not, I promise you. The bowl was small and had weird things in it such as pickled carrots and that was not a garnish, it was a main part of the meal. The Tofu was a single thin slice of Tofu. I was kinda hoping for some nutrition and protein with my dinner, thank you very much! The veggie soup came with an egg and I really did not like it. It was weird, gooey and awkward to try and eat with a giant spoon and chopsticks. My noodles had a huge clump that were stuck together and not cooked.

My partner had a couple bites of his soup and then pushed the bowl away in disgust. I felt so bad because I had asked to try the place. He declared Cup-O-Soup a better flavor and value. Sadly, he is right.

The Pie- We decided to try the pie because I love Pie and we were still famished after our, um, meal. I had the Peanut Butter an Jam pie with an oatmeal crust. The oatmeal crust was way overcooked to the point where it was impossible to cut through and eat with the rest of the pie. The peanut butter pie filling itself was drizzled with the jam, and that was velvety and delicious, but very small for the $5 the slice cost. 2 people really could not share the pie and feel satisfied. My partner had the Satsuma Pumpkin. He didn't really like it, especially once he tried the peanut butter. I have to agree with him that the Pumpkin had very little flavor and I actually make a much better Pumpkin silk pie when I can be bothered to do so (thank you Moosewood Cookbook!). For the $38 it cost us for 2 small soups, 2 small pieces of pie and 2 glasses of water, we won't be back. I give this place 6-9 months before they find themselves with no customers. It's a shame, because this town really, really needs more than Vietnamese and Creole and fast  food!!

text:
If you need a temporary home away from home, the  Stay America (101 Diemer Drive, Mount Laurel, NJ 08054) might be your best bet, especially if you have a pet. The hotel staff are friendly and helpful, and the accommodations are basic for a fairly reasonable price. If you're looking for luxury, though, this is not the place to be. 

You get a room (or "suite") with a queen bed, full refrigerator, and cooktop stove with a sink and microwave. The furniture and carpeting are decades old, but the mattresses are newer and comfortable. Rooms are cleaned with linens and towels changed once weekly and "breakfast" is included each morning from 5 AM to 9 AM. 

Breakfast is set up on a cart in the lobby offering a basket of Nature Valley snack bars, packaged muffins, apples and oranges, and microwaveable instant Quaker oatmeal to bring back to your room. Dishes and flatware are available upon request. Delicious fresh coffee is brewed each morning, with dark and light roast, but no decaf. Coffee creamer pumps are freshly set up in regular and vanilla flavors. Hot water is ready with an assortment of teabags, sugar packets, sweet & low, and Equal. There is no protein in this breakfast. 

If not for the friendly, helpful staff, I would have given the Extended Stay America only 2 stars. But that, along with the acceptance of pets (for an additional fee) merits a 3 star rating.

text:
This used to be one of my all time favorite Mod-Thai ("Modern Thai") restaurants: no longer.  They went through some serious remodeling a few years back, and apparently, a change in ownership (or possibly management) as well.

Gone are the gorgeous "traditional asian" (floor sitting booths) dining facilities that made me bring in dozens of groups.  Gone are the comfortable tables.  Gone is the relaxed atmosphere.  All of this is secondary, and would not normally be part of a review for me, but it was at least part of what made TK&I special.  In place of an actual dining area, they now have TELEVISIONS running! Really??? TVs!?!?!?

As for the food: They've gone from 5 stars, all the time, no exceptions, to 3 stars AT BEST.  Dishes that were to die for (ex: Red Duck Curry, the now missing seafood dishes), are mere shadows of their former selves.  My "duck curry" had only a few small shavings of duck, in a decent but not exceptional red curry.  The scallops they used to use in their seafood went from full sized 1.5" to the tiny ones you expect in a Dennys.  Very sad.  Oh, and the portion sizes are down to roughly half what they used to sell, and the price is roughly 20% higher.  We spent (without alcohol) about 125$ on three people, and had only tiny take home leftovers. Partly from drastically reduced portion sizes, and partly due to their service staff ignoring our requests: see below...

Service: WOW! Their service has changed *DRAMATICALLY*!!!  They are cold, un-attentive, and you are completely ignored once they have brought out your entrees! We had to ask for desert menus.  Even worse, while there wasn't a ton of leftovers, roughly 1/2 of everything we ordered was still on the plate (mostly we just weren't that impressed with the food, and left it).  We specifically asked for EVERYTHING to go, and even offered to package it up ourselves (as they used to do no matter what).  Almost all of the tleft overs were discarded. If the left overs exceeded the single plastic tub and single cardboard containers that everyone got, it was simply tossed.  Three separate orders of rice (paid for, and specifically asked for to go) was gone.  Most of my wife's seafood dish was simply gone.  The left over apps were - amazingly - tossed thoughtlessly on the entrees, all to be mixed together in transit home: they CLEARLY do not care.

I have not been so sad at what has become of a good restaurant like this in many years.  We've gone from eating there three times a month 9at $100-$200 a pop, sans alcohol and tips), to "Will Never, EVER, return.  YMMV.

The food is passable, the service is tolerable, and the atmosphere is now loud, cold, and hurried, but if it's someone else's money and you just can't bring yourself to eat Thai at one of the (now) better places in the Loop, I suppose it's OK.  But you'll never see any of the three people we had tonight back there, EVER.

text:
I dont understand the rave reviews. The only thing above average here was the service and nice people working there. 

Ambiance: this is where this restaurant really shines. This place is impressive on the inside, warm, charming, romantic, inviting, and very well done. 

Food: We started with the fried chicken wings. They were certainly good, but I've had better. Somewhat forgettable. Just ordinary breaded wings to me. The sour cream and onion sauce was way too mayo-y to me as well. 

Then, we moved on to share several dinner entree items:
 - Steak and Fries: a very nice quality skirt steak and decent fries. Steak was under-salted and therefore a bit bland but easily remedied. Their signature ketchup was very good too.
 - Octopus: very, very good, tender, and nice flavor kick from the kalamata olives. 
 - Wild Boar Ribs: biggest disappointment. Did not remotely approach your standard baby back ribs flavor, richness, and tenderness. These were somewhat chewy, dry, and the bbq sauce is just all wrong. The jalapeño corn bread was good though. 
 - Hamburger: very good, though relatively small for a double patty burger. Anyhow, clearly one of their fortes. 
 - Mac & Cheese: more like Mac & Cream Sauce. Meh. Was decent, I've had much, much better.
 - Baked Beans: Tasted fresh, firm, and nicely balanced sweet sauce with savory bacon. 
 - Sautéed Greens: I think this had bok choy mostly. It was clearly sautéed in butter and garlic, leaving it tasty if not too greasy from the butter. 
 - Baked Cookie dessert: what a missed opportunity. This could have been the start of the night, instead tasting like a reheated, stale old cookie with the inexcusably tiniest scoop of ice-cream ever.  Should have been more chocolaty, more tender, of ooey gooey goodness!

Summary: 
At the prices they charge, we expected more. Pretty good overall, not good enough at these prices.

text:
Visited this restaurant with three friends for the first time to take advantage of a Groupon coupon. Out of the 4 of us, one person hated it, one liked it and the other two thought it was "ok". None of us was blown away. Service was average.

We started out with caipirinhas. They were delicious and the limes were very fresh. It was the perfect start to the evening. We ordered a few appetizers - the empanadas de bife (beef empanadas) came in an order of 3 and were very bland. They were served with a "spicy" tomato sauce that was not very spicy or flavorful, although it tasted of plain fresh tomatoes. We had aipim frito, or fried yucca, which was also disappointingly bland and dry. 

Then the entrees came... Two of us ordered the National dish (Feijoada de Ogum) , which had been highly recommended and even posted in a local foodie site as one of the best comfort foods St. Louis has to offer. It was a very large portion - served in a large bowl, with a plate of rice, greens, oranges and farofa (a dry yucca flour). You are supposed to mix the large bowl contents (black bean stew with sausage and pork ribs) into the rice, greens and farofa mix. The oranges were dry and not very tasty. The mix tasted good and unique at first, but became boringly bland the more I ate. The pieces of pork rib (part of the bean, sausage and rib stew) were seared on the outside but very rare and bloody inside, making for a very unpleasant texture when mixed with the other parts of the stew. This was an ok meal, but the best I could say about the national dish is that it is "average" and too bland and boring to eat the whole thing. The other person that ordered it absolutely hated it.  Something tells me I should have tried something else from the menu despite the "national dish" label.

One of the people in our party ordered the bobo de camarao (jumbo shrimp in a creamy coconut and spicy yucca sauce). She really liked it, although was disappointed that the shrimp had tails and veins on them and after a while, she felt the sauce was also a bit boring to finish the whole dish. 

The last person in our party had beef kabobs. He said they were good, but that he's had much better elsewhere and, although the meat tasted fresh, it was underwhelming in terms of seasonings. It was served with rice and vegetables, which were reminiscent of side dishes in an old folks diner. 

Finally we ordered desserts. We tried all three desserts on the menu. The coconut bread pudding was by far the best of the three and probably the best overall dish of the night, with the flan coming in a close second.

We were quite surprised when we heard the server offer a nearby table some specials that were never offered to us, even though it was the same server who had taken care of us.  

Overall, the ambiance was very nice and the decor was great, but the 
food let us a bit underwhelmed despite having great expectations. The prices are reasonable ($6-8 for appetizers ; 18-23 for entrees) but for the averageness of our meal, the $35 groupon coupon was a very welcome discount.

 The venue itself deserves 3 stars, but it does need some updating.  The view from the lawn could be better, the screens on the outside of the venue could be bigger and sharper too...Ticket prices, fees, concession and parking costs, bundled with terrible traffic and parking bring this down to 2 stars.

It is an amphitheater with a HUGE lawn.  The venue holds 25000, the lawn about 18000...Seats undercover are TINY!  If you are a big person, forget about it unless you plan on standing.  Can't really spread your feet apart...

For whatever reason, this place seems to draw every idiot in the area.  I've never been to a show on the lawn without seeing someone puke, or a pile of puke, or someone peeing, or someone so wasted they can barely function.  Yes, it can happen anywhere, but I hardly see this at the Mann Center, which is about half the size and twice as nice...Why they sell high alcohol content beer is a mystery to me.  Really it's not, they must be making good money on it...I'd never offer Golden Monkey (almost 10% alcohol content) to the masses.  Just asking for trouble...And they get it here.  If you are underage you need to be careful, they have a bunch of alcohol enforcement agents patrolling the venue(Blue shirts and plainclothes).  If they catch you, that is the end of the concert for you...

Sold out shows are incredibly tough to navigate thru.  Traffic into and out of the venue tends to be TERRIBLE, especially if there is another event in Philly that night...Parking is a nightmare, altho you can find free parking if you are brave and patient.  The lots in the area charge 30-40 bucks.  There is a parking garage right next to the venue, but A) it was closed this past weekend for whatever reason. In the winter, and for some smaller shows, they close the lawn.  I've only been here once in the winter to see Tool.  It was a nice change with the doors closed, traffic wasn't as bad, nor the crowd.  

Concessions are very expensive, alcohol prices are basically highway robbery...Nico's pizza is OK, but the line is long and slow. Final issue with this venue, there isn't enough indoor space to hold all of the people on the lawn.  So when storms rolled thru, they had to cancel the show and told everyone on the lawn to seek shelter. text:
On a rare visit to downtown Sparks, glowing sign of newly opened Golden Rotisserie beckoned with the promise of marinated, spit-roasted meat. It's a counter service place with simple furnishings, but plenty of room for a family meal.

Despite having never visited their original Truckee location, I was immediately struck with deja vu. The menu is eerily similar to that of much-lauded T's Mesquite Rotisserie in Incline Village. When asked about that, the guy at the counter shrugged his shoulders, and said, "I don't know." Fair enough.

A large rotisserie dominates the small, open kitchen space, though it appears it's only loaded up with beef tri-tip, chicken, and pork shoulder in the morning, then "held hot" to be served as burritos, tacos, tostadas, quesadillas, and sandwiches. Or, you can order a quarter or half pound serving of meat with a choice of two sides: cucumber salad, black beans, spanish rice, potato salad, and coleslaw. Like I said, deja vu all over again.

The "daily special" trio of tacos al pastor ($7.50) was served in the traditional manner, a pair of small corn tortillas supporting a decent amount of meat, topped with plenty of fresh onion and cilantro. They were served with rice and beans, lime wedges, and a two ounce cup of salsa (choice of mild, medium, or hot).

The beans were a little soupy, but the slightly salty flavor was pretty good. The rice had plenty of lime and cilantro. Unfortunately, the telltale pineapple flavor of al pastor was completely absent, replaced by crunchy, charred, bitterness that even a healthy dose of medium salsa couldn't improve. I chose not to finish them.

My friend's chile relleno burrito ($8.50) was full of black beans, rice, guacamole, lettuce, and sour cream, with the stuffed mild pepper in the center. It was really tasty even before the addition of hot salsa, though strangely lacking in cheese. Further inspection showed a thin layer inside the pepper, so perhaps "stuffed" isn't the word.

Meat plates come with a choice of corn tortillas or a slab of garlic bread grilled with plenty of butter and garlic. The bread was a nice addition to a half-pound order of tri-tip ($11.50) with potato salad and beans. The sweet salad could do with more seasoning and less dressing, but the beef? Oh man. Marinated in a mixture of honey, soy, and lime, the large slices were tender, delicious, and surprisingly moist. It would definitely make a great steak sandwich, and was easily the high point of our visit.

Although a half pound plate of soy lime chicken ($9.50) may have been dynamite when it came off the spit, by dinner time it was a mushy, dry disappointment. The skin was still acceptably crispy, and the marinade flavor was pretty decent. Sure, the meat came easily off the bone, but the breast quarter was drier than a cheap,  frozen turkey left too long in the oven. The attached wing was essentially inedible jerky. The dark meat quarter fared better, but only just. The sides of nicely seasoned coleslaw and marinated salad of cucumber, carrot, and onion were pretty enjoyable. I'm tempted to see if the chicken is better at lunch, but I'd probably just give in to that drool-worthy tri-tip.

The Quiche Lorraine was the perfect slice with lots of bacon and swiss cheese and my daughter polished off her nearly her entire Sharazi salad leaving me just a couple of forkfuls to try. The hot Croissant with Ham and Swiss Cheese was delicious and the croissant was perfect; not greasy with just the right amount of butter for flavor. There was a ton of sliced sweet ham (honey baked???) and cheese. We also got a couple of desserts to go (Chocolate covered Strawberry, Chocolate Cupcake with Chocolate Icing and Chocolate Truffle Chocolate Covered Cake) that look absolutely delicious and we can't wait to dig in. 

They have one small table for two outside, but just down the block towards Lancaster Ave. is a large tent that allows outdoor seating for all of the N. Wayne Ave. restaurants in case the Elegance Cafe's only table is taken. The server behind the counter was very friendly and gave us a warm greeting and salutation after we received our order.

I would highly recommend the Elegance Cafe and we will be sure to visit again!

Feeling flush with success at finding good breakfast on Christmas day at nearby Hymies, the merry band of hungry people set off to experience breakfast at the 'other' Jewish deli in Bala - Murray's Delicatessen, just a1/2 block away, this time New Year's Day (it's a holiday theme).

Next time they should think about less meat (so jaws do not need to be unhinged to eat) and more flavor.  French toast was also just 'meh', not nearly the flavor you'd expect from challah bread.  Texas Tommy was not loved -bacon was in that chewy not really cooked state that only some love.  Fries were not battered but also lacked any kind of flavor.  If I had to put one word to the meal it would be "bland".   

Service was reasonably efficient and friendly, and the place was clean.  We may go back at some point but we were generally so not-impressed it wouldn't be an enthusiastic decision.  

One nice note - free parking behind the restaurant, accessed by an alley next to Aldair (next-door restaurant).

text:
Twighlight Zone alert! 
Just came back from this place. I was with a freind. He ate, I didn't eat. He said the food was "good" and I trust him. First noticed something was off when no utensils were brought to the table other than the spoon that came with his soup. I had to get up and grab a napkin for him off the bar. I did this in full view of the entire waitstaff and no one even noticed, let alone react in a service oriented way. Towards the end of the meal, the waiter asked if we'd like anything else... My freind was still hungry and ordered a bowl of red beans and rice.... I said "if he's ordering more, I'll just have a side of toast with some olive oil to snack on".

The waiter came back 5 minutes later and told me "I'm sorry but we don't have any olive oil"

He said this nicely but without a hint of awareness as to the extraordinary absurdity of this statement. I asked him bewilderedly "you don't have olive oil?" And he said, "Well sometimes we have it but we ran out"

 This is 4pm on a Friday before a busy weekend on Decatur street and this is an Italian restaurant that has allowed themselves to run out of, of all things....olive oil.

I said "um... Ok well how about any kind of oil? Canola maybe? Or margarine?" He said he would see what he could do.

He came back to the table with a bowl of red beans and rice with 2 pieces of toast on top and fully touching.  He placed the bowl in front of my freind and gave me a small dish and said "here's some scallion oil, is that ok?" And I accepted it . I didn't bother telling him but there certainly is no such thing as "Scallion Oil"... It was Canola oil with scallions in it and that was fine by me.

Here's the real mindfudge.. He asks me if I want a plate for my toast and points and the toast that is swimming on top of my freind's beans and rice..... Holy Cannoli! It took me more than a few seconds to process what he had said.... I said pointing to the bowl in front of my freind "Oh... that's MY toast?" 

He said "yes!.. Very cheerily too I must add as if there was nothing remotely wrong with the situation. I realized instantly that the gap between his reality and mine was so cavernously deep that any attitude or complaint I gave him would be utterly futile and just make us both vastly more uncomfortable than 2 pieces of toast ordered out of boredom was worth.

"Yes" I said "If that is my toast on top of his food, and I have no plate, I would like a plate for my toast"

He brought me a plate, I took the toast off my freind's bowl, we spoke no further on the subject and all was right with the world.

So....Alls I'm sayin' is.... I didn't really eat here but.... If you like olive oil, napkins and you prefer that the food you order come on it's own plate rather than stacked on top of other people food as if plates are a short-supply luxury, this Italian restaurant may not be for you.
