text:
I've been in the area a few times, but had not stopped in before.  This small coffee shop is tucked into a little neighborhood by Rolls-Royce which is cut off from downtown by all the road construction on Meridian Street, so I suggest approaching it from the south and finding some metered street parking out front or to the south of the building.  I didn't see any handicap accessibility ramps, so entrance is via some steep stairs up to the lobby of the cafe.

The cafe is just beyond the lobby at the entrance.  The left side is where the prep/order area is with some limited seating.  To the right side is more of a place to set up for chatting with friends or doing some work on your devices.  

If you want to place an order, you go down the middle and wait your turn at the counter.  There is a cooler of non-coffee drinks as well as a limited food selection.

I was there for the coffee and ended up getting mine to go.  I was fortunate that because I take my coffee as a simple black drip, I didn't have to wait for all the specialty drinks ahead of me.  Thanks!  They had a couple flavors of drip coffee to choose from and the barista let me know the characteristics of each so that I could get the one best fitted to my tastes.  

And the coffee, while still hot, was not scalding.  I was able to drink it right away though I was careful not to take big gulps at first.  I really appreciate when a coffee house gets the temperature right.

I think if I had wanted to stay awhile and set up a workstation, I might have appreciated this place more.  As it was, making a special stop, paying the meter, and then climbing stairs to get into the place seemed like a lot to expect for a cup of black coffee.  So, go with an intention of staying if you want to get your money's worth from the visit.

text:
After an hour of comparing prospective birthday brunch venues, the photos, location, menu offering, and "wow" factor of Cinder House won me over, so I booked a Sunday morning reservation. Unfortunately, I'd asked them on Social Media where we could get the complimentary hot cocoa and never received a reply, but that's a thing if you're dining here, fyi. 

I also found out from a friend that Cinder House offers free valet if you're dining in their restaurant via the Four Seasons valet. 
This too would have been really useful to know prior since my friend and I walked in the frigid morning temps from our hotel all the way down there for our meal. 

Make no mistake, not only is this in the Four Seasons, it's also in possibly one of the best places to view the Arch and the Mississippi. As such, expect to pay premium prices for drinks and food. The food:

Buffett style usually isn't something I find exciting, as the visuals remind me of my subpar, pre-yelp days living in Lake Tahoe - dried out food, poor quality items to offset high waste, and overall just eating for volume to justify cost.  Cinder House reminded me really good buffets can exist, even in St. Louis. 
Arriving into the lobby, I immediately saw the few carving stations to the right, and was already happier than most of my buffet experiences. Three stations, all with minimal lines, awaited once greeting our friendly hostess. The first station had perfectly seared Ahi tuna, the second had smoked brisket and smoked pork shoulder, and the third was an omelet station with so many fixins! The meat stations both had about five sauces, mostly mexican inspired. I tried the blended green sauce and a green salsa with my tuna, which was really yummy.

For a brunch menu, I was disappointed to see half of the entire offering was baked goods/pastries, but most of them were beautiful and delicious. We found out the dishes rotate every week, according to our server, which means each time you go, it's like a new experience. From the baked goods row, I tried the pumpkin bread, chocolate pot du creme, pomegranate topped torte, a croissant, and ginger carrot cake. Surprisingly, the carrot cake was the star. The sponge was light and fluffy but spicy, and the frosting was a not too sweet cream cheese, topped with a beautiful slice of candied orange. 

Opposite to the row of baked treats were some al fresca options including smoked salmon and cream cheese, along with deviled eggs, grilled veggies, and a few salads. I was surprised to love the shaved cabbage caesar as much as I did, I highly recommend it if you enjoy dressing-heavy salads.

Being this was my only meal for the day, I went back for seconds of meat, and by my estimate, I probably had around $100 of ahi tuna alone, which wasn't my goal, but it was just so darn good. 

The fixed price brunch also included two drink tokens each, or they can be used for freshly pressed juices and smoothies, but we started with a bloody mary, then a glass of champagne. The bloody mary was decent, but nothing impressive. I don't need 87 things in my bloody but something more than a piece of celery would have been good, along with a little more spice, but it did the job. 

For my birthday, our server brought us a delicious "Happy Birthday" flan from a well-known chef, but I couldn't remember who. I just remember how balanced and silky it was, even after eating way more than I should have.

Overall, we were pretty happy for the location, the experience, the service (day of, not prior since they didn't respond to my questions) and the meats on offer.  I'd wish there was greater variety and selection of non-baked/sugary items, such as swapping some of the baked items for a few quiches or frittatas, but I understand they may not keep as well. 

While a little pricier than I'd expect to pay for a nice buffet, for an occasion or event, this would be a fun place to bring family or friends again. I hope they have that Ahi when I return!

Feeling 3.5 on this one - I'll explain why I went with 3 stars in a minute. The food is good, but there were some weird experiences and I think the prices are ridiculous. 

Had no clue what to expect with the atmosphere but I was pleasantly surprised. The service was pretty fast and friendly, especially when it was busy before the Pacers game we were wanting to get to. 

The table side guacamole is as good as everyone says it is - and in my opinion, truly a must order. The chips they serve with it are delicious as well.

I was shocked at the prices of the entrees. We decided to split the vegetarian enchiladas and I LOVED them. The butternut squash, beans, mushrooms and of course, the sour cream, all worked really well together. The tortillas were great and unique tasting as well. 

Still, I don't think the quality justifies the prices. $8.95 for the guacamole seems a little extreme. $16.95 for the enchiladas (we were splitting so they gave us an even four) without rice or you could argue, that many beans? Hmm..

The margarita was good (kind of small if I'm being honest actually), but again, the pricing. 

I get they're really the only Mexican downtown, so they have a monopoly and can charge whatever they want. 

But I felt that one margarita, an appetizer of tableside guac and one entree of enchiladas should not have been $40. 

Also, the bussers were obsessed (legitimately, obsessed) with clearing things off our table. I still had several sips of my margarita left when one tried to grab my glass. Excuse me? I'll take that back please. The same thing happened with the guacamole and the plate that I ate my enchiladas on. It was weird. They weren't at capacity so I guess they just really wanted us to hurry up and leave.

Overall, glad I came here to try it out but I probably don't need to go back.

Sorry, I was excited to have dinner here. For the price, the quality of each part of the meal, there is just no real value. If you want to experience Hot Pot, and do not want to pay 25 bucks to park in Philadelphia, then sure by going to Ten Hot Pot you will, "kind of" experience Hot Pot BUT BUT, Ten Hot does not remotely come close to being a "Great" or even "very Good" Hot Pot. So, I won't waste your time describing each and everything, like the rest of Yelp and the like...

We were greeted and seated immediately. There were only a few tables taken. The Hostess was extraordinarily attentive and sincere.

Ordered two Broths, Tom Yum and Mushroom 
Tom Yum - Close to Flavorless. Not bad, because the lack of Flavor creates an opinion that is neither good nor memorable.
Mushroom - This was Flavorless.

The server brought over some Kimshi, Seaweed Salad, Spicy Bean Sprouts, And I think Marinated Tofo. 

Ingredients - Fatty Angus Beef, In-House Crispy Meat, Squid, Mussels, Chicken, Black Fungus, Enoki Mushrooms, Pig Throat, Boneless Duck Feet, Fried Tofo Skin, Fried Pig Skin

Sauce Bar - Was totally lacking any sort of creativity. This reminds me of the Americanization of so many potentially superb eating experiences if ONLY the restaurant served what the culture of the restaurant truly represents and not AMERICANIZE the menu. Give us the ability to experience an Authentic Food experience from cultures most Americans may not be aware of. No one goes to a Jewish Deli and orders Spaghetti and Meatballs.  We order Chicken Soup and amazing Corn Beef Specials. Unless you're in a big city,  you will not find Authentic in the Burbs. A restaurant which offers their cooking heritage to the public seems to think people will not pay for the authentic fare. WRONG! The sauce bar was at the best, MEH. 

An opinion of the ingredients;
Fatty Angus Beef - Good. But then again at Hot Pot the meats are sliced very very thin. So, by cutting the meats so thin, most just melts in the broth. 10 Seconds is all you need to cook the beef.
Squid- Good
Crispy Meat - Umm, no no. We think it was chicken and no crisp to it.
Mussels - Good
Chicken - Meh
Black Fungus - Server never brought it to the table?
Enoki Mushrooms - Good
Pig Throat - No no - 
Boneless Duck Feet - When cooked longer, the experience was better
Tofo Skin - Meh
Pig Skin - was soft and not crispy at all 

The sauces are supposed to make the hot Pot Experience amazing, Because of the choices on the Sauce Bar, this was a swing and a miss. Maybe paying 25 bucks to park in Philadelphia would have been a better choice! No value per price point.

We were in Nashville for our anniversary and made reservations at STK for our anniversary dinner. It was such an amazing experience! My husband loves steak and their menu looked like it had good non-steak options for someone like me who only wants a bite of steak from my husbands plate, so we made a reservation through OpenTable. For some reason, they had us wait for 10-15 minutes before they seated us - even though we made a reservation and the location was not really that packed, and the crowd ebbed and flowed throughout the night. 

They started us out with some bread with garlic butter on top which was pretty yummy, although the bread was a little dry for my liking. We started with the "lil brgs" which were wagyu beef sliders. YUM!!! so delicious and such a great way to start the food for the evening. For dinner, I ordered the mushroom and truffle tagliatelle which was very creamy and flavorful, and my husband ordered a steak (I can't remember which one it was, but the flavor was *chef's kiss* - so good, and done just the way he likes it, medium well. We really enjoyed our meal and the ambiance, except for when they started playing very loud music and gave out shots to everyone - I'm guessing to hype up the people in the restaurant and get them to order more drinks. We don't drink - so it was pretty awkward for us to be handed shot glasses. We ordered dessert after that awkward moment and appreciated the little "happy anniversary" chocolate they added along with the sparkler - the bag o' donuts with the different sauces was really good. 

Our server was INCREDIBLE - so friendly, and went out of his way to make conversation with us as well as answering all the questions we had about the menu throughout the night. 

The food and service were top-notch, even if the ambiance was a little awkward at some points. I'd definitely go back and try another STK location based purely on the great food and experience we had here!

text:
My husband and I dined here last night for his bday and I really don't get what all the hype is about. 
We started with a bottle of the Macedonian red wine, $40/bottle, which was just ok, we typically go for a Zin, but at $60 we opted for the lower priced one. Very small wine list but who doesn't appreciate carefully selected wines, there was something for everyone's preference. From the small plates we I ordered the potted shrimps, which was about 2 tablespoons of chopped shrimp mixed in a mason jar with sown sort of foamy cream, served with what tasted like  higher end Chinese wonton. There were barely enough pieces of this toast to eat the 3 bites of dip and they took it away before we were done. 
Next came the squid and cauliflower..there was practically no squid I think we counted 5 mini pieces the size of an almond, but the cauliflower was very tasty, on what appeared to be a smear of squid ink, both roasted and raw/pickled pieces. 
Next came the jersey burrata, melted over a round slice of roasted squash with some pumpkin seeds. It was delicious and our favorite dish by far.  
For entrees we ordered the angry crab spaghetti and was so disappointed in that there was no crab! The flavor of the sauce was very nice, spicy with old bay, but all together there were literally 4 forkfuls of pasta and no crab you could spot without a magnifying lens, for $20 this was weak. I get that they make their own pasta, Im at avid at home cook and make both the hand rolled and with the kitchen aid types and there is no reason for the stingy portion, or change the price to $10.  Finally, out came the crispy rabbit, which looks delicious and smelled fabulous. We were surprised it was battered and fried, not what we expected from the crispy description, but our fault for not asking. There were 2 legs and breast cutlet and a couple of other fried nuggets of I couldn't tell you, maybe organ meat?  The portion looked like a very nice size, but then cutting into the leg we can to find that it was an insane amount of breading, very heavy and sat in our stomachs like a brick almost immediately. Accompanied by a habanero sauce and few pickled veggies-carrots, radishes, helped to break up the heaviness of the dish but still didn't save it. 
Overall we would not come here again, and now I'm searching for another restaurant to redeem myself for completely missing the mark for my husbands birthday dinner. Living in philly for a 2 year period we have been on a mission to try every top rated spot and high street epically failed for us.. For $170 with tip we left feeling very ripped off.  Oh and the waitress was nice, service was good, atmosphere was welcoming and the open kitchen definitely made you feel like it was a personalized dining experience . 
Fork though, next door same owner is really great and would recommend it over High street any day.

text:
After a horrible meal at Continental Midtown last year, I wrote a complaint  and received a $150 "gift letter" which I could redeem at ANY Starr restaurant in the city.  I decided it would be a good time to try Barclay Prime since I had  been yearning to try it since its inception. I took my mother with me as a belated mother's day gift and the restaurant was everything I expected (I had high expectations for this place and it met every one of them).

The service:
Everyone from the hostess to the bus boys were welcoming and courteous and didn't have the stuck-up attitude that some other high-end restaurants can have.  Our server, Nicole, was a doll and was prepared for every question I had to ask her.  I really appreciated the fact that nobody rushed me through my meal and the next course didn't come out until they were sure we were completely finished with what we had on the table.  The manager also came to our table to make sure everything was okay.

For dinner we had:
1. Popovers with sea-salted butter- these are given to you after your orders are in and they are delectable.  I need to get a recipe for something like this.

2. Kobe Sliders-these bite-sized burgers practically melted in my mouth.  I was sad I had to share them lol
3. Wedge Salad-I loved the twist on this salad; instead of bacon they use crab meat and the blue cheese crumbles were really soft and of high quality
4. Chopped salad-very good
5. Lobster Bisque soup-YUCK.  This was the only thing I didn't like.  Aside from the fact that the caviar gave it a taste of "fishy", without it, the soup would have been really bland.
6. Aged NY Strip-EXCELLENT-BEST STEAK I have had in PHILADELPHIA (Del Frisco's in NYC may have been better but I really think its a tie)
7. Jumbo Lump Crab Cake- Loved it, but Devon's still takes the cake in my book.
8. Truffle Mac and Cheese-Good
9. Potatoes Au Gratin-DELICIOUS
10. Asparagus- A little too salty, but perfect consistency.

All of the food above was enough for 4 people.  Lucky for my husband, he got a really good doggy bag.  

For dessert we ordered a banana cake with banana caramel ice cream and caramelized banana-balls and we all really enjoyed it.  

All in all probably the best steak in Philly.

text:
Manna is a kind of a strange establishment.  It is tucked away in an odd location off Charlotte right downtown.  One of those locations that you can drive past dozens of times without even realizing that there is a business there.  Most of the times I have gone the place has been virtually empty.  Yet somehow they manage to survive and pump out some pretty quality Korean food.  I attribute a great deal of Manna's quality to sharing space with the Market next door.  The food always seems like it is made with quality ingredients which makes sense when everything is only five feet away.  

The food is very good and really has a homemade quality to it.  Makes sense as it seems to be a family run establishment and the back dining room seems to be equal part restaurant and living room for the staff. As one might expect from a family run place the service is interesting.  Typically there is only one staff member at the front of the house with a limited grasp of English, but they are attentive and helpful if you flag them down.  Me and my family have always been warmly welcomed and treated very well.  

As to the food, In my experiences the bulgogi and bibimbap are far superior to a much more lauded spot on the west side (name omitted to protect the innocent) and the side dishes are exceptional. It featured very tender and flavorful beef and fresh broccoli in a slightly sweet sauce.   I liked that they had brown rice as an alternative to white to accompany the entrees. 

The portions were perfect for lunch; I was satisfied, but not stuffed and was not carting leftovers back to the office.    

The service was very good; we had no trouble getting our food, eating without rushing, and paying the check within an hour total.   

I definitely am planning to come back to try some other menu items!

Oh, and the staff are all revenants summoned from their eternal sleep by the chef-necromancer Bobby Flay. They are dead inside, mumbling your order back to you like ghosts to insipid families in their beloved houses.

Bourbon + Vanilla Ice Cream+ Caramel Sauce = Bliss. 

But you can make this with a visit to the State Store, Aldi (Whole Foods if you're Bougie) and to your own Kitchen's Blender. 

Go if you have the munchies.

text:
My second day in Philly, the last before ENDO2012 would begin, started the same as most - a long run inclusive of a Stallone style jog up the stairs of the art museum - and after a shower I hopped in the car en route for a place I'd only heard about the day prior from a gentleman in the Italian Market, a place called Stock's Bakery up in Kensington that apparently served a legendary poundcake.  Wondering exactly how good a cake generally made without much more than butter, sugar, and eggs could be as good as the fellow raved I decided to find out for myself and warned that they only sold whole cakes by weight I was additionally glad to know that I'd have friends in town both that evening and the day following with whom I could share.

Guided by GPS and making my way through the streets in good time I arrived at the small bakery just after 7:00am and with street parking just steps away I entered to a nodded greeting by the lady behind the counter and proceeded to browse my options, eventually settling on three choices - one warm and two already packaged and ready to go.  Not particularly a welcoming place I paid in cash and thanked the clerk who I'm rather certain never said more to me than the total cost and 'have a nice day.'

Making my way to the street and quickly unbagging my first choice I started with a warm yeasty donut coated in granulated sugar and although some may fancy glazed or powdered, I personally enjoyed the texture while the dough itself was light and wispy - a good start.  Moving next to a large pan weighing in at what I estimate to be about 18oz, my second selection would also prove to still be warm and while the pound cake may get all the press I'll tell you right now that the Butter Cake is severely underrated - a slightly salty yet entirely sweet butter and cream cheese pudding resting atop golden vanilla cake.  Dense at the top yet flaky at the base and only $3 for a whole tray there was more than enough here to feed four - something I had to be wary of given the day's eating plans as I limited myself to only 1/3 of the tray, the rest given to Ray later that evening to take home to his family.

Moving last to the famous pound cake, mine with a slick vanilla frosting, I'll just come out and admit that although my sample size is small it is without a doubt the best I've ever tasted - the crumb dense, the flavors that of pure butter, flour, and salty vanilla beneath a mountain of sweet...a science experiment in super-saturation where even the smallest loaf on the rack weighed in at 3lbs.  Like the butter cake but with more heft and a higher price this is without a doubt something to be shared, or at the very least savored over the course of a few days - or a week.  Not friendly at all but delicious and a downright bargain I'd definitely go back and recommend anyone visiting Philadelphia with a car to check it out.

text:
Visited Frenchman on a Saturday and we came here because there was no cover and saw that there'd be live music in a few minutes at 7 and DJ spinning "japanese electronica" at 10.  

You probably won't find many places like this in N.O..  Me and my gal had already had dinner and were looking to drink.  They have a decent list of sakes and other japanese drinks and beers.  They also have tapas style food served on small plates, but like I said, we weren't hungry.  

The drinks are pricey.  We finally decided on a $15 300ml bottle of sake.  Unfortunately, they were out.  We got a different bottle for the same price but which sounded less appetizing.  And it was.  Then we got another bottle of sake, this time the cheap carbonated one.  It was a 250ml bottle for $12 and tasted great but I was rather disheartened when I read that the alcoholic content was 7%.  

After that quick bottle I felt really sober.  And I was, we'd already dropped $30+ and weren't even buzzed.  I started buying $5 sapporo drafts (tied for cheapest drafts they have), which were good, but after I had three and she had two and somewhere along the way I'd broken down and ordered the "seasoned octopus with wasabi" (ugh, slimy canned octopus) we'd spent over $60 with tips and were just barely scraping a buzz along.  

There were a couple reasons why we stayed there for as long as we did.  One, there was a cool black and white japanese movie being played on the top corner of a brick wall.  Two, Fi Yi Yi, the drum circle band played most of the time that we were there, which was cool, but we really wanted to hear the DJ spin jap-electronica and dance but we ran out of funds and left.  Not sure if he ever showed up.

In a way, I feel like Yukis takes advantage of their uniqueness.  Sake isn't the cheapest way to drink, especially at a bar.  It's just like buying wine at bars and restaurants, and beer for that matter; obviously it's going to cost more.  Yuki's just didn't have any reasonably good sounding cheap options.  Except maybe the one they were out of.  And then their beer is expensive as well.  I just can't warrant that kind of expense for half of a mediocre buzz.  Maybe they think that because they have food they can charge restaurant prices for booze.  Or maybe that's just Frenchman St. for you.  I don't know yet, I'm new here.  

Left at midnight and went home feeling too sober and broke.  And my bum hurt because those red stools are uncomfortable.

Will I be back?  Probably, because I don't learn well from my mistakes.  That and I like sake and Japanese kietsch.  Next time I'll just make sure I'm drunk first.

Regarding the star rating, it's tough because there were two things that were terribly wrong with our meals at our visit to Bardenay, but everything else was just fine.
Maybe not "fine." The service was lacking. We had a seat on the nice patio during the end of the lunch hour, and everything moved particularly slowly. The patio was almost full, but the inside was nearly empty, so there wasn't much of an excuse there.
And the niceties of the patio and this restaurant's immaculate interior are really its saving grace. Being on Grove Street in the Basque Block with a nice building though, I don't think, warrants a positive review in itself. The food is really what makes an experience excel over a location, regardless of the latter being a plus or not.
The two things that went wrong with this meal were food-related. First, I got a chorizo sandwich with fries. The chorizo was not as good as what I had eaten at Bar Gernika the night before, but was certainly still pretty good and the bread was really nice. The fries, however, were off. When I asked, the server freely admitted that they were the frozen/Sysco variety. WTF? This is Idaho! Does any respectable restaurant really need to subject their customers to frozen french fries? And not only frozen fries, Sysco fries. I mean, I'm not looking for the Bittercreek Ale House standard of excellent housemade fries, I'm just looking for something that I can't buy in a big bag at the supermarket for $2. text:
I'm tough on Louisiana cuisine. The first cookbook I bought in the mid-1980s was by Cajun chef Alex Patout. The spine of Paul Prudhomme's Louisiana Kitchen is cracked from extensive use.

During a trip to New Orleans and Cajun country, I ate 11 bowls of gumbo in nine days, downed numerous poboys and other delights.

I was excited to see Jody Charles expand his pop-up festival and catering business and open Louisiana Soul Bayou at the Chow Public Market.

I ordered a bowl of chicken and sausage gumbo and a shrimp po-boy and fried okra.

An old Louisiana adage is that first you make a roux. The combination of equal parts flour and oil are typically cooked to a dark brown and then combined with the trinity of onions, bell peppers and celery. It adds depth to the flavor of a dish and acts as a thickener.

The gumbo at Louisiana Soul Bayou lacked that depth. The broth was watery and there was little flavor outside of the chicken and sausage. The vegetables didn't appear to have been sweated, so they didn't incorporate into the dish.

Cajun dishes don't have to be firery hot, but they must be flavorful and heavily seasoned. The gumbo lacked that kind of flavor. Judged against thosec11 bowls of gumbo I ate in Louisiana, all of which were great, this one fell far short.

It's unfair to judge a Louisiana po-boy against one made anywhere else. You can't get the special bread from John Gendusa Bakery or Leidenheimer Baking Co. anywhere else. A thin, crispy crust and pillowy goodness inside. A hoagie loaf just doesn't measure up.

If I hadn't been spoiled by the shrimp po-boys at Zimmer's Seafood next to Gendusa's in the Gentilly neighborhood of New Orleans or at Liuza's by the Track, then the Louisiana Soul Bayou one would have been fine. There wasn't any seasoning, so it was a little bland.

I love okra, but again their fried okra didn't appear to have been seasoned so it lacked flavor.

The staff was friendly and I hope Jody can tweak his recipes and come up with a winning concept that can thrive here.

text:
If I had to sum up Campo's with one word, it would be: Meh... Now, its not bad, and would be close to great in any other city. But in Philly, where there is an astonishing amount of fantastic sandwich places, average just won't cut it. and that's what Campo's is, average for Philadelphia.

The deli meat here is standard, but the sandwich selection is surprisingly good. I have had the roast pork here and it is juicy and the cheesesteaks will satisfy, but neither are something I would go out of my way to get. All is well until you realize how over priced your meal just was for what you got. Example: A Philly stable is sharp provolone. Now you go to a great deli like Sarcone's and there are small bricks of it lining your entire sandwich. But at Campo's? They charge you $1.50 to crumble some on top? REALLY?!?! I mean come on... I would also recommend the balsamic vinegar on any deli style sandwich, it is really tasty (but they are going to charge you a $1 for that too).

And while you are there, look around. I understand its the area, but 8 out of 10 are tourists. There is a reason, because locals aren't traveling out of their way to go here. Another crime is to call this place a "cheessesteak place." This is not a "cheesesteak place" no matter how hard the purveyors of this establishment try to market themselves. This is a deli that serves cheesesteaks. If you are looking for a real cheesesteak experience, I recommend you go elsewhere. If you are hungry and in the area, then stop in, you could certainly do worse. As far as the rudeness, you will find that at most Philly lunch spots. People in this city are bitter, being bitter is a way of life here, its part of the experience.

Jumbo Lump Crab Deviled Eggs

Brussels Sprouts with Garlic Aioli and Grated Parmesan.

The Brussels sprouts are cooked exceptional well, which is rare. This is ruined, by the lack of salt and seasoning again. I assume this is due to the amount of Parmesan shaved on top of the dish. After about 10 bites, you begin to realize how white you are because you are essentially eating cheese and mayo.

Ratatouille with filet

No salt on the filet on top. No salt in the dish itself. What is on the Filet is a lot of balsamic vinegar, which is overpowering. The tomato paste hasn't been stewed long enough, so the dish is really acidic especially with the amount of balsamic vinegar being used.

Service:

text:
I've given this place a try a handful of times. Unfortunately, my last visit will be my very last visit to this place. 

It's a place that is a quaint, family style restaurant. The food is served family style, as well, so it's great for groups. I actually think it's best to go in with a big group of friends. If not, you become stuck sharing food with a group of strangers. (If that's something that you're into, then you'd love that aspect of it.)

I don't eat meat. So the menu has very little in the way of options for food for me. So, the few things on the menu I can eat have always been mediocre... bland & flavorless. (Those aren't typically characteristics of Basque food flavor profiles so that's been confusing to me, all along.) So, my biggest complaint is that there aren't many options for me when I go in with friends. For a family style type of restaurant that caters to groups, that's a big downside, as I usually have to order alone rather than with the more fiscally responsible family meal deals.

I do acknowledge that this heavy focus on meat-based entrees could be a characteristic of Basque food. (Meaning, perhaps meat is a staple in the cuisine.) However, I've been to other Basque restaurants where the options for vegetarians were limited, but at least they were flavorful. Unfortunately, Louis' Basque Corner hasn't been able to execute that quality, successfully, during any of my visits. 

I do enjoy their Picon punch. (If you've never had it, it's an acquired taste.) Keep in mind, this is a very strong alcoholic drink, so be careful not to overdo it. :-) The table wine is fine, but underwhelming. 

The restaurant itself seems clean enough and the staff has always been cordial. However, the decor is a bit old fashioned. It reminds me of a diner type of atmosphere. That's always been one of the things that has turned me off from this restaurant. Don't get me wrong, I'm not a snob who doesn't 'do' divey restaurants. But, when the options for food I can order is so limited, I expect some type of upside.

So, it's a fine place for big groups of friends to gather. But, be sure those friends are meat eaters so that you can get your money's worth out of your meal. Unfortunately, this vegetarian won't be returning to this establishment.

I wish I had paid attention to all of these negative reviews before I brought my children to this dentist office. I am writing this review as a WARNING to other parents not to bring their children here. Dr. Solow seems like a knowledgeable enough dentist/orthodontist, but he moved forward on my child's orthodontic treatment without my consent while I was in the hallway getting a very confusing price estimate from his receptionist. This is a minor problem compared to the BULLYING, PHYSICALLY ABUSIVE behavior of his staff.

Two of Dr. Solow's hygienists mistreated my thirteen-year-old son in absolutely inexcusable ways. The first hygienist didn't communicate with him at all, and after fumbling with many failed attempts to put spacers between his teeth, she called for help from another hygienist  who was even more rude, unkind, and physically abusive. These two hygienists proceeded to gang up on him, talk about him as if he was not there, and  ignore him when he asked them to stop. My 15-year-old daughter had just had her teeth cleaned and was there to witness all of this. When she spoke up on behalf of her brother, asking them to listen to him while they had him pinned  down in the chair, she was told she had no right to tell them what to do. I can't believe I was on the other side of the door while all of this was happening. When I returned to the treatment area, I saw a look of rage in my son's eyes that I had never seen before. My daughter calmly explained to  me how the hygienists had mistreated her brother, while they both tried to cover it up saying they just wanted to "get the torture over with." Was this supposed to make me (or him) feel better?

When I got home, I called the office and talked directly with Dr. Solow. He apologized immediately and asked me to repeat what had happened so he could repeat it out loud so the people involved could hear what my complaint was. I'm a forgiving person and appreciate a genuine apology, but this seemed a bit contrived--or perhaps it's a common occurrence. He didn't seem shocked or appalled by what I said. 

I have taught my children to be respectful of all people. What we experienced at this dentist office was total disrespect. I'm so glad my daughter spoke up for her brother. But I feel terrible for entrusting my children to people who clearly don't understand the basic trust and respect that must exist between a healthcare provider and a patient. Just because they have murals on the walls and cartoons playing does not make them the "child friendly" practice as they claim to be.

In the future, I plan to bring my children to a very caring dentist  I recently saw in Havertown, Dr. Petras. This Drury-run hotel near the STL airport seems a real bargain compared to its nearby competitors. The free (full) breakfast of sausage, scrambled eggs, biscuits, yogurt, cereals, breads, jams is plenty to choose from and available for about 3.5 hours each morning.  Staff is friendly and helpful. While this (APPARENTLY) was not the fault of the hotel staff, and we also checked with the customer service people by phone, it seemed to me they should have found me a room somewhere. 

What happened? I got the PTI shuttle to my car rental, was getting my car (so i could drive partway to my destination & find lodging there), when PTI called the car rental agency to tell me "a cancellation has made a room available for you". OK. That was good that they tracked me down. However, somehow I got the feeling this was rather odd (at midnight), so still not sure how to rank the hotel on this.

There is free popcorn in the lobby, free food at happy hour, and lots of other amenities at the PTI. Airline staff stay there, so it must be dependable and clean.

text:
Great rustic shabby decor and lots of outside amenities (i.e.,weather permitting!).

Been twice but both times disappointed.  The first time we ordered calamari for an appetizer and it was average.  Hankering for shrimp & grits but thoroughly disappointed for $19.95!  It was very soupy so I did not see the tails left on the shrimp.  Very awkward eating and average taste.  Outrageously priced since it was mainly grits!  We also ordered a grouper sandwich and was disappointed in that.  It couldn't hold a candle to the grouper sandwich at Molly Goodhead's in Ozona.

Second time we went for lunch it was very cloudy but our friends wanted to eat outside on the deck.  We were only seated a few minutes before it started to sprinkle and we were getting wet and then it started to pour.  We picked up our silverware, drinks, etc. (awkward) and moved inside since the awnings that are over the deck are small and in sections with openings in between.  Fortunately, it was not crowded inside.  I am not sure what would happen to people out on the deck if  there was a cloudburst in the middle of their meal and it was full inside since the interior dining space is relatively small.  So little forethought given to the rainy season and providing a way to continue to dine on the deck in bad weather.  This is Florida with unpredictable weather but it seems that their focus is mainly on outside drinking & dining to the exclusion of weather conditions. 

Now to the food!  Our friends ordered "Joe's Pile of Nachos" and that has to be the most unappetizing appetizer that I have ever seen.  It looked like someone took all the scraps from the kitchen and piled it on a plate.  The longer it takes to eat, the soggier the nachos get.  Gross!
We ordered the "Coconut Mahi Nuggets" which didn't have any particular taste.  Ordered "Firecracker Shrimp Tacos" which was a soft taco shell overwhelmed with coleslaw and very few small shrimp making it soggy and it fell apart.  Would not recommend.

I played it safe and ordered the "White Sands" pizza which I enjoyed.  So out of all the things we have ordered, there is only this one thing that was good and reasonably priced. 

Parking situation is atrocious!  Pay for valet (very limited space) or park blocks away.  They do provide a golf cart shuttle from the remote parking.  Of course, the last time we were there for lunch valet parking was free with tip suggested.  $5.00 during dinner.

My kids only went to Kids R Kids for 4 months, during these 4 months my kids became pretty wild. They stopped listening, everything was a fight, we were late everyday - and yes I know, they are 1 and 3, but it was absolute complete chaos! It was outside of the norm of chaos. Kid R Kids has the Watch me Grow system, so I was able to watch my child during the day. Every day they have their learning activities and all the children will sit in a group on the carpet, instead of my child participating I would see my child be redirected to the classroom table practically every day, because they wouldn't just tell her to stop acting up, sit down and listen. Instead they would redirect her to the classroom table with a book (of course she is unable to read by herself because she is 3). So she wasn't able to participate in the learning activities. 

As we are working parents, this daycare center just wasn't working for us. So I pulled them out and moved them to another daycare center. I have waited a of couple months to write this review, but in the last two months my kids are doing so much better, they have respect for others again, they are listening, we are back to the normal chaos, and we are never late anymore. After the first 3 weeks my 3 year old was at their new daycare, she even said to me 'Mommy they don't sit me down to read books by myself anymore' - SERIOUSLY I could not even believe that she said that to me! It breaks my heart the way they are doing business at this daycare center. Kids R Kids is a place where they are just running a business, I don't feel that they actually give individual nurturing attention to the kids that are there. 

A few additional things that I didn't like... 
1. About 90% of the time I walked in to pick up my kids the reception people would never make eye contact. 
2. They always forgot I had two kids, and they could never remember who my kids were when I asked them questions. I'm sorry, when I am paying you $400 a week, I feel that you should at least know who my kids are.

4. 5. My kids got Hand, Foot and Mouth... I know this can go through all daycares, but... it is weird that I was warned about it from a friend before my kids attended Kids R Kids. 

I do not recommend this daycare to anyone. I went and checked out a pre-school for my 3 year old and they were more personable within the 20 minutes I was there taking a tour than Kids R Kids ever was in the 4 months my kids attended. In 4 months we just had way many problems.

Overall, I give the three stars because their is some stiff competition right in the vicinity and because the ambiance is nothing to write home about. text:
I absolutely LOOOVE this place!! Yes, it's true that Franklin Fountain is a go-to tourist dessert shop in Philadelphia, but for good reason. The ice cream flavors are unique and the employees are so nice, helpful, and accommodating. Even the layout and ambiance of the shop is unique, cute, and fits right into the Old City vibe. Their flavors are perfect for any type of sweet tooth here - so many flavors ranging from classic and traditional to unique and different. The location is also very convenient since it's right next to the 2nd street stop on the SEPTA blue line and is right off of Penn's Landing. 

Now to talk about the flavors. The Green Tea and the Black Raspberry are my absolute FAVORITE. I've never had better or creamier ice cream before, and all of the flavors that I've tried are just so deliciously rich and satisfying. My sister, who absolutely adores ice cream, really recommends the Hydrox Cookie (basically Franklin Fountain's take on cookies and cream ice cream) and the Peach ice cream.

There is also quite a wide selection of sundaes for those ice cream maniacs. The sundaes and specialty orders are quite expensive - more than $10 a pop - but they are definitely something special. I've tried the Mt. Vesuvius sundae, which is an absolute treat for chocolate lovers. It's quite an extravagant mix of ice cream, brownies, hot fudge, and whipped cream. Though I would highly recommend sharing this sundae since it's huge, I thought it was one of the best desserts I've ever had.

So my one main complaint really has to do with the price. Though the servings are large, I still would prefer not to pay over $5 for a small cup of ice cream or over $10 (the price of a meal!) for a sundae. If the prices were a little more reasonable, I would definitely try to stop by for ice cream a little more often.

I take all of my visiting friends and family here, and I haven't heard anything but good feedback from everyone. You can't go wrong with Franklin Fountain ice cream!

text:
I have eaten at Longhorn just about every Sunday for the past decade.  We are guaranteed a table and a good steak dinner every single time.  Sadly, I am writing this review during the ONE time we did not have a great experience, so I am knocking off a star.  

We always get the same thing.  I had the caesar salad, he has the house salad.  I have the New York strip.  He gets the filet.  I get steamed broccoli, he gets a baked potato.  We both always agree on the stuffed mushrooms for an appetizer because they are so incredibly good.  Also, we usually down a loaf of their steaming hot bread before the salad even arrives.

Once in awhile, we will take out our LH dinner.  Eat it at home instead.  We do this a bit more often during football season, because we cheer kind of loudly and we don't want to be obnoxious in the restaurant.  The bar seating is usually full during football season so we don't want to eat there.  

Last night, hubby brought home all of the aforementioned food.  We live 20 minutes away, but the food always arrives home still hot.  Not last night. Last night EVERYTHING was ice cold and the salads were luke warm.  Not only that, but the steaks were not medium rare like we ordered but more like medium RAW.  They were still mooing.  When we cut into it, it was like someone cut the cows femoral artery and blood spurted all over our plates.  No lie.  The blood got all over my broccoli.  My husband actually had to fire up the grill to re-cook our "cooked" steaks.  I had to reheat all the veggies in the microwave.  The bread had cooled by then, was no longer hot or even warm by then.  I wasn't really in the mood to have to turn on my oven as well to reheat that.  I have been sick for quite awhile now and my husband was trying to do a nice thing for dinner to give me a break.  I could have cooked everything myself and gotten a better result.  Meh.

So, after everything was reheated and what not, I tweeted Longhorn, showing them the bloody mess they sent us home with.  No answer.  Retweeted.  No reply.  So, we just called the manager at our Longhorn. John was very courteous, offered to remake our steaks, but we had just done that ourselves, so that was kind of pointless.  Plus, we're 20 minutes away and by the time we were done, it was nearly 9:30 pm and no one was in the mood to go out (and hello?  The Giants were playing.  Duh!)  So, he took my husband's email address and our home address and said he was sending something out to us.  If it isn't a damn steak dinner, I don't want it.  Two, as a matter of fact.  I offered to send him photos I took of the bleeding massacre, but even he didn't want it.  Can't blame him.  I'm a surgical nurse and even I don't want to see that much blood, let alone put it in my mouth.  (Although being a sparkling vampire would be kinda cool.)

Anyway, I have to yank a half star on that because consistency is key in the restaurant biz.  I am yanking another half star because from time to time, we have had servers who were kind of on the bitchy side, which I generally don't care about most of the time; I would just reflect that in their tip if I was that upset with them.  However, there have been a few times that it was a little over the top.  Then again, if that's all I can complain about in 10 or more years, that's really not a bad thing.  Most of the time, the culprit is usually gone by the time we go back.  And one takeout faux pas is really not enough to whine about.  

By the way, Longhorn Corporate? Whoever runs your Twitter can kiss my bloody cow steak.  They finally got back to me almost 24 hours later. In social media time, that was like...ten years.  I already spoke to the manager about it and he handled it just fine.  Your social media person is awful.  Just saying.

If we get something awesome in the mail, I will update this review.  If I get a $5 gift card, I am yanking ALL THE STARS and replacing it with a bloody cow.

text:
Love this store! If you need or are looking for any decor items, speciality gifts, local items (including sweets!) and/or an assortment of older or antique items or furniture, this is your place. There's even a small cooler with unique drinks in the corner. 

I started following the shop on Instagram ages ago. So I was thrilled that they are close to my relocated area. The first time I was in the shop was honestly to only grab flowers to brighten a friend's day. Yet, I ended up walking out with an assortment of things - ribbon tape, soap, some candles, hand cream, Edmonton trivia cards, etc. Small but unique or local items always makes good gifts! I love so many things in this store and recommend this place if it's gift giving items you're looking for or even the extra self love/care items. I've shopped here for gifts that I felt I could further customize for friends and family or add to a group gift to enhance the selected theme. 

The staff is always very helpful when they see me looking at the displays or carrying multiple items (I walk with a cane so I appreciate their concern of I can hold onto something for a time). I've even suggested this place to others to stop at when they come to Edmonton as it's a very pretty store just to pop into quickly for future inspiration.

Most recently I've bought myself bouquet filter to fix my seasonal bouquet (sadly the seasonal element to a Christmas bouquet was severely lacking from a different store - people let this be a lesson on you get what you pay for). The ladies suggested some items I wouldn't of even thought to consider or ask for. Some really cool red berry looking thing too. Happily I can report that adding those suggestions plus what I wanted together with the flowers I already had resulted in an amazing amount of virtual complements during the holiday. Plus I got what I really was looking for - that real tree smell in my little apartment! I recently had to reduce the filler in my vase to only the pine. So I can confirm their product lasts a good amount of time or longer than expected. I've brought multiple bouquets and floral items from them in the last couple of years and everyone I've gifted a bouquet has said the same thing.

If I could give a 4.5 I would as seriously this place. It truly is a great as a store and the shop for the most part is arranged to give a lots of space to move around. This was before only a few people were allowed in at a time (covid restrictions). They even have the most lovely shop dog. Hand sani out at the front and easy to read signs.

It's honestly the parking lot that makes it go down a point. As someone that is mobility limited, I don't enjoy the real life game of frogger. Especially in winter amongst cars entering quickly off  the corner of Whyte ave and 96 St into the uniquely shaped and noticeably slopped parking lot. To make things really challenging for drivers (and shoppers trying to get to and from cars), there's one access point parking lot. Lots of times you see people backing up further into the lot or back on the street to get another car out or into the parking lot. So drive with caution, especially when reversing.

Yes, there's a handicap stall and a few other spots near the door but that's usually the first to be taken. Especially if it's a long weekend. I don't mind trying to challenge myself from time to time with walking distances but it's the slope in the parking lot that personally makes me nervous in winter due to my lack of balance.

The unique parking situation is not the shop's fault. One assumes from the look of the building, the footprint is definitely from the older days. Do keep in mind if you choose to park there, that the lot is shared with Earth's General Store. As you can imagine, being connected to a small and unique grocery store creates a very busy parking lot with usually few people waiting to go inside (due to limited number of customers allowed at one time). So if you can bike, bus or walk over, I would recommend it. Bike rack is located along the dividing wall that leads to the sister store of Maven and Grace. Bus stop is literally as close as you can get for a bus stop on Whyte Ave. I have also noticed the last few months a lot of people parking in the Humpty's lot across the street or along the other side of Whyte Ave (so not to be in the bus zone) and walking over. 

All in all, the shop itself is awesome to find that perfect gift or brighten your own day with something a little special.

text:
A group of 10 looking for a restaurant week spot only a few weeks before it begins can be tough - so choosing Twenty Manning Grill really came down to the fact that they were willing to take us. They required a card on hold to make sure we showed up, but after reading the menu online it didn't take much convincing. 

We were seated at two long tables, and the waiters were fine with us getting up and moving around a bit.  It was much appreciated, as catching up with 9 other people can be tough.  Food all came out at the same time and the whole meal was coordinated well, which can be tough with such a large party. 

To start, I went with the crab cake.  From other reviews, I had fairly high expectations. Unfortunately it was a lot of filler and only a little crab, though the remoulade sauce it was served with was tasty.  My partner ordered the crispy phyllo shrimp, which was much better - if I go back, I'd get those as a bar snack. 

There was a surprise entree option on the RW menu, the sole fish tacos.  Being a sucker for fish tacos, I couldn't resist.  They came in a pair, and were stuffed with lettuce, fish, and other goodies.  I ditched the double tortilla, and appreciated the fresh lime slices and yummy sauce that were served with the tacos.  By the end of that, I was stuffed, but of course, then came dessert.

Twenty Manning Grill took my favorite approach for dessert - rather than making you choose one, they give you a trio of dessert samples.  Our consisted of a chocolate chip cookie, melty brownie, and passionfruit cheesecake, along with a bit of fruit.  All were delicious. 

Overall, this was a good option of RW, and I think I'd come back to sit at the bar and sample cocktails and snacks.

My father bought the beer battered fish. The moment he cut it open, the gray colored fish slid out of the crispy shell. He couldn't even eat it, it looked very unappetizing. 

My dad talked with the woman at the counter who seemed to be the owner and asked about the corned beef and where it came from. He was told they did it in house.  If this is what you think corned beef is, think again. 

Disappointed in the other menu items so if you go here, stick with the ribs or wings only.

text:
I'd agree with the sentiment from several of the previous reviews: I want to love this place, but they make it hard sometimes.  

Pros:
-Food is awesome.  I expected typical bar food, but it was actually quite impressive.  You can tell they've put some effort and thought into their menu and ingredients.  Farm burger is good, and their chips and queso are excellent!

-Sports/TVs.  For some, this could be a con, as the "sports bar" vibe is a little overwhelming.  I really enjoy that aspect, but it's not a place I would typically come with the old lady for a regular dinner, as it's pretty loud and obnoxious.  It's sort of a destination to watch games and that's about it.


Cons:
-Service/management is a joke.  As most reviews have indicated, the servers here are, for the most part, rude and inattentive.  When we came in the last time, we stood at the hostess' table for a LONG time before anyone finally acknowledged us.  Then our server was nowhere to be found, so another gentlemen finally came and offered to take our table (thank goodness, as he was fantastic...but he seems to be the only one).  

This is despite the fact that the owner was at his table nearby, more concerned with hanging out with his overgrown frat brothers than serving his customers, or expecting even a modicum of effort from his staff.  If you can imagine the most cliche stereotype of a "sports bar owner," that's this guy.  It's not necessarily a bad thing, as he is clearly doing well, but it's cringeworthy IMO. 

The kitchen (way) undercooked my burger.  It was so bad that the waiter apologized when he brought it out and said I'd likely need to send it back.  Can't help but wonder why not just make sure it was right before bringing it out?  At any rate, I did have to send it back, as it was practically raw.  1) they just put my patty back on the grill, which is borderline gross considering I had eaten from it...just eat the $2 and send out a new patty and 2) it would have been a nice gesture to comp the burger or offer a dessert...something for my trouble, since they knew it wasn't right to begin with and brought it out anyway.  That was the most troubling part.  Thankfully I sent it back, otherwise I would have gotten sick.  

-Prices.  He's sort of got the market cornered in this area, so his prices are on the high side, especially for beers ($6-$7 each adds up fast during a football game).  A full meal with an appetizer and drinks here cost us ~$80 for 2, which is pretty high considering that, when it comes down to it, you just had cheeseburgers and beer.

text:
I'm sure Dr. K is a knowledgeable veterinarian however lately I have seen a change in his care that appears to be influenced by how much money it will make him. I have a two year old cat that I took to Dr. K for over a year. I always thought my bill (which was never itemized) was a little pricey but figured that all vets were expensive. When my cat started developing bald spots from itching I took him in and Dr. K examined him for what felt like one minute, declared my cat had allergies and needed a hypoallergenic diet indefinitely. There was no discussion on alternative diagnoses like anxiety, seasonal allergies vs. food allergies, or fleas. 

Dr. K then said that the food can only be bought through his clinic and would be about $60/month. I had an older cat I brought to Dr. K years ago that he said also required special food but since she was already 13 I was more receptive that an old, sick cat might need special care for her last few months. But with a 2 year old cat I had a hard time facing years and years of expensive, prescription food. There was no discussion of steroid injections, topical creams, or any alternatives. Dr. K was insistent that food would be the only fix. Side note - the vet tech is amazing. Even though Dr. K brushed our questions off she was thorough and reassured us that if the food didn't work we could bring it back for a refund.


So we left with 2 bags of food and a $200 bill. I didn't start the food however because something didn't sit right. I ended up seeing a different vet in the KC area (I recently moved for school/work) and the experience was night and day. Long story short - a vet spent 45 minutes with my cat examining him and discussing at least 10 different treatment options before we decided that a steroid injection would be a good thing to try. My cat has since stopped itching, the hair is growing back, and it only cost $35 for the shot and $60 for the exam. Literally HALF the price of Forum plus no need to keep returning to purchase food every single month. 

I would strongly consider looking elsewhere so that you can be confident that the services you pay for are necessary. I have other stories I could share about Dr. K from my last cat, too. This is an ongoing problem and unfortunately it has taken me this long to figure it out. Save yourself the time and money and seek out another veterinarian.

text:
Slice & Soft Drink Review

Walked in to Yordana II tonight for a light bite and went with a slice of regular pizza that was sitting under glass. The place was empty but for me at 7:15. It had about a half dozen booths along the inside wall.  It was a clean house, with three guys in the kitchen. Everyone was polite. 

I asked that the reheat be "well done," to bring the wedge fully back to life. The young cashier took my $4 and handed me some change for the tip jar on the counter. I went to pour my drink and retreated to a booth to await my victuals. 

It arrived a few minutes later in the hands of the chef. It was a smallish slice, but I wasn't starving. My standard for good pizza wants the point to stand firm when picked up by the crust. It demonstrates a well baked and strong chassis upon which the rest of the vehicle is built. This one collapsed on elevation. The weight of the cheese and the trapped moisture in the underbaked bottom made for a soggy base. 

I folded it over longitudinally to hold it together, and a rivulet of oil rolled off onto the paper plate. Cheap cheese. When I could finally take the first bite, the triangle was hot enough to melt the surface and warm the undercarriage, but had not reached full reheat, let alone the heavier burn I requested. Also, the top was almost entirely cheese with a thin tasteless layer of sauce. Bad proportions. 

This was not a good pizza for me. Everyone has a different preference for their pie, but when requests are not honored, the problem goes deeper than lack of real experience with a classic American comfort food. It is about listening and translating that request into the desired product. This just wasn't done. 

Everything else on the menu may be great, but the pizza reheat was not.

text:
Okay, Yelpers, these reviews reeally let me down.  Being from California and having the same dentist nearly all my life, (I've seen two other dentists that have been fine) I had hoped this would be a one-stop shop after reading reviews, but nah.

My first visit was fine, a breeze even.  The front desk staff is friendly and pleasant, and the place is clean.  I was seen on time and felt okay about how things went.  I expressed my complaint as having pain on the lower right side.  Xrays showed that that tooth is growing in awkwardly, pushing against the tooth in front of it creating a pocket of sort. The doctor explained how pain works.  In a nutshell, he says the pain is likely coming from the top right side because there are two visible problem teeth--it simply FEELS like the bottom.  I confirm that I have had some "zings" of pain up there, but most of my pain is on the bottom. I remember specifically saying, "it's weird, it doesn't really feel like the pain associated with having a cavity."  It was easy to accept his theory on how pain worked because I knew with certainty it wasn't a cavity.  I'm prescribed antibiotics and schedule two extractions for a week later for the top right side, per his medical advice.   Upon taking the antibiotics, the pain never stops!  Mind you, this isn't my first extraction or infection, so when the pain is still pretty constant, I deduce that there is no infection. The way pain works is probably true, but not applicable.  It's the bottom right. Like I said initially. Still in full blown pain.   So I go back for the extractions and say I want to have the bottom right extracted instead because the antibiotics didn't work, pain still constant, yaddah yaddah yaddah. He pulls the xrays up again, reads the notes he wrote in my chart and insists we move forward with the two extractions he suggested.  This is where I take FULL RESPONSIBILITY for staying. At that point, I should've hightailed it outta there and gone for a second opinion. Instead, I laid back and settled in. :-(  Minus One Star for Lack of Attentiveness/Bullying

Here's where it gets sticky. I mean bloody. I mean, you get it.  I get numbed up with shots and ointment and Doctor Michael Leggio dives right in. The first extraction was a piece of cake. The tooth had fallen out some years back and only needed the remaining tooth to be removed and thoroughly cleaned out.  He wasn't the most gentle, but that's nothing I couldn't deal with.  Suddenly, painfully, I feel my lip being ripped/split open.  He was standing behind me, and I swear he had his hands all over my dang face.  My mouth obvi, was wide open, & having his hands positioned that way, caused a tiny, painful laceration from pulling at my teeth one way and my face the other. It hurt when it happened, I definitely felt every bit of the tear, but by the time I got home and started looking, I couldn't see or even feel it. I assumed it was so tiny that it had simply healed already. WRONG. Once the shots wore off, there it was.  You had better believe that thing got progressively worse living inside my wet, inner lip.  See photo for grossness. Minus One Star for Pain & Suffering Due to Face Damage.

On to the second tooth--the doozie apparently. Leggio is doing his job and the inevitable drool arises and starts to trickle.  It ran down my chin, down my neck, over my shoulder, and onto my back.  That's some rapid moving spit, isn't it? The RDA, Marsha is sitting there doing god knows what. Whatever it was, it must have been more important than chasing saliva. Nonetheless, I give her the benefit of the doubt--maybe this saliva is still clear and not bloodied? Perhaps that's why she hadn't noticed it? My mouth HAD to have been filled up with spit for it to eventually spill over, right?  Dah well, I'm numb, maybe not. So I struggle from underneath the bib thing & wipe it myself.  In fact, to my surprise, it's up to me to wipe my own drool for the duration of my visit. At this point, I'm absolutely flabbergasted. One, how in the hell is this woman still employed? Two, why in the hell wouldn't Leggio wake her a$$ up? (I shared this experience with my RDA niece and boy was she disgusted) Minus One Star for Negligence/Sleeping On the Job/Acting Like I Aint Sh!t

Now here I am, three weeks + hundreds of dollars later and what do ya know?   My gums surrounding that lower bottom right tooth are now INFLAMED, SWOLLEN, THROBBING & STILL IN PAIN. So swollen that it hits the top teeth when I chew. I've found myself literally holding my mouth slightly open--there's no such thing as having a comfortably closed mouth at this point. ugh.  Minus One Star for Time & Money Wasted + Problem Unresolved.

Final Answer:  I went in for a service, and that service was provided.  The experience, tho, was a nightmare.  Also note, if I wasn't such a team player, I would've had my phone out despite the signage and captured a dirty mouthwash cup. Another win for dear old Marsha. Stay away, guys.

Let's start with the highlights...

Food: this is where Edge really shines! They offer all your expected pub items but with an elevated flare, which I feel sets them apart from other brewpubs in town. I had the fried chicken sandwich which was hand breaded, tender, and crispy and served with a house made fry sauce concoction on a tender bun. The snake bites (fresh jalapeños stuffed with pork sausage and cheese and broiled instead of deep fried!) were delicious! Other selections include the scotch egg, a variety of burgers, fried pickles, and homemade mac and cheese with various fillings/toppings. In addition, everyone is offered a complimentary basket of house made BBQ chips, which is a great option especially if you are only interested in beer and just want something to snack on. Also, half price appetizers during happy hour. 

Beers: I am a craft brew geek and I will say that the beers at Edge are drinkable, but middle of the road and a bit non-memorable in comparison to other breweries in town. However, there is a large selection to choose from and they do offer flights if you are "beermiscuous" like me and enjoy sampling different styles!

Now for the low(er) points...

Location: off of Emerald near the DMV and surrounded by offices, warehouses, and call centers, so it's a bit off the beaten path (unless you work in the area and are looking for lunch options) and can easily be an after thought for me when considering, "Hey, where do I want to go tonight?" It just doesn't have that funky neighborhood feel I love in breweries, but I suppose they are just working with what they have. 

Service: friendly and attentive. However, the bar is directly across from the food window and service station and while seated there I've found myself during several occasions within earshot of server/kitchen staff personal conversations, the content of which wasn't always pleasant or appropriate (discussions of personal matters, baby daddy drama, relationship woes, bad mouthing customers, foul language, etc). I'm not a sensitive prude by any means (I even kind of chuckled to myself about some of the things I heard), and I worked in the service industry for several years so I know how things go, but it is a bit unpleasant to overhear these things on the customer end. It appears unprofessional, detracts from the experience, and isn't what I want to listen to while enjoying a meal and a beer.

Overall, I feel the food and beer at Edge is worth checking out if you are willing to sacrifice convenience of location, though I would recommend getting a table away from the bar unless of course you want to feel like you are part of the studio audience on "The Maury Show!"

My wife and I went to Marigold tonight after being told how amazing it was (and seeing the #2 ranking in Philly Mag) and we were let down.

First... the service ran from checking in on us every 30 seconds to then receiving no service for long stretches of time. We had our cheese plate collected and then had a good twenty minutes before dessert was served. And the cup of coffee I asked for didn't materialize for over a half-hour until I went back to the kitchen to ask for it. 

The food... interesting, with some real highlights. I loved the halibut ceviche, and the nitrogen popcorn was playful and fun. The salad with pear vinaigrette was very good, the sweetbread hot appetizer was interesting, both my beef entree and my wife's chicken entree was respectable, if not out of this world. But many of the "mouthful" bites were mediocre to not very good. (The cheddar cheese cracker bite, for example, stood out as nearly inedible.) 

Finally, we thought both our desserts (my wife had Going Bananas and I had the Chocolate in Many Forms) were huge let-downs. 

In the end, the food runs from very tasty to not very tasty. It's clear they are doing some really adventurous things, but given the prices, I think they should hit more often than they do, and their misses should not be as big as they were, and they could really work on their service. 

Marigold Kitchen is an interesting idea, but it's nowhere near the second best restaurant in Philly. My rating is somewhere in between two and three stars.

text:
Oh Mai Lee, where do I start... I really, really, REALLY wanted to like this place. Did I say "really"? For YEARS, many of my friends, co-workers, and associates have told me that this place is awesome. I believed them. I've been wanting to come here for YEARS, and just haven't had the chance. That chance finally came on Friday when I came here for lunch. I was disappointed...

If I had to put in one sentence why I didn't really care for this place, I would say: "Mai Lee offers a wide variety of fresh but basic Asian cuisine, at a moderate to high price, with lacking customer service and consistency."  Let's unpack this.

The menu here is massive with almost every variation of Chinese, Vietnamese, and Thai dishes. Seriously, the menu is a book. I ordered #171, just to show you how many different options they offer. #171 was the Vietnamese Special Fried Rice. I asked the waiter what made this Vietnamese when compared to Chinese Fried Rice and he said that Chinese Fried Rice is soy sauce-based, while this one is tomato sauce based. Now, having heard that, I must say although my rice was freshly prepared and had all the meats and trimmings of Chinese fried rice, to me there was NO DIFFERENCE in flavor between what I had and the Chinese Food I get from Chinese restaurants all over town. NONE. Now was it as greasy as the local Chinese restaurants offer? Probably not. But you can't tell me that THAT was "Vietnamese, tomato-based". Plus it was $15, which I don't have a huge gripe about that, but I could have ordered a box of special fried rice elsewhere for less. IJS.

Now for the service... My waiter was nice, but he was often MIA. I sat and waited for refills, which a busser took care of for me. I sat and waited for a while to receive my check. I was never asked how I liked my meal. Upon getting my box, I boxed it myself. All this waiting wasn't necessary as the place wasn't busy at all.

Now, here's my biggest gripe about my experience at Mai Lee. So I just said that I waited a lot during my time there. During the long time that I was waiting, I noticed that when EVERY table received their check, they were also given fortune cookies. WHY, OH WHY, was I the ONLY table in the ENTIRE restaurant that was NEVER brought fortune cookies?!?!?!?!?!?! That's not an exaggeration. I seriously watched this with my own two eyes. I thought about asking for a fortune cookie, but I shouldn't have had to. It should have been brought to me like it was brought to EVERY diner there! Consistency is a devil in the detail, that should not be ignored. Treat me like everyone else, please and thank you.

The 90s R&B playlist playing in the background and "great" reputation that this place has aren't enough to have me waste any more time waiting or being slighted by this restaurant again.

As they have grown and have now become one of Tampa's must visit locations, things have definitely matured and changed within their selection of provisions in an excellent way!  

If you are use to over-sauced, over-salted, over-sweetened, over-portioned traditional American food from chains or over-baconed establishments:  OE may not be the place for you. 

The best way that I can describe OE's menu is:
New American Fresh Southern Comfort Food.

The menu is not huge, but it does pack a punch: whether your are looking for something light or even something that can stick to your bones -- they have the perfect plate for you! Our favorites are the Chicken & Biscuit, the Chicken Pallard, the Tuna Tartar... .     The wine list also never disappoints.  OE's chefs and kitchen have lovingly taken the best of homemade food and elevated it to what is fresh, delightfully modernized, and attainably delicious.  You will not leave your meal feeling gross since the portions are just right.  The unique clean and savory flavors for your eyes, lips, and nose are awesome compliments to the company that you keep -- simply happy!  

OE keeps their audiences' experiences new and bright with cool events like monthly book clubs, game nights, cocktail evenings, and chef's night.  In addition, the employees that work there -- from the servers to the tea and coffee baristas, from the book / gift sellers to the custodians -- they are all an intricate part of the customers' piece of mind when we visit, and it shows!

There many reasons for the outstanding ratings and the number of yummy pictures that you see here on Yelp.  This place is definitely an experience that each walk of life should dance with at least once!

text:
tl;dr tasty tacos were overshadowed by hefty prices and a culinary blunder at this popular Rittenhouse taqueria

Since Rosy's opening, it's been nearly impossible to miss the consistent buzz around their restaurant. Admittedly, I've lived within 3 blocks of Rosy's for years, but only now have found the opportunity to give them a whirl.

The indoor space is dimly lit, accenting the offbeat wallpaper choices against an otherwise minimalist decor. The long wooden bar sports a flatscreen and a chalked menu of specials. The space booms with contemporary music and chatter alike. The outdoor accommodations are modest at best, with a surprisingly little lighting to illuminate the chipped paint along with the uncushioned benches. Make your way from the Walnut St entrance past the bar to the host stand, where a staff member may or may not be available to seat you (in our case, it was almost 5 minutes until we were seated at one of the many open tables).

During my visit, I opted for the Coreanos Tacos, sporting Korean-style short ribs, chipotle mayo, and pickled accompaniments. In a matter of minutes, our taco plates were whisked to our table. Immediately, I was struck by how small the meal was -- these are street taco portions. After a few bites, I was impressed by the depth of flavors and quality of ingredients, which maintained a fine balance between savory greasiness and light freshness (albeit, partially because of the petite portion sizes). However, 2 tacos in, I almost chipped a tooth on a large bone fragment interspersed with the meat.

Apart from the host, the service was prompt, friendly, and attentive. My meal sat at $17 after tax and tip -- and that's after I intentionally eschewed even the entry-level margaritas (which ring in at $10). As a Rittenhouse restaurant, Rosy's is very on-brand: great location, premium prices, and middling culinary experience.

Quick summary of my review: Food would be 3-4 stars without considering price but 1-2 with the price. Service was 2 stars, atmosphere was 4.

I was there with a family gathering on Sunday. We were seated at a table near the window. The place is beautify but out table was a cheap, plastic table with a table cloth (which is why I say atmosphere is only 4 stars). Our server was very nice but surprisingly incompetent. We brought our own cake for dessert (which was very good but they didn't have anything to do with it). Coffee was good but the inattentive service made it hard to get refills.
