text:
Just went to a wedding reception that was catered by Peachtree & Ward at their Radnor reception venue: Pomme.  I was super impressed from beginning to end.

Reception Venue:  It was beautiful and natural.  Even though it was sleeting outside, I could see the gorgeous potential of this site.  To get to the reception area, you cross a bridge over a lake inhabited by real swans (although, word on the street is that they are not very friendly).  The reception area has great natural lighting and beautiful large spherical lamps.  There is also a cocktail hour reception area on the bottom level which opens up to allow for an outdoor heated tent for more cocktail space.  The reception manager for the night was also very helpful as we tried to set up the decorations for the venue before the guests came.  They seemed very flexible and accommodating.

Cocktail Hour:  The food was delicious and the service was amazing!  I have been to many receptions with passed hors d'oeuvres but none with such great variety and service as the reception I went to this past Saturday.  The bites were amazing!  From crispy phyllo dough wrapped crab rolls, mushroom duxelle triangles, tuna tartare on a crispy potato chip (think: kettle-cooked style), peking duck rolls (o-m-g possibly the most delicious invention ever--it was like a crispy Peking Duck wrap you make at an authentic Chinese restaurant), new potato skins with smoked salmon and creme fraiche, and cuban sandwich bites (my least fave of the group but really with such stellar bites, someone has to be the so-to-speak "loser" even if it was also good).  I never felt like I was in want of an hors d'oeuvres and even with a group of famished Asians (trust me, not a group that you want to keep hungry), there were so many servers still with hot and fresh appetizers.  Also, the servers were really attentive...it's like they could read your mind when your face was saying "oh no, I couldn't possibly eat another" but the little piggy inside of you was saying "oh please insist because this is like heaven in a bite!" they would know and make sure to find you.  As if they passed hors d'oeuvres weren't enough, they also had stations with philly cheesesteak sliders (cute, gooey, and cheesey), pretzel bites (with mustard dips), and a nacho chip/juicy pulled pork taco station with mango salsa, guac, and all the typicals.  

Seated Dinner:  Dinner was served in three courses and always very timely.  We started with some mixed greens and a caramelized onion tart (with cheese--my fave!).  Next, was butternut squash ravioli--loved the filling but by this point, I had filled up way too much during cocktail hour so I couldn't finish all of the wrapping.  The main course was a perfectly cooked miso glazed cod over watercress and lime-infused rice.  It was delicious but I was so stuffed from everything else!

Dessert:  Dessert had three options: vanilla and chocolate milkshakes (in shots), adorably cute but possibly too tiny mini coffee & strawberry gelato cones, and little jars filled with shortcake, strawberries, and whipped cream.  The jars were a great idea but I think it would have been even better with vanilla custard at the bottom and whipped cream on top--it needed some other flavor/consistency to bring it all together.  Otherwise, it would have been a rockstar finish.  Best of all, they served FRENCH PRESS coffee with dessert--both decaf and regular.  I mean, if you're gonna serve coffee, at least do it right! :)

Overall, I was super impressed by the service and the quality quality quality of the food!  Really spectacular!

text:
So my friend and I went to this place for a nice get away and tried some good Italian food.  I recently cam back from a trip from Italy so my taste buds still remember the good food I had there but here's what I found about Ca'Dario!

Pros:   Good seafood antipasti
I really liked the seafood mussels and clam soup. A bit salty to my taste but very good flavor.  I used to go to Brophy Brothers right at the pier in Santa Barbara but that place is always overcrowded and this soup at Ca'Dario tastes more fresh.

I ordered Penne alla boscaiola.  Good sauce. I like the pasta more al dente like real Italians do, but I guess most Americans like it more soft so this is somewhere in the middle. If you don't like too al dente, this is perfect for you.

Gnocchi is really fresh and I liked it a lot.  If you are a big gnocchi fan, you should try it out. I like it a bit harder but I could tell it was fresh and flavorful.

The portions are not small so secondi isn't really necessary unless you would like to share with others.  I'd like to come here during dinner time with more people and try different things next time.

Cons:  As I mentioned above, the pasta could be a bit more al dente, but that's totally up to everyone's preference so I'll leave that up to you.  This is not cheap but not too expensive either.  It's Santa Barbara so relative to other places, this is not a surprise.  

I didn't think that there were anything very special or unique though, so ended up going to the seafood market right by the pier and got some fresh white fish and uni (sea urchin) and made my own pasta with it, and that was yummy- you guys should try that too:)

text:
It's really hard for me to give this place a rating. How much you like this place kind of depends on what you're looking for in a bar. If you want a crowded, super fratty bar filled with college students and other 20-something-year-olds and you want to get super wasted, this is THE place to go. However, if you don't like fratstars or crowds or waiting forever to get a drink or being at a bar with people who are still in college or still act like they're in college or waiting in line forever to get into a bar, then you should avoid this place. 

Even though this place is very large with several outdoor bars, a few different rooms, including one with a stage where they have live music some nights, and a some nice outdoor patios, on Thurs/Fri/Sat nights, it still gets completely jam-packed. On Thursday nights, they have $1 Miller Lite drafts and this really brings out the underaged college students. The Thursday night crowd is usually incredibly young, so don't be surprised if you go on a Thursday night and you see some kids who don't even look old enough to drive yet. Also, on their more popular nights (Thurs/Fri/Sat), they charge for valet parking, which tends to get full later in the evening, but on less popular nights they have free valet parking, which is nice. 

On Friday nights, MacDinton's has their happy hour from 6pm-8pm, which is all you can drink for $10. The lines to get into happy hour can get extremely long, and then they give you a teeny tiny cup, which you again have to wait in line for every time you want to get a refill. 

The bouncers here can also be huge pricks sometimes. I've seen people get thrown out for no reason at all, and I've even almost been thrown out myself for no reason. 

If you're 25 or under, make sure you have 2 forms of ID (i.e. driver's license and something else with your name on it, such as a credit card). They can be pretty strict about this and I've had friends who have come and only brought their driver's license and then been turned away. 

I have had some nights where I've had a LOT of fun at MacDinton's but those nights generally involved a ton of alcohol and some fuzzy memories. Being completely sober here can be pretty miserable. Overall, this place can be a lot of fun, given the right circumstances and if you're into the "MacDinton's scene". However, the lines, crowds and expensive drinks usually suck the fun out of it unless you're too incoherent to even notice or care.

text:
Has Adobe jumped the shark?

Adobe became one of my regular haunts in South Philly over the past 7 years. Mostly because I love that they have karaoke on both Friday and Saturday. It's entertaining and good, social fun.  However this past Saturday the experience was a complete bust.

We came around 10ish and immediately put in some songs to sing. We waited hours and in the meantime some people sang two or three times, and some that had put in songs after us were going first.  We were informed by a nearby patron, "You have to go complain to the guy, then he'll play your song."  I glance up to see a line 7 or 8 people deep at the DJ area. People had actually queued up to complain so that they could go up and sing. The DJ had a mess of papers everywhere, and others were also complaining because there is no more paper to write songs on.  I simply have never seen this level of disorganization for a karaoke DJ.  It's a shame that the previous DJ Amanda left.  She was amazing at organizing the song flow, being fair and pleasing everyone, letting people know when there were too many songs in and what the wait would be.

Since I'm not getting my karaoke on, I decide to do some more drinking and go to the bar.  But each time we try to get drinks we are usually vaguely ignored for about 20 minutes.  There are piles of credit card receipts and dirty glasses everywhere on the bar.  The bartenders were working, and friendly, but were totally in the weeds and unable to keep up.

So, I decide to play some foosball. The other main reason I love Adobe is their free foosball table in the back dining room. I'm watching four people play, considering asking to jump in on the next game.  Then I realize they have yet to replace the two missing men from the table.  Not only that, now one of the rods is missing a screw and completely pulling out of the table.  These issues would only take a few little screws or replacements parts.

I return to my group of friends in the karaoke room where it's about 90 uncomfortable degrees.  No songs to be sung. No drinks to be had. No foosball to be played. And I realize the horrifying truth that, although Adobe was always a dive where the food was horribly overpriced, it was usually a dive where I could get at least get karaoke, beer, and foosball.  Adobe had moved beyond a fun dive to a dump, where they don't care to hire a competent karaoke DJ (their bread and butter), they don't care to hire another bartender for extremely busy Fridays and Saturdays, and they don't care to buy a few screws to fix the foosball table. I hope the managers read this, because without a bit of extra effort you will start to loose the patrons that supported your business for so long.

text:
3.5

I haven't been to the original spot, but Edley's East is comfortable, welcoming and cozy. It's pretty close to what I'm looking for in a neighborhood bbq joint.

I tend to stick to what works: turkey sammich. It's nothing too special but I find the turkey has a nice smoke to it that makes it easy to eat on its own. Add in the red & white sauce and you have a party. The portion size isn't quite what I'd expect from a bbq place in the south but I chalk that up to a plethora of out-of-town customers. Not to knock Edley's but if I were looking to impress a visitor with real deal down home bbq, I wouldn't make EEB my first stop. Like I mentioned upthread, it's good for what it is. When I've felt adventurous, the specials are pretty... special. Of note, the burger with pimento cheese was enjoyable. Again, it's nothing mindblowing (burger, topped with pimento cheese, tomato, raw red onion) but it's enjoyable. The sides are hit or miss. I'm not crazy about the mac. The slaw gets thumbs up for being vinegar, rather than mayo, based. The potato salad is (I think) the best side and the black-eyed peas are serviceable. Everyone I've encountered on the food side is pretty nice.

Where Edley's falls down (but lures me in) is the bar. I've yet to receive decent service from a bartender. I've found them either flirting with women, watching the game, talking to their friends, or being otherwise occupied from actually providing me with a beer (their job). The thing that keeps me coming back, though, is 2-for-1 beers on Thursdays. The beer list is well curated and stocked with a wide variety of beers, both local and international. Come in, order a beer, (in my case get ignored and then) receive said beer, get a slip of paper that allows you to get the same beer for free. When in the mood for a sandwich, two sides and two beers for, about, $15 and Thursday night football... you could do much much worse. But, if I'm being honest, Edley's could do a lot better, too.

Patio seating available for those not interested in watching the game.

Pre-lockdown experience.

Glad to see these guys are still going strong. Nashville doesn't have a ton of Colombian offerings so I am glad to see that people are responding to this concept. It's also nice to see a decidedly local (and, small) food offering in a city that's dang-near pricing everything else out in favor of out-of-town chains. 

Living in Miami, eating Colombian food wasn't anything special. In fact, you might call doing so 'Tuesday.' Here in Nashville, it's a bit more rarefied. When I first heard about the truck, I was all in to check it out but because I am stodgy in my food ways, I'm not one to chase a truck. So time moved on and nary an empanada crossed my lips. Reaching my limit, I resolved to fix this and discovered the truck a neighborhood away from me. Figuring this was better than in the Wilson County hinterlands, I made my way to East End and prepared to eat all the food.

Rolling up, the truck's distinctive. Rather than a usual food truck, this bad boy is a school bus. Me gusta. AND it's tricked out in eye-catching designs and pumps music to get you in a South American mood. You can also smell what they're cooking so the sensory marketing campaign is in full effect -- and it works. Oh, and did I mention the folks who run the truck/business are genuinely nice? Yeah. That, too. There's a ton of win here, people.

Since this wasn't my first trip to the rodeo and was starting to put on my winter weight, I went all in to shrimp (onion butter and gouda), beef (gouda and spices) and chicken (pulled chicken, spices, gouda).* Because all the offerings were gluten-free, I felt cute enough to get a side avo-tomato salad (avocado, tomato, onion, lettuce, and lime), as well. You know... to be healthy and stuff. Everything tasted incredible: abundant meat, balanced seasoning, creamy cheese, and cornmeal empanadas with bite, chew and just a little crunch at the edges. I miss VERY FEW things about Miami but eating South American fare on the regular is one of them. Chivanada most certainly scratched that itch.

*On a subsequent visit, I went with the recommended lentil empanada and it's every bit as good as advertised. I never saw it coming.

text:
We met some friends staying at the Royal Sonesta across the street.  They wanted to check with their hotel concierge for recommendations.  The concierge walked around from the desk, grabbed my friend's arm, and practically marched us over to Oceana Grill, which was across the street.   The aggressive marketing (and what I can only assume are kickbacks to hotel staff) set a bad tone for the meal -- how good can a restaurant be if they have to try that hard?

One couple in our group ordered an appetizer of fried eggplant that was tasty, although I recommend skipping the blend of ketchup and mayonnaise that they served as a sauce.  (Ask if they have a marinara.) 

I ordered "Redfish Amer" ($18), which was pan-fried redfish smothered in a creamy crawfish sauce.  I grew up on the gulf coast, where we used to catch our own redfish.  I can only assume the redfish in my dinner (if it was indeed redfish) was farm-raised.  At first bite, I thought it was catfish -- it tasted like the bottom of a lake!  The crawfish sauce was bland almost to the point of being tasteless.  It was like hollandaise with no lemon, with some chewy red bits of meat thrown in.

Several people at our table ordered the "Taste of New Orleans" ($16), which was a trio of Crawfish Etoufee, Red Beans and Rice, and Jambalaya.  The jambalaya had a pleasant spiciness, but the rice was a little gummy and the sausage was a little rubbery.  This was the first time I've had jambalaya, and I would have to try it at a better restaurant before I passed final judgment.  The etoufee was bland but passable.  Is it possible that they used canned beans for the red beans and rice?  I'm just not sure.

On the plus side, we had a group of nine and we were seated immediately.  We had some picky children eaters with us, but they had a kid's menu if you asked -- Chicken fingers or fried shrimp or fried cheese sticks (each served with fries) for $5.  The mixed drinks were $6 and served in large schooners.  The service, while not superb, was adequate - no complaints there.   The prices, which seemed a little high at first blush, may not be too far out of line for a touristy restaurant  just off Bourbon Street.  Portions were large -- a couple could easily share an appetizer and one entree and fill up.

text:
Luke's Lobster, the much touted and celebrated New York lobster roll company (by way of Maine) has finally arrived in Philadelphia, opening to much fanfare and praise.  It does have something that despite all the food options in Philly, the city had previously lacked: a good lobster roll at a good price.  If you are expecting something that resembles lobster salad with gobs of mayo, then Luke's Lobster is not for you. Otherwise, prepare to be delighted.

On opening day, I waited in a 20 minute line to get my hands on one of their famous rolls.  The lobster roll (for $15, or add chips and a drink for $2 more) comes chock full of fresh lobster claw and knuckle meat, overflowing out of a buttered and toasted New England style bun.  With just a hint of mayo to hold the meat in place, you can actually taste the lobster instead of the dressing.  Because this is real lobster meat, don't be alarmed if you find a bit of shell or cartilage in your food (as did I, and it ended up being my only gripe about the quality of the meat).  Because this is real lobster meat, the sandwich is short, but dense.  Savor it.  The menu also includes lower priced rolls with crab and shrimp, or if you're indecisive, a Taste of Maine ($20) gives you half a roll of each variety with chips and drink.

The space is completely different from the previous tenant (Bonte), with a New England crab shack feel.  The staff is young and friendly, and I liked the fact that all their chips and soda come from New England (Cape Cod chips and Maine Root soda).  I question whether or not Philadelphia can really support an "everyman" Lobster Roll place, because at $15 per roll, that is still a pricey fast food lunch for Philly.  Still, it's a quality product and much better and cheaper than nearby options.  It also doesn't hurt that being steps away from the park gives diners the opportunity to enjoy their Luke's Lobster in the Rittenhouse sunshine.

I have astigmatism and a relatively high prescription so I needed to go back a few times after trying different trial lenses to find something that really worked for me. Dr. Cullinan made sure I didn't pay anything beyond the one contact fitting appointment fee even though I believe I ended up going back to be re-fit 3 or 4 times total. She was super patient and made it clear that she really wanted to find a contact lens that was right for ME, the patient. This is the kind of care and attention that definitely is appreciated, since I know some doctors would have tired of seeing me after visit two... 
That being said, I have not had a great experience with the front desk staff. Calling to make appointments, it was clear that they were being logged or categorized incorrectly--and since the Dr. asked that I give them notice so they could order new trial lenses for my unique Rx before I shuffled in, I tried to communicate that but was brushed off and booked for the next day. Ended up working out alright, but feeling like I wasn't being listened to was frustrating. Finally, we found lenses that were right for me. I ordered a year's supply through Clarkson. So the word on the street was I needed to go check out the Oxford Exchange in downtown Tampa of which I've heard nothing but rave reviews. So Ryan and I booked a table for two Saturday, September 20 for brunch. 

Knowing the area and knowing exactly where it was located it was an easy find...It's right off of Kennedy as you make the bend heading towards downtown on the right-hand side. We parked right up front and entered and I have to say I was immediately impressed with the decor and feeling of the building. 

When you enter you feel like you're entering a 1920s establishment as Edison bulbs light the halls, dark rich mahogany walls and staircase adorned with an assortment of pictures the coffee and tea bar and the list goes on!! OMG entering for the first time was truly an experience in itself.... But I digress...

Being rather savvy people we were able to navigate our way to the hostess stand without any direction but I could see how some could be confused. 

We were set and immediately welcomed by our server who was very engaging and knowledgeable. I asked for a coffee Ryan a Mimosa both were delivered promptly and tasted delicious! As a sidenote they pride themselves on using Buddy Brew coffee which is located a few blocks up the road. The coffee was a very rich blend and definitely did the job..

After looking through the brunch menu which offered a good selection including breakfast items, lunch items as well as salads and soups. I ordered the bagel and salmon Ryan ordered the Crabcake Benedict (fancy) 

Both meals made it a timely fashion I would say under 10 minutes. Mine tasted wonderful the salmon was fresh and plentiful as well as the pickled onions and chive cream cheese over an everything bagel.

Ryan's tasted great the crab cakes tasted like crab and contained lumps of crab the hollandaise sauce was fantastic the potatoes on the other hand that came as a side dish were overdone and perhaps had been cooked prior. Other than that both meals were great as far as taste seasoning and presentation. 

Overall the experience was enjoyed and we  would deftly patronize this establishment again... 

Small nuances that would definitely add to the experience especially with the environment I feel the owners are trying to create would be as follows

I believe it was the floor manager a gentleman blonde hair black suit including a vest blue shirt and a tie standing in the dining room texting on his cell phone. 

And through my whole experience of around one hour I never saw anyone recognized as a manager doing table visits and checking on the guest experience... 
Other than that it was a wonderful experience and I would definitely recommend it to anybody wanting to experience something new and exciting as far as dining in downtown Tampa goes!!! 

Cheers!!
